News.title: What happens when you get malaria during pregnancy?
News.content:
Huge strides have been made in recent years in combating malaria but one group is more at risk than ever before: pregnant women.

They are uniquely vulnerable to the disease and because sub-Saharan Africa shoulders the burden of global cases the continent’s rapidly growing population means far more women are exposed today than at the turn of the millennium.

According to a recent study, 52 million pregnant women in Africa face the threat of malaria each year, up from 37 million in 2000.

And the toll is heavy: malaria in pregnancy kills at least 10,000 mothers and 210,000 infants every year.

Malaria in pregnancy is uniquely dangerous, and the disease acts very differently to how it does in someone who is not pregnant.

“Pregnant women are one of the most vulnerable groups to malaria, it can lead to severe anaemia, immune suppression, and in the worst cases, mortality,” Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK told The Telegraph.

Malaria parasites infect and feed on red blood cells, dividing and multiplying in the bloodstream. This makes them easily detectable through a simple blood test, which allows life-saving treatment to be administered quickly.

But in pregnancy, the parasites are notoriously evasive.

Instead of floating in the bloodstream, they colonise in the placenta – the organ that feeds and sustains the baby.

News.title: Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants
News.content:
In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

Sports.title: Lech Poznan 1 Sunderland 1: Ukrainian Timur Tutierov denied dream night in Europa League despite extending unbeaten run
Sports.content:
Next

CRIMEAN CANNONBALL Timur Tutierov was denied a dream night as Lech Poznan ended Sunderland’s rampant start to the Europa League.

The Ukrainian forward’s goal after just 78 SECONDS looked to be enough to earn a third-straight win in the competition.



But substitute Leo Bengtsson came to the Polish side’s rescue to earn a share of the spoils as the two fought-out an exciting 1-1 draw.

Tutierov, 21, made little impact and failed to stop Exeter City from suffering relegation from League One last season on loan.



Fast-forward five months, and star was the toast of Wearside after nodding home to cap off a fairytale week at the hostile Enea Stadion.

Tutierov was only handed his first start a week ago in the 2-1 victory over Torreense and followed that up with a Premier League debut on Sunday at Bournemouth.

Now with his first goal under his belt, he could prove to be an ace up Regis Le Bris’ sleeve as the Black Cats’ look to end their dismal domestic form at home to Leeds this weekend.

Le Bris said: “He showed tonight that he is a good striker and a hard worker.

“He had a really good pre-season, he’s a nice lad as well, really well-connected with the team.

“He’s good in behind, presses always in good timing. He was a bit tired at the end, but had this opportunity and scored, which is really good for a striker.”



Given the injury issues of Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor, the Bakhchysarai-born hitman’s first goal for the club could not have come at a better time.

Barely a minute had passed when a short pass out from goalkeeper Mateusz Lis to Michal Gurgul was pounced on by Nilson Angulo. The winger stole it and delivered the perfect cross from the right for Tutierov to power home a header.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The frantic start was the sign of things to come. Straight up the other end the visitors had Robin Roefs to thank for denying Poznan an instant response.

The Dutch goalie first saved from Patrick Walemark, then produced an even better one to claw away Antoni Kozubal’s follow up header.



Swedish winger Walemark stabbed another into the side-netting before Le Bris breathed another sigh of relief when Daniel Hakans dragged one wide having gone clean through.

Not that the traffic was all one-way. Malick Fofana came agonisingly close to doubling Sunderland’s advantage only to see his vicious strike cannon off the inside of the far.

Right-back Nordi Mukiele, who accused Sunderland’s squad of being “arrogant” after the dismal loss at Bournemouth, tried his luck either side of the break. He fired into the side-netting first and then had an effort tipped over by Lis.

Poznan began to build up ahead of steam in search of an equaliser but Luis Palma had their vocal Ultras ducking for cover when he blazed one at the backpost.



Sunderland fail to clear their lines from a corner, and it drops kindly for Bengtsson just inside the box. The substitute drills a low shot through the crowded six-yard area, and beyond Roefs at his near post.

Finally, with 20 minutes left, the local fanatics in the stand had something to celebrate. The Black Cats failed to clear from a corner and it fell perfectly for sub Bengstsson to drill through a sea of bodies past Roefs.

Another magnificent double-save from Roefs prevented first Walemark from point-blank range and then Michal Gurgul on the rebound as both sides chased a winner.

But it was Chris Rigg who came closest to snatching it at the death with his 25-yarder curling effort flashing just the wrong side of the bar.



Even though he they failed to hang on against previously pointless Poznan, Le Bris was delighted to see his men produce a response from the tame showing at Bournemouth.

He added: “It doesn’t mean because we lost a few games in the Premier League that the players, the team are weak, that’s not the case. It’s a question of details, sometimes confidence as well, and these games are useful for that.

“We expected this atmosphere, this style of play from our opponent. They are a good team. After the first goal, they showed they had the quality to build up pressure and get through our block when we were a bit open. They created chances as well. After that, we created our chances, we deserved to score the second goal. We didn’t, and in a stadium like this, the momentum can switch really quickly, and it happened.

“We started the game with seven players under 23, so they need to experience these intense situations against good teams to get better.”

Sports.title: Backtracking Kyle Walker vows to KEEP ‘four in a row’ Prem champions tattoo after backlash from furious Man City fans

FOOTIE ace Kyle Walker has vowed to keep his “four in a row” Premier League champions tattoo after a backlash from outraged Man City fans.

We told yesterday that he said he would “probably” have it lasered off if City are stripped of titles.



But fans accused the former skipper of throwing in the towel over the ­historic achievement with his talkSPORT comment.

Walker, 36, has since backtracked and says he “never had any intention” of removing the inking that marks City’s 2021 to 2024 record successive league triumphs.



The defender, now with Burnley, wrote on Instagram saying he never had any intention of removing his Manchester City tattoos.

He said: “My time at City was a huge part of my career and journey as a player, and something I’ll always be incredibly proud of.

“I shared some unbelievable moments with great teammates, people at the club and of course the City fans, who supported us throughout.

“Those memories will always stay with me.



“As will the tattoos.”

Co-hosting talkSPORT Drive alongside Andy Goldstein, Walker acknowledged the grim reality facing his old club while fiercely defending his former teammates.

“Let’s not hide from the fact that, you know, they’ve been found guilty, but they’re going through an appeal,” Walker said.



An independent ­commission found Man City committed more than 100 breaches of ­Premier League financial regulations.

The club are appealing the decision.

Rooney added: “If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martinez and all of them looked at themselves in the mirror, they’ll find what’s looking back at them is them, and that’s not good enough.”

United’s all-time record goalscorer also claimed that Carrick needs to “come out fighting” to regain some control of the situation.

He said: “Well I’ve been in four jobs and certainly in two of them – in the Birmingham one and the Plymouth one – I was in that situation.

“I can only say now, looking back and reflecting on them two, if I was there in Michael Carrick’s position now I’d come out fighting.



“You come out fighting and there’s no more Mr Nice Guy.

“There are certain things you’ve got to do to protect them players but you have to come out fighting for yourself.

“Because them players will drag you down and it’s going to be you who’s going to lose your job over it.



“The players… we have seen it time and time again, they don’t care. And then what will we see again?

“They’ll have a little bounce when the new manager comes in again. They don’t care.

“I’ve said this for a long time. A lot of them players need to move from that football club, because there’s not a nice feeling in there.

“There are players who have been there a long time, it needs fresh faces, it needs fresh minds, fresh ideas in there because we’re going to see more of this.

“I think if he doesn’t come out fighting and doesn’t show who is the boss then we’re going to see more of what’s happened over the last week.”

They next face Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Sports.title: How contenders to be next Man Utd boss compare as Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte all in running
Sports.content:
Next

THE prized Manchester United job could be back on LinkedIn very soon.

Michael Carrick‘s side can lay claim to just one Premire League so far this season win as they pitch up in 13th, making it their worst league start in 40 years.



Cesc Fabregas’ Como delivered the heaviest blow of the season so far as a rain soaked United were drowned 4-1 in Italy, having lost the week before to Atletico Madrid with ten men.

Lisandro Martinez burst into an explosive rant after that Atletico defeat, targeting the lack of summer recruitment from the club’s hierarchy.



The Argentine defender said he expected more from director of football Jason Wilcox – but later apologised, insisting United were actually united.

And just as things looked like they couldn’t get any worse, skipper Bruno Fernandes delivered a sensational slam to Carrick.



The 2026 PFA player of the year called out the decision not to press man-to-man, saying that “sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of playing high and making them uncomfortable”.

But Carrick was having none of it, taking full responsibility for the overall team and the performance before taking a swipe at his players.

The 45-year-old said: “Whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Amid the furore, Carrick’s future is under intense speculation, although SunSport understand he will remain in charge at least for this weekend’s match with Bournemouth.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Potential replacements are beginning to emerge should United make a change, and SunSport has drawn up a shortlist of runners and riders to take the job…

Antonio Conte

Antonio Conte, who is out of work, would bring a trophycase to the North West to make the knees of his Prem rivals weak.

Boasting silverware from Chelsea, Napoli, Juve, and Inter, the Italian manager fancied the United job in 2021.

But United did not have the nerve then, and he went to Spurs, securing Champions League football.



But before long, things turned sour, famously saying that money “cannot buy the winning mentality”.

He would be certain to bring the shock factor and a whole new rule book, but he’s also a proven winner who could help with United’s 2028 title aim.

Fabian Hurzeler

Fabian Hurzeler is the shiny new toy in the manager market as Brighton fly in domestic and European football.

With the Seagulls’ history of letting anyone who wants to walk depart for the right price, he could be up for grabs.

Chelsea paid £20million for then-boss Graham Potter in 2022, but many expect that the 35-year-old could be a world record fee for a manager.

The Red Devils are already £1billion in debt, so if the price tag was too hefty, it may rule the recently-married gaffer out.

Concerns about Hurzeler’s experience are never far away, leaving fans wondering whether he may be eaten alive by a club like United.

Julian Nagelsmann

Julian Nagelsmann, former Bayern Munich and Germany boss, has also been earmarked as a replacement.

The 39-year-old stepped down from his national team role after this summer’s World Cup, where the Germans were sensationally dumped out of the competition in the last 32 by Paraguay.



Nagelsmann has been out of club management for three years and a return now to what’s been a manager’s graveyard since Sir Alex Ferguson‘s retirement could be a Halloween fright.

Eddie Howe

Eddie Howe is now the bookies’ favourite to take over from Carrick at Old Trafford, as SunSport exclusively revealed he is ready for a return to management.

The 48-year-old is out of work after stepping down from his head coach role at Newcastle in July and has been tipped for the England job too.

But United have a tendency to appoint British bosses which will help his cause, along with his CV boasting Newcastle’s first silverware in 70 years.



Cesc Fabregas

Cesc Fabregas‘ Como delivered the gut-wrenching blow that led to Fernandes’ electric rant on Wednesday evening.

The former Chelsea and Arsenal star has taken his Serie A side from Serie B to the Champions League in less than three years.

The Red Devils even attempted a heist for the star in his playing days, so it doesn’t seem a leap to believe they’d now look at him as a manager.

He was even asked about the possibility before his side’s win over United.



Kieran McKenna

Kieran McKenna, 40, walked away from Ipswich this summer, having secured three promotions during his stint with the Tractor Boys.

And they returned to the top-flight at the first time of asking.

It would be a return to the Red Devils for the Northern Irishman who first joined the United set-up as U18s boss in 2016.

Then, alongside Carrick, he was promoted to first-team coaching staff as Jose Mourinho‘s assistant ahead of their short-lived 2018/19 season.



But it may be that McKenna is just too similar to the current boss to make the necessary statement.

Unai Emery

Unai Emery has led Aston Villa from strength to strength after helping the Villans complete their arc to lift the Europa League last season.

While it’s thought it would be an uphill battle to prise the Spaniard from the West Midlands, he remains an option.

Mauricio Pochettino led the USA to surprising success at the 2026 World Cup, even amid the controversy.

And it’s not surprising given his Premier Leagie pedigree plus an impressive track record of developing stars like Harry Kane and Dele Alli at Spurs, Luke Shaw at Southampton and Cole Palmer at Chelsea.

Sports.title: Bournemouth 3 AC Milan 0: Cherries romp to best night in their history and mock Ruben Amorim with cheeky chant
Sports.content:
Next

BOURNEMOUTH took their stripes from AC Milan 55 years ago, now they just take the p*** out of the Italian giants.

One of Bournemouth’s greatest nights was a calamity for Ruben Amorim – who was serenaded with cheeky chants of ‘it’s happening again’ – and one of European football’s most storied clubs.



Two first half penalties, from Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier, and a daft red card for Mike Maignan set the Cherries on their way to their biggest ever scalp.

Amine Adli capped a night that will live forever with a belter of a second half free-kick.



A banner draped from the roof of the North Stand ahead of kick off read: “How did we end up here?”

Even for the most optimistic of Bournemouth fans a night like this would have felt impossible at various points in their history.



They have hosted AC Milan before, in a 2016 testimonial friendly, three years after Luka Modric, on the bench, had been here for a summer friendly with Real Madrid.

But that was as close as any at the Vitality thought they would ever get.

It never felt possible in 1997, when players – including a young Eddie Howe, whose name was chanted here – were shaking buckets in the Winter Gardens in a bid to save the club from insolvency.

And 15 years ago to the day, it was Bury playing at Dean Court in League One, and leaving with three points.

Now it was the 19-time Italian champions, with many of the pack they had brought with them from Milan having little old Bournemouth down as favourites – and rightly so.

The only caveat to this memorable night was the fact that the state of Milan and the way they played was an affront to their great history.

But neither that fact, nor the early biblical rain, was ever going to dampen spirits here.

The great and good of Bournemouth’s history were gathered for the occasion.

American owner Bill Foley was in attendance, as was his predecessor Jeff Mostyn, who dragged them from darkness to the Premier League, while Steve Fletcher and Harry Redknapp were also beaming in the stands.



This was a special atmosphere, ratcheted up thanks to Kluivert’s early opener, aided by VAR after the video assistant spotted a handball from Koni De Winter as he tried to stop Evanilson’s header at the far post.

Kluivert, whose father Patrick not only played for Milan but also scored a Champions League final winner against them for Ajax in 1995, sent a cool, low spot kick past Maignan, who went flying the wrong way.

That was by no means his worst decision of the night, however. The Frenchman sent an already rough night through the floor for the visitors when he inexplicably thumped Tyler Adams in the face at a corner.



Greek referee Vassilis Fotias did not need any help there, quickly brandishing the red card.

Maignan protested and took an age to leave the pitch, not helping his replacement, 21-year-old Lorenzo Torriani, who was himself sent the wrong way by Tavernier’s spot kick.

Amorim scrambled with a double change at the break but it made little difference.

The Cherries continued to dominate, with sub Rayan sending a header narrowly over.

It was the night Milan came to town and left with tails between their legs and red faces staring down at their toes.

Sports.title: Verstappen criticises 'unacceptable' COTA surface amid concerns over injury
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen revealed concerns over the state of his spine as he unleashed a scathing criticism of the "out of control" bumpy track surface at Circuit of The Americas.

The four-time world champion arrives in Austin for Sunday's United States Grand Prix after claiming his first two victories of the season in back-to-back races.

Speaking to the media on Thursday, Verstappen was unexpectedly passionate over the state of the circuit, which is generally considered as one of the most popular among the drivers on the F1 calendar.

"You can also see the track conditions. From what I saw in the WEC [World Endurance Championship], the circuit was extremely bumpy," Verstappen said.

"I'm not really looking forward to that to be honest, for your spine. I was joking about that in the last race but it's not really a joke to be honest because we mentioned this already for years that it's actually getting a bit out of control.

"I'm sure it's going to be quite tough to find the right compromises around this track in places where it's just extremely bumpy. I don't know how our car is going to respond to that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner reflects on the 'abnormal talent' Max Verstappen possessed when working with the Dutchman at Red Bull.

The Red Bull driver appeared to be urging the event organisers to place greater emphasis on improving the surface for the event in future.

"Of course, you can use the excuse that the soil is the problem, but then you should have known that you need to make sure that you reinforce it more," Verstappen continued.

"I love this track. I love this place. It's one of the best layouts ever and it's one of the venues, best cities to be at. But for me, the bumps that we have are unacceptable.

"Over time, they've been grinding a little bit here and there, but it's just putting a plaster on the big problem - that's just what's coming underneath.

"That's what you need to actually tackle in the first place. Of course, it means you need to really fully open up the track. That costs a lot of money and time, but honestly, that's the only way to get rid of it because these bumps are not natural and they are out of control."

Image: Verstappen is seeking a third successive Grand Prix victory

Verstappen then explained that medical checks had shown that "the bottom end" of his spine "doesn't look that great".

The 29-year-old said: "That I think sometimes people don't really understand that because I can tell you from the checks that I've done from my spine, the bottom end doesn't look that great, the spine.

"I know that's part of racing. I know that can be part of sport, but it's of course also further damage from the cars that we had the last few years.

"Now, if we continue with finding this acceptable to drive on, then, you are going to suffer with that much more."

Norris: I need to take headache tablets

Reigning world champion Lando Norris revealed that he takes headache tablets before driving at certain tracks due to their bumpiness.

Norris also explained that if COTA was a brand-new circuit, it wouldn't meet the requirements to be added to the calendar.

"If you build a new track now, the rules, the regulation of building a new track, the tolerances you have to be within are pretty small," Norris said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris says he is 'allowed to race' teammate Oscar Piastri despite McLaren suffering a double DNF in the Singapore GP Sprint Race.

"It certainly doesn't fit anywhere close to what those regulations are now, but it's an old track, not a new track.

"It's pretty bad. There's a lot of places… I need to take headache tablets before I go out simply because it's so bumpy and you're hitting your head pretty hard against the headrests and things because of the bumps. It's certainly not a nice thing.

"There's not much we can do. We complain about it. It's something we've brought up many, many times, but there's only so much we can complain about things."

Mercedes driver George Russell said the bumpy nature of the circuit is "just part of racing," but expressed concern over the general standard of surfaces throughout the year.

"It's bumpy, but I think it's just part of racing," Russell said.

"I'd say my general view is F1 tracks probably need to be repaved every couple of years just to make it a bit more consistent because we're going to tracks now where tarmac's coming up, it's falling apart, it's causing more issues than not.

Image: Verstappen won last year's race in Austin

"We're not an IndyCar or an F2 car that run their ride heights, reasonably high. Our ride heights are 10mm at the end of the straight, a centimetre from the ground, so any time you bump you really feel it.

"The side profile of the tyres now since we've been at the 18-inch is substantially smaller.

"The circumference of the tyre is the same. The circumference of the rim is far greater, so you've lost all of that effective suspension in the tyre, which was a damper, which we kind of don't have anymore. Not ideal, but not much we can do."

Sports.title: Norris: 'Incredible' Antonelli two levels above Russell all season
Sports.content:
Lando Norris believes Kimi Antonelli has done an "incredible job" and performed "two levels above" Mercedes team-mate George Russell this season, in form which has taken the Italian to the brink of a record-breaking world championship triumph.

Antonelli looks all but assured to succeed Norris as F1's reigning world champion this year thanks to the 102-point lead he holds at the top of the standings with six races left.

The 20-year-old could become the sport's youngest-ever champion as early as this Sunday's United States Grand Prix if he wins the race and nearest challengers Russell and Lewis Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay in mathematical contention.

And Norris, who claimed his own maiden crown with McLaren last year, has spoken glowingly about Antonelli's second season of F1 up against the "very good" Russell.

"I think it's very impressive what he's been able to do," said Norris.

"At his age, his second year in Formula 1, he's going to be the youngest world champion ever. It's pretty incredible, especially because, I wouldn't say he had a bad first season in Formula 1, he was against George, who I think is very good and has performed very well, especially in the last year [at Mercedes in 2024] against Lewis.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater explains how Kimi Antonelli can clinch the F1 world title this weekend at the United States Grand Prix.

"For him to take quite a huge step from last year to this year, in terms of optimising things and understanding how to drive this year's car, more than other people as well.

"Dealing with the pressure, the lack of mistakes that have come from him, in both qualifying and races, the consistency to beat his team-mate.

"I rate George and I think he's a very good driver, but Kimi has been two levels above George the whole season. He's done a pretty incredible job and I'm sure the world knows that. I don't need to say it, I think it's obvious enough."

Image: Kimi Antonelli looks set to succeed Lando Norris as F1 world champion

Mercedes made the then-18-year-old Antonelli the sport's third-youngest driver in history when they promoted him to the seat vacated by the Ferrari-bound Hamilton, F1's most successful-ever driver, from the 2025 season.

Asked in Austin on Thursday if he had any advice for Antonelli as his successor closes on the title, seven-time champion Hamilton quipped: "Slow down!

"No, I don't know. He doesn't need any advice. I think he's shown this year, and also last year, but particularly this year, his talent and his ability, his calmness and his approach.

"He's done an amazing job this year, and I'm so proud of him. I'm so proud of the way he's carried himself, how he interacts with the drivers and even with you guys.

"It's great to see him and the team excel. If it's not my team, I'd always want to see my old team do well."

'Crazy if you think about it' - but Antonelli not thinking about title win yet

Although it has become a question in recent races of when and not if Antonelli will win this year's championship, the mathematics required for him to do so as early as Sunday evening in Austin are not in his own hands.

Antonelli would clinch the title if he claims his ninth race victory of the season and Russell finishes ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower. That exact three-way result has not happened once in a race so far this season.

"I mean, it definitely is crazy if you think about it, but that's why I won't think about it," said Antonelli.

"I've heard that something catastrophic needs to happen to the others for me to become champion. For me, it needs to be a perfect weekend. The others need to have a poor result, which is unlikely to happen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell takes over from Kimi Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore.

"So, of course, anything can happen, and it's crazy to think about it. But, as I said, we had a meeting with Bono [Peter Bonnington, Antonelli's race engineer] this morning, and we just said, 'Just have fun.' It's always the same mindset I've had all year: one race at a time. Just try to do the best I can every race weekend, and then we'll see.

"But, of course, if I do things well, then the result will come."

The Italian is aware of the significance of what almost-certainly awaits him at some point in the forthcoming weeks, but is focused on making it a reality first.

"I mean, it would be a dream. It's something I've dreamt of since I was little," he added.

"First of all, to find myself in such a position is incredible. But at the same time, I need to keep going, keep pushing, and it's not over yet.

"So first, we'll try to finish the job properly, and then we can enjoy the rest. But, for sure, it would be an incredible achievement, but there's still a bit to go."

Sports.title: Celtic stunned by quick double in Europa League defeat to Celta Vigo
Sports.content:
Celtic's Europa League hopes took another blow as Celta Vigo came from behind to inflict their third straight defeat in the competition.

After an emphatic 7-1 win against Hearts, the Hoops once again showed their struggle to take their domestic dominance into European competition. The defeat leaves them as one of four clubs in the 36-team table yet to register any points.

The Celtic fans were screaming for a penalty midway through the first half when Callum Osmond went down from a push from Javi Rueda. It was just outside the box, with the referee deciding not to award a free-kick.

Image: Mika Baur gave Celtic the lead just after the break

Mika Baur did give them the lead just after the break as he swept home a deflected cross from Haissem Hassan.

After Liam Scales hit the crossbar, Celta hit back with a quick double.

Javi Rodriguez scored twice in three minutes - a header then an unstoppable drive - to stun the home side who could not find a way back as they suffered another damaging Euro night.

Celtic, four points clear of Old Firm rivals Rangers at the top of the Scottish Premiership, face Hibernian at Easter Road on Sunday (kick-off 12pm) - live on Sky Sports.

Key moments from Celtic Park....

12: BLOCK! Colby Donovan is well placed to clear Javi Rueda's cross as Celta Vigo look to open the scoring.

15: BLOCK! Mika Baur is in the right place this time to stop Iago Aspas' effort.

23: PENALTY APPEALS! Callum Osmand is pushed as he ran into the box, but the referee is having none of it. Camilo Duran is booked for his protests.

43: CHANCE! The ball falls to Osmand outside the box after Duran failed to get his shot away. He sends it well over the bar.

44: SAVE! Ferran Jutgla is denied by Sam Johnstone with half time approaching.

47: GOAL CELTIC! Haissem Hassan sends in a dangerous cross, it takes a deflection and breaks to Mika Baur to fire in.

52: CHANCE! Aleix Febas meets Sergio Carreira's low cross only to send it past the post.

63: OFF THE BAR! Liam Scales inches from doubling Celtic's lead. The defender gets his head to Hassan's cross, but it hits the woodwork.

68: GOAL CELTA! Javi Rodriguez meets the free-kick and his header can't be saved by Johnstone.

72: GOAL CELTA! A brilliant strike from Rodriguez, a nightmare for Celtic.They fail to clear the danger and he fires in from outside the box.

85: SAVE! Forrest sets up Donovan, but his effort lacks power and it's easily saved.

The stats don't lie

Image: Celtic have lost their last four games in Europe

Sky Sports' Luke Shanley was watching at Celtic Park:

Celta were worth their win. The stats don't lie and they had many more chances than Celtic.

The home side were ahead though and what will annoy them is not being able to see it out. Losing two goals in the space of three minutes was a hammer blow.

Martin O'Neill might not be happy with the award of the free-kick that led to the equaliser, but ultimately they needed to defend it better.

Celtic have now lost four European games in a row. The frustration or the worry is that Celtic are not competing enough at this level and can't bridge the gap after winning 7-1 at the weekend in the Scottish Premiership against Hearts.

Their Europa League campaign is all but over but their misery in Europe might not be.

'Still a lot of points to play for'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic manager Martin O'Neill believes they can still progress in the Europa League despite Celta Vigo inflicting their third straight defeat in this season's tournament

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill:

"Where did it all go wrong? Well, we hit the bar with the header, we could have gone 2-0 in front. I think if we had done that we'd probably have won, but forget ifs, buts and maybes, we conceded a goal from a set piece.

"We just lost a bit of momentum, but conceded the second goal, which was a blinding shot by the player outside the penalty area.

"It was a tough evening, but I can't ask for any more from the players.

"Tonight is disappointing because I thought that we could win the game, I felt that beforehand, and while it was a tight match throughout, I still thought we could win.

"I haven't looked at the table, but I was told roughly that there's still a lot of points to play for.

"We have to obviously win a game at Celtic Park, and we have to win away from home, and I think we're capable of doing that."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Hrgovic on course for title defence in Croatia before Dubois unification
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic's hopes of a world title unification fight with Daniel Dubois are on hold as plans are being explored for a homecoming fight in early 2027.

Hrgovic won the IBF heavyweight world championship when he scored an upset stoppage win over Moses Itauma in August.

He was ringside on Saturday at The O2 arena to watch Daniel Dubois defend his WBO heavyweight championship and even faced off with the Londoner.

But rather than an immediate unification with Dubois, Hrgovic looks set to make a mandatory IBF title defence against Frank Sanchez in Croatia.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBO heavyweight rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley. Video courtesy of DAZN

Sanchez's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports: "I expect Frank Sanchez versus Filip Hrgovic to take place in the first quarter of 2027, perhaps in Zagreb, but too early to know for sure."

He continued: "I have already communicated with George Warren [of Queensberry promotions] and will likely speak again this week. Frank has speed and power, but also brings experience and stamina, so he is anxious to fight Hrgovic.

"[Sanchez's trainer] Eddie Reynoso loves the match and so do I. Sanchez will become the first Cuban heavyweight champion."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the IBF heavyweight world title fight between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic. Video courtesy of DAZN

Zagreb is a potential location for the Hrgovic-Sanchez fight and the local arena has welcomed the possibility.

Sretan Saric, the manager director of Arena Zagreb, told Sky Sports: "Of course I support the opportunity to hold the fight at Arena Zagreb."

Dubois will fight 'anyone who wants it'

Dubois has previously beaten Hrgovic but will be open to boxing the Croatian once again.

"To win all the belts. That's the main thing now for me, collecting all the other belts," he previously told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player WBO heavyweight world champion Daniel Dubois says he is eyeing a future clash against Tyson Fury next year, admitting the fight would be 'ground-breaking'

"It would mean everything to have all those belts. No one can take that away from me. That's what I'm after now.

"Any one of them, Hrgovic, he was there on Saturday, maybe him or [WBC champion Agit] Kabayel," he said. "Hrgovic was tough as well, Kabayel, we'll see, we'll see what he's about. He ain't been in with a guy like me but he's a good fighter.

"Just anyone with a damn belt… Anyone who wants it."

Sports.title: Bournemouth seal historic win over Amorim's 10-man Milan
Sports.content:
Amine Adli scored a fine free-kick to cap Bournemouth's historic 3-0 win over 10-man AC Milan, which continues their brilliant start to their first-ever European campaign.

Ruben Amorim's side are far from the standard of the great Milan teams of the past but this is nonetheless a treasured scalp for Bournemouth who, for the majority of their history, could not have imagined they'd play this fixture. The seven-time European champions, humbled by the Cherries.

It was a wet and wild night on the south coast, with the weather fitting for the chaotic first half, which included Milan captain Mike Maignan being sent off for brutally pushing both hands into Tyler Adams' face at a corner.

Image: AC Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan looks at Tyler Adams as he is sent off for a push to the face of the Bournemouth player

That recklessness from the goalkeeper brought Bournemouth their second penalty, which was expertly dispatched by Marcus Tavernier after Justin Kluivert had slotted in the first spot-kick following a Koni De Winter handball.

Another dead-ball moment brought Bournemouth's third. It was a wonderful whip from sub Adli - but Amorim would not have been happy with the Milan wall which broke apart to sum up their sloppiness.

Image: 'How did we end up here?' - Bournemouth's tifo before facing AC Milan in the Europa League

'How did we end up here' was the sign on the Bournemouth banner before kick-off. Their supporters would have been in even further disbelief with their side two-up against 10 men before half-time. By full-time they were gleefully taunting Amorim, who has now failed to beat Bournemouth in five attempts. It was a miserable return to England for the former Manchester United boss.

But it's lift-off at Bournemouth now, after they recorded their first Premier League win of the season over 10-man Sunderland at the weekend and go third in the Europa League table with a perfect record of three from three.

Rose proud of 'brilliant' Bournemouth performance

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose:

"A big night for us. I'm happy for the club, our fans especially and really proud of my lads. The way they did it was brilliant from the first minute until the last minute, we played a really good game.

"Even with 11 against 11 we started well, we put pressure on them, we got one penalty. Then the red card makes something of the game. Sometimes you get in trouble in these situations but, like on Sunday, we did it really well. We didn't give anything to them.

"It suits us to stay humble. We know we are good. We know if we have the whole squad we can compete with everyone everywhere but the season is long."

Amorim: There was no game after 20 minutes

AC Milan boss Ruben Amorim:

"It's hard to talk about our performance. There was no game after 20 minutes. We need to avoid our mistakes. We need to have 11 players on the pitch all the time.

"We tried to defend in the way they are comfortable and try to push the game forward like we did until the last minutes and then the free-kick killed the game.

"It was a hard night for us, a difficult night in every aspect."

Key moments from the Vitality Stadium...

5: PENALTY! After a VAR check, the officials spot a handball from De Winter, who had his arm up and connected with the ball when Evanilson headed wide.

8: GOAL! Kluivert coolly sends Maignan the wrong way to side-foot into the other corner for a historic early opener for Bournemouth.

Like father, like son Bournemouth’s Justin Kluivert scored against Milan 31 years & 151 days after his father Patrick netted the winner against them in the Champions League final in May 1995.

Image: Justin Kluivert celebrates giving Bournemouth the lead vs AC Milan

28: RED CARD & PENALTY! Maignan is shown a straight red for shoving Adams in the face as Bournemouth send a corner into the Milan box. After a VAR check and plenty of confusion, Bournemouth are awarded another penalty as well!

Maignan's unwanted record Mike Maignan became the first ever Milan goalkeeper to be sent off in a major European game.

32: GOAL! Tavernier steps up this time but it's the same result - he sends replacement goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani the wrong way to put Bournemouth into dreamland.

57: CLOSE! Moments after De Winter is forced to clear the ball over his own bar from close range, Kluivert whips the follow-up short corner narrowly wide of the far post.

67: OVER! Sub Rayan rises high but sends his header from Ben Gannon-Doak's cross over the bar.

84: GOAL! Adli whips a free-kick through the Milan wall and into the net to cap a brilliant night for Bournemouth.

87: SAVE! Rayan takes a crossfield pass into the box with his chest - and then is denied a goal by Torriani's fingertips.

Upcoming Bournemouth fixtures...

Sports.title: Emery and Nagelsmann are top targets if Manchester United sack Carrick
Sports.content:
Unai Emery and Julian Nagelsmann have emerged as leading targets to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United’s head coach should the board decide on a change after the club’s poorest start to the season since 1986.

Carrick is expected to remain in place for Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth – he is due to hold his pre-game media conference on Friday – but the 45-year-old’s job is in the balance after two wins from 11 games this season.

Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation at Como in the Champions League has focused attention at United on a potential candidate to succeed Carrick should he be removed. Emery and Nagelsmann have admirers at board level.

Emery is contracted to Aston Villa until 2029, and Nagelsmann is unemployed after leaving his position as Germany’s manager in the wake of the team’s last-32 World Cup exit in the summer.

Emery has impressed since taking over Villa in 2022, last season winning the Europa League, the club’s first major trophy since 1996, and finishing fourth, one place behind United.

But Emery earns between £10m and £12m a year, so the compensation package United would have to pay Villa may be a stumbling block. He has also won trophies with Sevilla, Paris Saint-Germain and Villarreal and had a less successful spell with Arsenal.

Nagelsmann has managed Hoffenheim, RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich, with whom he won the Bundesliga in 2022 before being sacked in March 2023. He is highly regarded by United’s head of recruitment, Christopher Vivell.

The 39-year-old Nagelsmann guided Germany to the Euro 2024 quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by the eventual winners, Spain. It is understood Nagelsmann would be interested in an approach from United.

Other potential candidates who may be considered include Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe and Kieran McKenna. They are out of work after leaving jobs with Napoli, Newcastle and Ipswich respectively. It is understood Fabian Hürzeler is not open to leaving Brighton at this stage.
