Sports.title: Enzo Maresca says honest talks have revitalised Foden’s Manchester City form
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has revealed he held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden to help the midfielder back to his best. Foden has struggled over the past two years but has scored four goals in his past two games to give hope he can recapture the form that won him the Professional Footballers’ Association player of the year award in 2023-24.

City travel to Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime aiming to continue their perfect Premier League start under Maresca, with Erling Haaland fit after sitting on the bench for Wednesday’s Champions League win over AEK Athens.

“Since we started I sat down with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning,” said Maresca, who knew Foden from a spell as Pep Guardiola’s assistant. “Maybe love is not the right word to use but just to show him how important he is.

“I said many times that I know Phil from years ago so I know how good he is. For different reasons the last few years he was not good enough, but again I think when you have more players like Phil available you are a better team because at the end it’s a matter of improving players. If you improve the players you improve the team, so for me it’s my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England. But it’s not just about one game – the season is very long.”

Foden, 26, needs to remain consistent to keep his place in the team, with plenty of competition for the attacking roles, including from Rayan Cherki, who Maresca has described as “one of the best players in Europe”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City’s only competitive defeat under Maresca came against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, and they have seven straight wins in the Premier League to sit three points clear at the top. Maresca is waiting to find out whether Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic and Nico O’Reilly are available after missing the AEK game. “The mood is good, we are happy with our start but we are still hungry for more wins,” Maresca said.

Sports.title: How Enzo Maresca stepped out of Pep Guardiola's shadow at Man City: 'Fire' in his team talks, heart-to-hearts with Phil Foden, rejecting old boss' office and a new attacking philosophy
Sports.content:
Stalking the room, Enzo Maresca is demanding answers. Demanding to know that his message is seeping in, demanding his players answer in the affirmative.

Maresca commands the space, down on his haunches complaining about Manchester City’s attitude towards second balls and defending. He’s loud, possesses what modern-day managers describe as ‘fire’ and players do not allow their gaze to divert inside that dressing room haze.

The scene, from a team talk earlier this season, reminds you of somebody. Pep Guardiola might be gone but the process of replacing him had to lead City towards a successor who while his own man, carving his own way, does bear a reasonable resemblance. And no, not just physically.

This decision, taken by director of football Hugo Viana with the blessing of Txiki Begiristain – who championed Maresca’s cause more than anyone else – is one that needed to strike a balance of continuity and change. Maresca has moved the dial without new concepts feeling completely alien. That’s the trick – a refresh, not reset.

Guardiola was back in town last week, far earlier than expected after waving a teary goodbye in May. The seismic guilty verdicts accelerated a return, as Guardiola sat in the directors’ box for the defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and had a debrief with Maresca in the inner sanctum afterwards.

Once it was security green-lighting requests for Noel Gallagher to enter the area around the dressing room to see Guardiola and now it was the same staff doing it for Guardiola himself.

Enzo Maresca has moved the dial at Manchester City after Pep Guardiola's exit without new concepts feeling completely alien

The Italian has led City to seven wins from seven to begin the Premier League season

Maresca is not in constant contact with his predecessor, as he has reiterated on a number of occasions. They spoke following the emotional one-goal victory at Old Trafford last month but Guardiola is mindful of staying out of the way and thought long and hard before accepting the invite for PSG, fearing his appearance might prove a distraction.

Given the pair are close, Maresca the assistant during the Treble campaign, the situation must be taking some getting used to.

Guardiola is watching City at home religiously and, more pertinently, paying close attention to the fallout of the guilty verdicts handed down for serious breaches of financial rules that could see the club relegated to the Championship, pending an appeal.

He will have noticed the consummate way in which Maresca handled the scrutiny in media briefings, with an authoritative charm and dry humour. A slight detachment certainly helps – something Guardiola could not have utilised were he still in the chair, where the exchanges would likely have been considerably more adversarial.

The way a sanguine Maresca addressed the charges with the players, ‘we have a title to win’ and ‘let’s make our own noise’, was designed to insulate the squad from a hurricane of comment and censure.

In 2023 when the charges dropped, Guardiola used it as fuel. No one likes us and all that. Clearly both styles have their merits and the one three years ago kickstarted a phenomenal run ending in Istanbul.

Maresca was a picture of relaxation as he flicked through his phone while leaning on the Etihad’s breeze blocks down the tunnel on Tuesday night after hammering AEK Athens 5-1. Guardiola looked identical, propped on exactly the same spot hundreds of times before.

Maresca is content at the start, surprised at the consistency of results – City will attempt to go eight from eight in the Premier League at Aston Villa on Saturday – and knows there is room for serious improvement.

Maresca is content at the start, surprised at the consistency of results and knows there is room for serious improvement

Guardiola is mindful of staying out of the way and thought long and hard before accepting the invite for the PSG game, fearing his appearance might prove a distraction

‘When you lose important players, many important players, and you lose the manager after 10 years, it always takes time to compete again,’ Maresca said, referencing the exits of Rodri, John Stones, Bernardo Silva, Nathan Ake, Manuel Akanji and more. ‘But we are competing at the moment. This is already a great achievement. We want more.’

There is a degree of pride in that statement from a man who is aware of the need to change certain bits of day-to-day life at the City Football Academy and how they tactically go about winning trophies – for however long that remains a possibility.

So keen is Maresca to subtly alter the messaging that instead of assuming Guardiola’s office he moved to one down the hall. He’s held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden in a bid to recapture his form, with the previous boss having once visited the academy graduate’s house for similar reasons.

Undoubtedly, the 46-year-old wants a more aggressive City. A City more in the image of the 2018 Centurions than the Treble winners. An invitation for the wingers to go at their markers with more regularity, owning their individualism, and the general sense of attempting to force the ball into the box for Erling Haaland with added urgency.

Players keep saying that the messaging is clear – even if Maresca claimed recently that he’d rather win 1-0 than the basketball 5-3 against Sunderland, which is a position at odds with their swashbuckling performances. ‘I think we can attack better, we can defend better,’ Maresca said. ‘It's a matter of finding balance.’

While Maresca bristled at suggestions they gave up a few too many chances when beating Ipswich Town, the 4-2 home defeat by PSG a few days earlier gave stronger answers on the balancing act.

He talks about needing the build-up to sharpen up – meaning more control and retaining midfield stability – and removing Rayan Cherki at half-time for teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi when three down offered that.

The midfield trio of Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez appeared more symmetrical and could represent a blueprint in the tougher games – especially away from home.

Maresca has held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden in a bid to recapture his form

He wants control and balance in midfield, exemplified by bringing on Ayyoub Bouaddi at 3-0 down to PSG and getting a foothold

‘One of the best in Europe in the right position,' Maresca said of Rayan Cherki. 'I also like simple things. I think the most difficult thing in football is to do easy things, don't complicate.’

The Cherki flicks and tricks were mesmeric in midweek against AEK, with another spectacular goal to boot. ‘Top player,’ Maresca said. ‘One of the best players in Europe when he is in the right position. I also like simple things. I think the most difficult thing in football is to do the easy things, don't complicate.’

We’ve definitely heard those words before, delivered from the same seat last season. Maresca says he learnt more from PSG than any other game and some of that will be down to the mentality of his leaders from the break onwards. The second-half dominance, when City created scores of opportunities, taught him something tactically but also about the fortitude of certain players.

‘We don’t like to lose games, but the mood in the dressing room afterwards was very positive,’ he said. ‘The players can see with their eyes that if we compete in the way we did in the second half, we are there. It was a nice feeling because yes, we lost the game, but we can be there, we are there.’

Again, that sort of summation sounds familiar. And that is definitely no bad thing for City. Just don’t call him Diet Pep. Somebody tried that once and it didn’t end well. This is Enzo Max.

Sports.title: 'They've lost that edge': How Bath fell back down to earth thanks to stars departing and second-half woes - as bitter rivals Gloucester smell blood
Sports.content:
'They've lost that edge': How Bath fell back down to earth thanks to stars departing and second-half woes - as bitter rivals Gloucester smell blood

‘Never too high, never too low,’ is one of Johann van Graan's most-used phrases. Win or lose, Bath's head coach doesn’t get too carried away. That remains the case, even though the latest evidence suggests his team is simply not at the elite level that saw them claim a brilliant Treble in the 2024-25 season.

A 71-48 hammering at reigning PREM champions Northampton saw Bath drop out of the top four for the first time in more than three years. Then came an even more disappointing defeat in Europe – a 32-14 loss on home soil to Montpellier last weekend.

In their past 11 competitive matches, dating back to and including May’s Champions Cup semi-final defeat by Bordeaux, Bath have lost seven and won four. Not a crisis yet, but certainly a drop-off from the high standards Van Graan has been used to setting since the South African's brilliant overhaul of the club began in summer 2022.

'You can't deny, Bath are not playing to their full capacity,’ club legend and former England prop Gareth Chilcott tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘What's slightly concerning me is that they're creating chances and not taking them.

'Their discipline is a little bit wayward and they seem off the pace slightly. Bath have won lots of games by overpowering teams late on in games. They seem to have lost that little bit of an edge.’

When Van Graan joined Bath four years ago, he took charge of a club that was criminally underachieving at the wrong end of the PREM. He has since worked wonders, winning a first league title for 29 years in 2025 while also lifting the European Challenge Cup and PREM Rugby Cup in the same season.

Johann van Graan won't be getting carried away, but his side have been in a rut in recent weeks

Northampton thumped Bath 71-48 last time out in the PREM, in a reminder of who the standard-bearers are in the English top flight

And that was followed by Montpellier hammering Bath on home turf in the opening round of the Champions Cup last weekend

Now, though, there appear to be a few chinks in their armour, just in time for a mouth-watering West Country Derby at bitter rivals and the PREM's early leaders Gloucester on Friday night.

'It’s not a crisis for Bath yet, but when a team that has been a high-flier starts to look like they're faltering a little bit, then it’s understandable people ask questions,’ Chilcott says. ‘Once teams see you are beatable, it can be very difficult to win games.’

Bath’s success under the no-nonsense, methodical Van Graan has been built on the power of their forwards and a clinical edge. Bath used to be unstoppable from close range through the likes of hulking forwards Thomas du Toit and Alfie Barbeary, but both left the club in the summer.

The Montpellier game summed up Bath’s current travails. Their defence and set-piece was inconsistent and they missed a host of opportunities, summed up by wing Joe Cokanasiga dropping a sitter of a pass for what would have been a certain try had he collected. Star No10 Finn Russell was intercepted for a French score and his team conceded 15 penalties.

Bath are still creating opportunities – in each of their past three games, they have had more than 12 entries into the opposition 22. But against Montpellier, their average points per entry was just one.

‘If you don’t use your chances, you’re not going to win rugby games against top quality opposition,’ Van Graan admitted. ‘We had multiple opportunities five yards from their try line which we didn’t finish. It’s up to us to be better.’

Where Bath were once ruthless, there is now a degree of profligacy. The departure of juggernaut, try-machine Springbok prop Du Toit cannot be underestimated. When the likes of Ollie Lawrence, Guy Pepper and Ted Hill saw their salaries increase after initially signing on meagre terms, Bath had to juggle their squad and that meant there was no room for Du Toit and Barbeary, now with Saracens.

‘They were two really big players – Bath’s two biggest ball-carriers,’ Chilcott says. ‘That will take its toll. Du Toit was unbelievably good. There is no doubt they’re missing him and Barbeary.

Star No10 Finn Russell (right) has not quite hit the heights since Bath won the league in 2025

Springbok prop Thomas du Toit was a massive loss over the summer as he headed back to his homeland

‘Will Stuart has come back from a long-term injury. We know he’s a great England international and a Lion, but he’s a different type of prop to the big South African. He’ll take a while to get back into the swing of things.’

Van Graan lost his highly-rated attack coach Lee Blackett to England and replaced him first with Martin Gleeson and then Irishman Mike Prendergast. The club’s former head of recruitment Rob Burgess also left to become general manager at Gloucester and will now have eyes on beating his former employers.

Injuries have undoubtedly played a part too. Unheralded but hugely influential wing Will Muir hasn’t played since the Bordeaux loss, while captain Ben Spencer, Henry Arundell, Tom de Glanville, Miles Reid and Billy Sela have all had fitness issues at the start of the season.

Stuart is still working his way back to peak form after a serious achilles problem. His club and England team-mate Sam Underhill ruptured his bicep in the PREM-opening win at Harlequins.

New signing Dan du Preez, Barbeary’s replacement, has torn his hamstring and starting prop Beno Obano has already confirmed he is leaving for France, with Saracens' Rhys Carre a leading contender to replace him.

‘They need to get back to winning ways as quickly as possible,' says Chilcott. 'It’s maybe ridiculous to say this so early in the season, but I think the Gloucester game is massive for Bath.’

One worrying trend for Bath fans has been their team’s tendency to fall away in the second half of matches.

In their shock home PREM semi-final loss to Exeter last season, Van Graan’s team conceded 17 unanswered second-half points to fall to a 26-27 defeat. Such a situation has not been a one-off.

One worrying trend for Bath fans has been their team’s tendency to fall away in the second half of matches

Joe Cokanasiga has lost his place for the trip to Gloucester on Friday night

‘We’ve not had everybody available and that’s been the theme of our season. But we never make a big issue out of it,’ Van Graan said. ‘We just back the next man. We are very comfortable with the way we do things and there is a lot of rugby to be played. There are still loads of players to come back.’

Van Graan, who has never lost at Kingsholm, has overhauled the team for the derby with eight changes, bringing in England Under 20s wing Tyler Offiah on the wing in place of Cokanasiga and starting young Italian Enoch Opoku-Gyamfi at lock. Offiah and Louie Hennessey get their first starts of the season.

With Bath not quite at the races and the Cherry and Whites the league’s most improved team by some distance, an enthralling game is anticipated – though a severe weather warning is in place.

Another loss for Bath would mean the storm clouds already gathering over them darkening even further.

Sports.title: Jordan Henderson's Chelsea revival: How he's still running Premier League midfields at 36, why Xabi Alonso is so enamoured with his role as dressing-room mentor and referee whisperer, and why he hasn't given up on England dream
Sports.content:
Wherever Jordan Henderson has travelled in his long career, his fittingly no-frills nickname follows, and it’s also how he is addressed by his manager at Chelsea.

All of which is vaguely interesting for a single reason – Xabi Alonso almost never uses soubriquets. But with Henderson, there’s an exception.

According to sources on the staff at Chelsea, if you want to see Alonso’s eyes light up, mention 'Hendo'. His responses tend to be revealing, too. Alonso doesn’t rave about the two goals in the recent 5-1 win over Bournemouth, or what the rest of us say about Henderson’s primary function at the club. His preference, instead, is to drift towards the nuances.

As a midfielder, Alonso was capable of spectacular moments but those close to him cite his deeper obsessions with tempo control, positioning and the minutiae that doesn’t make for exciting reels. In Henderson, he sees a kindred spirit and a master of the subtle arts, which has evidently survived into a 16th season as a Premier League regular.

If Henderson starts a fourth straight game against Tottenham on Saturday evening, it will come as no shock. But the surprise, beyond Chelsea, is the comfort with which he can still control a midfield in the frenzied hothouse of our top flight at 36.

An athlete excelling into their mid or late thirties is not as uncommon as it once was. But a fact lost on no one at Chelsea’s Cobham HQ is that Henderson is thriving in the physical battle.

If Jordan Henderson starts a fourth straight game on Saturday evening, it will come as no shock. But the surprise is the comfort with which he can still control a midfield at 36

If you want to see Xabi Alonso’s eyes light up, mention 'Hendo' - one of the few players the Spaniard calls by their nickname

Alonso has kept him on the field for every minute of the past three games – a hiding by Brentford and strong wins against Bournemouth and Everton – and Henderson covered more distance in those fixtures than any player from either side. Against Brentford, whose squad rank third in the Premier League for this metric, that was notable.

Henderson’s engine has always been one of his defining qualities. When he was taken on a free from Brentford in the summer, in a move largely driven by recruitment executives Paul Winstanley and Sam Jewell, his physical capacity was one of the pull factors.

Granit Xhaka, 34, had been their first choice on a brief to land an experienced midfielder for a young squad, but even before the Swiss rejected the move, it had been established that Henderson’s numbers offered no evidence of a declining output.

Last season, at Brentford, he ranked in the Premier League’s 95th percentile for his distance stats, but in isolation it can be a misleading data point – a player running to bad spots is no use to anyone. Keith Andrews never came close to levelling that complaint against Henderson.

There is a famous irony here – Sir Alex Ferguson once rejected the chance to sign Henderson for Manchester United in the early stages of his career on the basis of an idiosyncratic running style. He feared it would make him prone to injuries but 466 Premier League appearances in, that case has long since been put to bed.

Naturally, the conversation around Henderson these days goes to broader places, and namely his role as a mentor to a young group that was awfully ill-disciplined under Liam Rosenior and Enzo Maresca.

The initial evidence suggests that an emotionally volatile squad has benefited hugely from a strong leadership figure – it has been observed internally at Chelsea that he carries more weight with referees and team-mates.

Two examples came up in the Everton game. He was able to instantly silence his captain, Moises Caicedo, when the latter launched into a rant at Jack Grealish, and then when he led a retaliation against a rough challenge from James Tarkowski. Walking the line between aggression and a red card has often been a problem at Stamford Bridge, so an old head will add value.

It has been observed internally at Chelsea that Henderson carries more weight with referees and team-mates

It is common for him to still be at the training ground at 5pm or 6pm, when most will head for home mid-afternoon, and he spent the recent international break honing his free-kicks

Curiously, Henderson seems to bristle at any depiction of him being recruited purely as a ‘vibes’ man and has admitted the notion has fired him with a point to prove. But he presumably knows it was part of the club’s thinking. Just as it was for Thomas Tuchel during the World Cup and for Andrews at Brentford.

Henderson’s value to the dressing room ranked among the reasons why Brentford had rescued him from his post-Liverpool wilderness, which saw a poorly-judged move to Saudi Arabia followed by a fractious, uncomfortable period at Ajax. Some sources at Brentford thought he might reward the club by sticking around; that he decided to leave once Chelsea came calling will have stung.

At Chelsea, there have been predictable tributes around Henderson’s influence. One source said it is common for him to still be at the training ground at 5pm or 6pm, when most will head for home mid-afternoon, and it is known that he spent the most recent international break honing his free-kicks with set-piece coach Austin MacPhee and Cole Palmer.

Henderson celebrated his strike against Bournemouth by running to MacPhee on the touchline; it was MacPhee who impressed upon Alonso that Henderson was a good option from that 25-yard range.

For Alonso, the strike served as a measure of public vindication for a transfer that, at first glance, seemed quite strange. No doubt he would say the move for ‘Hendo’ was always about a bigger picture and smaller details. But for now, it is working well either way.

Time will tell where it leads for Henderson – he still believes he can do a job for England heading into Euro 2028. Betting against it somehow feels like the riskier choice.

Sports.title: Why Nottingham Forest are standing by Oliver Glasner despite Austrian sidelining influential players in his dressing room - and the numbers that back up George Syrianos
Sports.content:
It is awfully quiet at Nottingham Forest these days. At any other time in the last four years, five points from seven games and 19th in the Premier League would have had alarm bells ringing at the City Ground and possibly cost the manager his job. By this time last year, Forest had already sacked Nuno Espirito Santo and Ange Postecoglou. If things feel different now, that is probably because they are. Oliver Glasner was hired at huge expense to bring his trophy-winning magic to Forest and the Austrian is usually a slow starter. Besides, despite only one win from his first eight games in all competitions, the underlying numbers say Forest have been unfortunate and are due a run of better luck. None of that changes the importance of Friday’s trip to Ipswich. Oliver Glasner has had a disappointing start at Nottingham Forest, with his side sitting 19th in the Premier League after one win in seven Some doubt whether Glasner can harness a free attacking spirit like Morgan Gibbs-White in his rigid tactical framework Where does Glasner stand? Forest’s chief football officer George Syrianos drove Glasner’s appointment and will likely stand or fall by how it proceeds. In recent meetings with supporters’ groups, Syrianos emphasised that this was a long-term project. According to Forest's modelling, Glasner is the third-best coach in the Premier League at coaxing his squad to play above their potential. Success with him requires patience. Good, rational explanations for a good, rational appointment. Yet few things are as difficult as sticking to principles when a team keeps losing. Syrianos has had various roles at Forest but now arguably holds more power than ever before. He pushed Glasner to Evangelos Marinakis when Steve Cooper was sacked in December 2023, only for the Forest owner to choose Nuno Espirito Santo instead. Glasner would eventually land at Palace and we all know what happened next – three major honours following decade upon trophyless decade. Forest have hired Glasner to win things. Delivering the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League at Palace was a stunning effort and at a club of similar dimension, the hierarchy believe he can do the same. Forest are already out of the Carabao Cup so depending on their league position in January, we can expect them to attack the FA Cup. Marinakis wants to be back in Europe as quickly as possible and given the strength of some of England’s wealthiest clubs, a good cup run might be more realistic than a top-six finish. Right now, just moving away from the relegation zone would be a relief. Forest’s chief football officer George Syrianos drove Glasner’s appointment and will likely stand or fall by how it proceeds Have Forest been unlucky? No doubt about it – Glasner deserves time. Few Forest bosses since Brian Clough arrived with a better track record than Glasner’s. Despite never managing among Europe’s elite, he still has four trophies, including two European titles. To rip up those plans after a handful of league games would be impulsive even by Forest’s standards. Miltiadis Marinakis, the son of Evangelos, is a regular visitor to the club’s training base and was there again this week. He will be aware of the statistics that indicate Forest deserve to be higher in the table than they are. You can take your pick of the Opta data that suggests Forest are hard done by. According to the Expected Points table, Forest’s performances should have them in sixth. By the Expected Goals metric, Forest should have 11 goals rather than five. No other Premier League club is underperforming those standards so dramatically. Forest’s defensive numbers are good, but they must sharpen their finishing. They have the fourth-worst big chance conversion rate and those five goals have come from 120 shots, with only Manchester United and Brighton taking more. Two seasons ago, Forest finished seventh by outperforming their underlying numbers to an improbable degree. Maybe the current sequence is simply payback time from the football gods – not that this will be of any comfort to Glasner.

Your browser does not support iframes.

What about the players? For much of Forest’s top-flight journey, Callum Hudson-Odoi and Ola Aina have been key figures. No longer. While Aina’s exclusion is logical as Glasner wanted Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace to play at right wing-back, the decision to sideline Hudson-Odoi is strange. Glasner seems similarly unconvinced by midfielder Ibrahim Sangare, who signed a new deal only three months ago. With Morgan Gibbs-White injured, Glasner picked the energetic Nico Dominguez against Arsenal over the silkier Hudson-Odoi and even brought on forgotten man Arnaud Kalimuendo ahead of the former Chelsea winger in the second half. If Glasner stays in charge, the days of both are likely to be numbered. No huge drama for the finances, either – Hudson-Odoi cost £3million in 2023 and Aina joined for free in the same summer. Both would bring Forest a profit if sold. Yet in the short term, the pair need careful management. Along with Anthony Elanga, Aina and Hudson-Odoi embodied the unbreakable spirit that nearly carried Forest into the Champions League under Nuno in 2025. They remain strong voices in the squad – just like Gibbs-White. Gibbs-White wanted to leave Forest for at least part of last summer and duly changed his agents. The 26-year-old is believed to be on the radar of Bayern Munich, should Michael Olise join Real Madrid at the end of the season. Few expect Gibbs-White to be at the City Ground by next September. Between now and May, though, Glasner must extract the best from him. (From left) Callum Hudson-Odoi, Anthony Elanga and Ola Aina embodied Forest's spirit under Nuno Espirito Santo. But Elanga has left and Hudson-Odoi and Aina are now sidelined Glasner is convinced he can turn Liam Delap into an elite centre forward - but the £50million man has just one goal in six games Some doubt whether Glasner can harness a free attacking spirit like Gibbs-White in such a rigid tactical framework. Glasner would counter that by pointing out that Olise and Eberechi Eze flourished under him in a similar system at Palace. Ultimately, Glasner needs his big bet to pay off. He is convinced he can turn Liam Delap into an elite centre forward and was instrumental in the decision to sign the 23-year-old from Chelsea. Delap did well against Arsenal but one goal in six is not what you hope for from your £50m No9. Delap had his breakthrough season at Ipswich and he will hope that returning there will light the fire – and put a few out at the same time.

Sports.title: NFL fan event in Paris canceled amid violent protests as league faces huge criticism for not scrapping game
Sports.content:
A weekend event for Pittsburgh Steelers fans in Paris has been canceled because of security concerns following recent street protests in the French capital.

The NFL and the team both said Thursday that the event, at a bar in the Bastille neighborhood, was off.

The announcement came a day after league Commissioner Roger Goodell said he has a high comfort level in the teams playing in Paris amid recent civil unrest.

More demonstrations could be in store this weekend in the capital and elsewhere around France, but the NFL has refused to scrap its game between the Steelers and New Orleans Saints.

'Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood, and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers House fan event in Paris,' a message sent to fans read.

'Preparations for Sunday's NFL Paris game at Stade de France continue as planned,' it added, 'with the NFL working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters.'

The NFL's first ever game in France is taking place against a backdrop of violence and anarchy

Players arrived in Paris while the streets continued to burn in a series of dangerous protests

Around 2,400 people were arrested, with thousands of businesses damaged or looted

Nicki Ewell, NFL vice president for global events, said the decision was made by the club. She told The Associated Press at NFL House on Thursday that the NFL distributed the message to fans because they worked together to promote the event.

Ewell added that no NFL fan events have been affected.

An Irish pub called O'Sullivans in the Bastille area had been advertising a 'watch party' for Sunday.

The Steelers, in a statement to the Associated Press, said: 'The NFL, as they do for every game, including international games, is working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. As stated by the NFL, there have been no disruptions or impacts at League sites.

'As a precautionary measure, the Steelers designated bar that had been planned in Bastille - an area that has experienced recent disruptions - will not proceed,' the team's statement added.

On Wednesday, Goodell said he had spoken with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and that officials remain in contact with Parisian and French authorities.

'We've made all the preparations,' Goodell said. 'Protests are not unusual in France, as you know, and that's something that we will be aware of and make sure that the appropriate arrangements are made.'

View of charred objects from a newsstand after the weekend riots over the cost of living

The game will take place at the Stade de France, which has been transformed into an NFL field

Pittsburgh Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers speaks during a news conference ahead of the game

The demonstrations first erupted last month in a high school in Creteil, southeast of Paris, over a lack of staff. From there, class strikes, blockades and demonstrations spread to other Paris suburbs and then nationwide, even in smaller towns.

High school students have raised concerns about underfunded schools, dilapidated facilities and staff shortages, particularly in lower-income neighborhoods.

Some also called for a reform of the university admissions system, seen by many as complex and unfair.

With the government seemingly unable to respond to students' demands, the school demonstrations and blockades have morphed into larger protests over soaring living costs, just months before next year's presidential election to choose Emmanuel Macron's successor.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney rips into Man United's 'babies' after explosive outbursts from Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes - and labels captain 'selfish' following public criticism of Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney lambasted Manchester United's players in the wake of explosive comments made by Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes, describing the group as 'selfish' and 'like babies' amid a dismal run of form. Team captain Fernandes openly questioned Michael Carrick's tactics after a woeful 4-1 defeat to Como on Wednesday evening, one week after Martinez criticised the board's transfer strategy after a first limp showing on the road in Europe against Atletico Madrid. Man United legend Rooney admitted that the moment he heard Martinez's comments, he knew it was an 'absolute nightmare' scenario, destined to 'rip the dressing room apart'. 'That was the start,' Rooney explained on the United Stand podcast. 'We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players because they don't want to take responsibility. 'You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players. 'These players, they're selfish. They don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. If they're not getting what's right for them, they're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.' Wayne Rooney described Man United's players as 'selfish' and 'like babies' in the wake of their 4-1 defeat to Como Bruno Fernandes appeared to hit out at his manager Michael Carrick's tactics after the loss Rooney added that he believed that Fernandes had made his comments because of his unwillingness to 'face' a personal drop-off in his form this season, instead opting to put 'pressure on someone else'. 'If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martinez and all of them looked at themselves in the mirror, they'll find what's looking back at them is them, and that's not good enough,' he continued. 'They need to show more.' Fernandes had shrugged off questions of Man United's passivity and instead directed it towards his manager in the aftermath of defeat beside Lake Como on Wednesday. 'It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,' he said. Asked if he meant that Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: ‘That's on the manager and staff to say, not me. ‘Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with Como, the centre back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.' When his comments were put to Carrick in his post-match press conference, the former midfielder suggested that there was an issue with his players' willingness to run. ‘We actually were half-pressed man-to-man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,’ he said. ‘There's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, but if you don't run – you don't run forward and you don't run back – you aren’t going to win.’ On their performance more widely, the former United midfielder said: 'It was more than disappointing. I think everyone has to take responsibility for that. 'I'll 100 per cent take responsibility for the overall team and performance; that stops with me and I accept that. But as a supporter of this club for so long and I care so much about this club, to see a performance like that is unacceptable.' Man United were outplayed on a dreadful rainswept Champions League night on Wednesday His team-mate Youri Tielemans admitted that the squad had been lacking effort in every area, and outplayed by Como. 'It's a combination of everything: tactical, technical, effort. We need to try do better at everything,' he said after the match. 'It's the same message as we've had the last few weeks. We can be here and talk about it, but we have to show it on the pitch. We can only apologise to the fans who travelled, the fans who watched us from home and support us. They're disappointed and we're disappointed. 'The only thing we can do is try to show something on the pitch, which we haven't done over the last few weeks.' Man United have three days before facing their next opponents Bournemouth in Premier League action this weekend and Rooney implored his former team-mate to 'come out fighting' amid widespread speculation that his days in the dugout might be numbered. Giving his own advice, he told Carrick he should show players 'there's no more Mr Nice Guy'. 'There are certain things you've got to do to protect them players, but you have to come out fighting for yourself because those players will drag you down and it's going to be you who's going to lose your job over it,' he stressed. Man United's civil war is not limited to the dressing room: Daily Mail Sport reported on Thursday that there are growing tensions between director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell over the next manager of the club - should Carrick be replaced. Vivell is understood to be pushing hard for Julian Nagelsmann to be the leading candidate, with the 39-year-old out of work following a disastrous World Cup in charge of Germany. Chelsea assessed Nagelsmann as a potential manager when Vivell was technical director in west London and his admiration remains. But sources have suggested that Wilcox, who is Vivell’s boss in the chain of command, prefers a Premier League proven manager, with Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery and Antonio Conte, who have all come up on a shortlist, a tick in that category. Hurzeler does not have a release clause in his Brighton contract and so would require enormous compensation. There is well-placed scepticism as to whether any move would even be remotely possible, regardless of how well liked he is inside Old Trafford. Carrick is set to be in charge at least until after Man United's pre-Premier League weekend press conference, which is set to take place on Friday. After facing the Cherries at Old Trafford on Sunday, Man United will also play host to Roma at the beginning of next month, after a test away at Chelsea. A final home match against Aston Villa will come before the next two-week international break in November.

Sports.title: Victories like this show Bournemouth's top stars that the club is no stepping stone as they enjoy another night to cherish in 3-0 humbling of Ruben Amorim's AC Milan, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
At £15 a pop, the half-and-half scarf sellers outside of the Vitality Stadium were cleaning up, and while those souvenirs are often derided as cringe fodder for tourists, there was no blaming those Bournemouth fans queueing to buy one this time. On the one half, Bournemouth, a club beaten 2-1 at home by Bury in League One 15 years ago on this night. On the other, AC Milan, the Italian behemoths and seven-time conquerors of Europe. It was only once inside the Vitality that those supporters found a free scarf awaiting them courtesy of their club, reading: ‘We are all going on a European tour.’ Not to worry. They would happily take multiple mementoes from this – the night AFC Bournemouth famously flattened AC Milan. There was a special feel to it all, from the fireworks exploding over the Vitality to the playing of Andy Williams's The Impossible Dream to the enormous tifo reading: ‘How did we end up here?’ A few in the Milan end may have been asking themselves the same, especially when their once-great team was trailing 1-0 after eight minutes and 2-0 after 32 in this Europa League fixture. Both of those goals were penalties – Justin Kluivert scoring one and Marcus Tavernier the other – while Milan then spent the remainder of this match playing with 10 men as their goalkeeper Mike Maignan was red carded for shoving Tyler Adams in the face. Bournemouth rolled over visitors AC Milan 3-0 in a historic outing at the Vitality Stadium 15 years on from facing liquidation, fans will savour this impressive showing on the continent By the end, when Amine Adli delivered the coup de grâce with a 25-yard free-kick, Ruben Amorim could only laugh. Literally, the former Manchester United manager now in charge of Milan chuckled as Bournemouth’s supporters serenaded him with: ‘Ruben Amorim, it’s happened again.’ Considering one Italian journalist in the press box angrily ripped his accreditation to smithereens as the visitors trailed 3-0, Amorim’s smiling response may not go down too well back home. Yet our newspaper counterparts from Italy saw this coming. They were wearing a told-you-so look after it all, having warned us this would happen. ‘You don’t understand,’ one said when asked before kick-off. ‘This isn’t the AC Milan of old.’ Indeed it is not, and Amorim tried to hide behind Maignan’s dismissal afterwards: ‘We need 11 players on the pitch at all times. We killed our game.’ Bournemouth boss Marco Rose added: ‘Our club, we stay humble. We know we are good. If we have the whole squad, we know we can compete with anyone, anywhere. But the season is long. We have so many games. Sunday, Wednesday, Sunday. It’s so demanding.’ Bournemouth might not have even existed were it not for their former chairman Jeff Mostyn, who was here as a fan, writing another £100,000 cheque to save them from liquidation in 2008. This represented a major milestone for them in their first-ever season in Europe, and while Bournemouth were happy to embrace this as extraordinary on this occasion, they want these nights to become the norm. Their owner, Bill Foley, is striving for that and victories like this cannot hurt show their better players such as Chelsea target Alex Scott why this club is no stepping stone. Bournemouth won here even without the injured Scott. Rose’s side took the lead when Evanilson headed Tavernier’s cross, but Koni De Winter handled the ball on its way wide. Nobody in the stadium noticed it, but VAR Dennis Higler of the Netherlands did, and then referee Vassilis Fotias of Greece did, too, via his monitor. Kluivert rolled the ball into the bottom-right corner for 1-0. Amorim’s anger with his players was already rising in the technical area when Maignan pushed Adams in the face at a Bournemouth corner. The whistle was blown. Again, hardly a soul in the crowd knew what was happening until Maignan was shown a straight red card. AC Milan are a far cry from their status in the game as the seven-time European champions Milan were further reduced when Mike Maignan was handed a straight red card for pushing Tyler Adams in the face Needing to bring on replacement goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani, the unfortunate one sacrificed was Omari Hutchinson, the 22-year-old whose shin pads carry a picture of himself representing England’s Under 21s. A new taker in Tavernier made it 2-0. Adli’s free-kick in the 84th minute capped this victory with Milan ending the match without a single shot on target. Even with 10 men, that was an embarrassing statistic. This was a night to cherish for Bournemouth, now winners in all three of their Europa League outings. Indeed, a fair few will hang those scarves in their homes as a reminder. But as a club aiming to go places, they hope this is just the first of many matches with European heavyweights.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim FUMES at officials after AC Milan goalkeeper is sent off for pushing Bournemouth star in the FACE - as ex-Man United boss tries to bring on a replacement without taking anyone off!
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim FUMES at officials after AC Milan goalkeeper is sent off for pushing Bournemouth star in the FACE - as ex-Man United boss tries to bring on a replacement without taking anyone off!

Ruben Amorim went ballistic on the touchline as he suffered a nightmare return to England, losing 3-0 with AC Milan at Bournemouth in the Europa League.

The former Manchester United manager was furious that his goalkeeper Mike Maignan was sent off in the first half for pushing Tyler Adams in the face.

Amorim flew off the handle on the sidelines and fronted up to the fourth official, but had little cause for complain as his side's European middling campaign took a turn for the worse.

And there appeared to be a mix-up on the touchline as he sent on replacement Lorenzo Torriani before bringing anybody off, leading to ridicule.

Bournemouth could hardly have imagined a more generous start to their glamour tie, as Milan gifted them two penalties in a first half of anarchy and farce.

They were already 1-0 up thanks to Justin Kluivert's penalty when Maignan's head-loss gifted Marcus Tavernier a spot-kick, which he promptly scored.

Ruben Amorim was furious when his goalkeeper was sent off as AC Milan visited Bournemouth

Mike Maignan was given his marching orders after shoving Tyler Adams in the face

Amorim gave the fourth official a piece of his mind but ducked out of confronting the referee

Maignan hung around for a couple of minutes during a VAR check and left the field reluctantly, giving referee Vassilis Fotias a piece of his mind.

Omari Hutchinson appeared disappointed to come off early to make way for substitute goalkeeper Torrianai and Amorim comforted him.

Milan regained their composure to get to half-time only 2-0 down, but Amorim waited by the touchline for the officials, seemingly ready to give them an earful.

Yet when the officials reached him, the Portuguese gaffer seemingly bit his lip and it was unclear if he said a word to them before stalking off.

Towards the end of the match, Amorim could only hang his head in disappointment as Amine Adli curled in a free-kick for Bournemouth to make it 3-0.

Amorim has had an average start at AC Milan, who sit fourth in Serie A and 24th in the Europa League - the final play-off spot.

The 41-year-old has stuck by the three-at-the-back system which saw him fail at United but has hinted he could adapt.

While derided for his stubbornness at Old Trafford, he said after a 2-0 defeat by Benfica last month: 'I change all the time, we need to start with a base, we have two months of work.

Amine Adli's stunning free-kick gave Bournemouth a 3-0 win and left Amorim stunned

'We lost tonight, but we will find the solutions to adapt to these games, because we need to create an idea, but we also need to win, so of course we can adapt.'

Amorim was sacked in January with United sixth in the Premier League after a £250million summer spend.

He was in charge at Old Trafford for 14 months during a turbulent period in which United endured their worst season in more than half a century and missed out on Europe for only the second time in 35 years.

In an explosive final press conference, the man who led United to the 2025 Europa League final said: 'I came here to be the manager of Manchester United… not to be the coach of Manchester United. That is clear.'

Returning to England, he has been asked about the future of Michael Carrick, his successor who has United 13th in the Premier League.

'The most important thing is that I am here as the manager of Milan, and I need to respect that,' he said.

'What I said when I signed for Manchester United, that I love that club and the people there, remains true.

'What happened since doesn't change that. That's all I want to say on the matter. I've moved on and I'm at another great club now. My club, Milan, has plenty of issues to address.

'I'm focused on my own life and our collective journey here because, as you know, at any big club, challenges are always just around the corner. So, I am fully focused on my work, my team, my players and my staff, not on what's happening at another club.

'But, as I said, it doesn't matter what happened in the past with Manchester United. My feelings from when I first joined that club remain exactly the same. I still love that club.'

Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Trent Alexander-Arnold tipped for rival transfer as Chelsea battle emerges

Liverpool are lining up several ambitious moves for 2027, with Trent Alexander-Arnold's potential Premier League comeback gathering major interest

View 2 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold has been backed for a Premier League return - but not with Liverpool (Image: Getty)

Andoni Iraola has his hands full between trying to get Liverpool back on the path to silverware while planning for the next leg of the club's future. A 4-3 midweek win over Villarreal provided the latest sign things are moving in the right direction, though the job's only just beginning.

‌



‌



The Reds don't have another Champions League fixture for a fortnight and turn their attentions back to domestic matters. That starts with a clash against Brighton on Sunday as they looks to unsettle one of the Premier League's in-form sides.

‌



That being said, moves are constantly being made in the background to prepare for the January transfer window. Mirror Football has all the latest out of Anfield as another round of rumours make their way through the mill.

‌



Trent backed to join United or City

Premier League icon Kyle Walker has backed Trent Alexander-Arnold to make a Premier League comeback in future. However, he doesn't envision the right-back returning to Anfield after the manner of his departure.

Andoni Iraola brings Liverpool star Rio Ngumoha back down to earth after Villarreal impact READ MORE :

Alexander-Arnold, 28, hasn't been the revelation many might have expected at Real Madrid as he continues to jostle for minutes under Jose Mourinho. And after winding down his contract at Anfield to leave many fans embittered, Walker worries the player may not be welcome back at his boyhood outfit.

"Why not?" he told talkSPORT when asked if he would see Alexander-Arnold back in England's top flight. "Can he go back to Liverpool with the way that he left? I'm not too sure.

‌



"Do I see him at another club? He's got to go to one of the big ones. Manchester United [or] Man City [for example]."

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



If Alexander-Arnold thought he was in the bad books with some Liverpool supporters now, joining United or City would only exacerbate any tensions. The England international continues to battle summer signing Denzel Dumfries for starts at Real but could be convinced to swap teams again if things don't improve soon.

A move to City looks all but impossible amid the club's current situation regarding their Premier League spending breaches. However, United could well have use for someone of his talents on the right side of defence.

‌



Liverpool 'tracking' Camara

View 2 Images Lamine Camara saw a £47.1m deadline day switch to Chelsea collapse (Image: Getty Images)

One battle that's emerging in Liverpool's transfer future could see the Reds lock horns with Xabi Alonso. Fabrizio Romano has reported Iraola's side are "tracking" Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, who came close to joining Chelsea in the summer.

The Blues were reportedly inches from signing the Senegal international before the deal broke down on deadline day. Camara had even reportedly completed a medical to sign for Chelsea before the £47.1million move fell through.

Their loss could be Liverpool's gain, given links between the two parties refuse to go away. However, that could set the stage for a showdown between Alonso and his old side if Chelsea decide to revive a bid.

‌

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Michael Carrick replacement ready for talks as Fabian Hurzeler decision made

Manchester United round-up as potential successors to the under-pressure Michael Carrick emerge

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is under mounting pressure (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are in the midst of another crisis ahead of Sunday's home clash with Bournemouth. Wednesday's 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Como has piled further pressure on Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



As well as poor results on the pitch, there is disharmony in the dressing room, with Bruno Fernandes speaking out against the manager, accusing him of getting his tactics wrong against Como. Carrick hit back by questioning the team's work-rate.

‌



Carrick will be in charge for the Bournemouth game but club chiefs are considering making a change in a bid to save a season which is threatening to unravel completely. Numerous big names have been linked with the Old Trafford hotseat, including some who are out of work.

‌



Given the managerial churn at United, it must be asked if the club remains the sought-after destination it has traditionally been. As Carrick sweats over his future, here's a round-up of the latest United news…

Next Man Utd manager odds as clear bookies' favourite emerges READ MORE :

Hurzeler decision made

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler would reportedly turn down an approach from United. The German coach, 33, has done a phenomenal job with the Seagulls, who are third in the Premier League and chasing Champions League football.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta told to make risky change as he delivers Bukayo Saka update
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta told to make risky change as he delivers Bukayo Saka update

Mikel Arteta has been told to make a significant change to his Arsenal starting XI

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has been advised to change his formation (Image: Getty )

Arsenal return to Premier League action this Saturday afternoon when they face Everton at home. The Gunners will be hoping to secure all three points as they look to close the gap on league leaders Manchester City.

‌



‌



Mikel Arteta’s side are coming off the back of a tough 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest last weekend, having made hard work of their recent league encounters. That was followed by an impressive display away at Bayern Munich in the Champions League in midweek, where the English and German champions had to settle for a point apiece.

‌



But, despite coming away from the game with plenty of positives, Arteta had to deal with a fresh injury blow and a new dilemma regarding how to get the best out of Viktor Gyokeres, who set up Declan Rice’s late equaliser after coming on as a substitute.

‌



Now, Mirror Football brings you two of the latest stories involving the north London club.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta provides worrying Bukayo Saka update after Arsenal star forced off READ MORE :

Arsenal leave it late vs Bayern Munich but Mikel Arteta dealt huge injury blow READ MORE :

Arteta told to make change

Former Arsenal midfielder Anders Limpar has suggested that Arteta should change his formation if he wants to get the best out of Gyokeres. The Spaniard usually deploys a single striker in a 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1 formation in possession, very rarely fielding two strikers at the same time unless his side are in urgent need of a goal.

‌



Gyokeres, who arrived in the summer of 2025, scored 21 goals for the Gunners last season. But the Swede often looked isolated and ineffective up top on his own, with his limitations in the lone striker role seeing him fall behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order this term.

But Gyokeres' compatriot Limpar, who mentored him during his formative years at Brommapojkarna in Sweden, has encouraged the Arsenal boss to deploy a two-striker formation to make the most out of his attacking options. Gyokeres usually plays alongside Liverpool’s Alexander Isak for his country and has scored 10 goals in 11 international games this year.

‌



View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres has had a tough start to the season (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"When I see Viktor playing for Sweden, he is much better because he’s playing with two up front, and he was brought up in the Swedish system, playing with two forwards," the former Gunners winger told Betarades. "Playing up front on his own is hard for him because it’s not his game to be a target player.

‌



"He is good going forward, chasing the ball, and he’s a threat on counterattacks, so he needs a player who is a really good target so he can play off them. At the moment, you can see that he’s struggling a little bit when it comes to receiving the ball, to pass the ball around.

"It might be nerves, or that he’s not comfortable coming off the bench. But you should never ever go out in the press saying that you want to leave or that you want to play every game.

‌



"That’s not good for Arteta, that’s not good for him, and that’s not good for the club. I’m pretty sure that all the Arsenal players are squad players."

Limpar added: "If you ask me if I want him to play, then yes, I think he should play as a starter. I think he should be a starter, especially now when Kai has struggled a little bit in the last couple of games, but we have to wait and see who is playing the next game."

‌



Bukayo Saka injury update

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka sustained an injury against Bayern (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Arteta provided an update on Bukayo Saka after Wednesday night’s game, expressing concern over the severity of his recent injury. The Gunners talisman was taken off after just nine minutes against Bayern, having gone to ground holding his leg in discomfort after playing a pass.

‌



He was replaced by Eberechi Eze, who scored just 15 minutes later. But Arsenal fans will be disheartened by the immediate prognosis for the 25-year-old, revealed by Arteta after the match.

"[The medical staff] are a bit concerned," Arteta told TNT Sports. "A player that has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news. But we have to wait and see. It does not look good at all. It's his quad."

Article continues below

Saka started all seven of Arsenal's Premier League fixtures this season but has suffered several injury absences over the past two years. He missed 15 matches for Arsenal and England last season with various injury issues. In 2024/25, Saka missed 25 games across a total period of more than three months due to a hamstring injury.

Sports.content:
As the saga around Manchester City's 115 charges continues to rumble on, Mirror Football will be here with all of the latest updates and news

Welcome to Mirror Sport's live blog about Manchester City's 114 guilty charges.

The football world is still reeling from last month's announcement which confirmed the Cityzens had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18.

It was deemed that the club artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through the use of supposed 'sham' sponsorship deals. City continue to insist they are innocent and launched an appeal against the verdict on October 1.

They also maintain there is a "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" that exonerates them, but this is yet to be communicated to the public. In and amongst the saga, the legitimacy of their achievements over the last 20 years have been brought into question.

Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney rips into 'selfish' Bruno Fernandes as Man Utd captain brutally exposed

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been brutally exposed by Wayne Rooney, who has branded the skipper 'selfish' after his criticism of Michael Carrick

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney has come to the defence of Michael Carrick (Image: The United Stand)

Wayne Rooney has accused Bruno Fernandes of putting pressure on Michael Carrick because he does not want to face it himself. The former Manchester United captain has compared their current crop of players to babies, calling them "selfish" and saying they care only about themselves.

‌



‌



Fernandes called out Carrick and the club's coaching staff over their tactical approach against Como in the Champions League. Lisandro Martinez was the first to speak out after being beaten by Atletico Madrid last week.

‌



Rooney has now singled out those two for criticism. However, the players as a whole are also being called out.

‌



Speaking on The United Stand, Rooney has said: "When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart; that was the start. We've seen it now with Bruno, and you're going to see it with more players because they don't want to take responsibility.

‌



"You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said, but you have to take responsibility on the pitch; you have to take responsibility as a group of players.

"These players, they're selfish. They don't care about their team-mates, the manager, the staff, or the fans.

"They care about themselves. If they're not getting what's right for them, they're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame onto anyone else but themselves."

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes publicly called out Michael Carrick's tactics (Image: PIERO CRUCIATTI, AFP via Getty Images)

Rooney understandably focused on Fernandes following his public criticism of Carrick, saying: "He is putting pressure on someone else because he doesn't want to face it.

Fernandes told TNT Sports: "It's a decision from the staff not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence."

He added: "That's on the manager and staff to see, not me."

‌



Carrick responded: "We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that. And there's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Sports.title: Fallon Sherrock among 'amateurs' playing Luke Littler for shot at Netflix's £501k prize
Sports.content:
Fallon Sherrock among 'amateurs' playing Luke Littler for shot at Netflix's £501k prize

Women's world number three Fallon Sherrock is one of the 24 players who will take on Luke Littler for a £501,000 prize as part of a new Netflix show

View 2 Images Fallon Sherrock will play Luke Littler in the Netflix show (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Fallon Sherrock is among the competitors who will try to beat Luke Littler for a £501,000 prize next week.

‌



‌



Sherrock, the women's world number three, is one of 24 players who have made it through to the live show of Netflix programme ‘Beat Luke Littler’. She could get the chance to win half a million pounds if she can beat the double world champion in a one-off leg of 501.

‌



The 32-year-old is a trailblazer of the women’s game, having created history by becoming the first woman to win at the World Championship when she made the third round in 2020.

‌



She has competed at Alexandra Palace every year but one since and has also played several other high-profile tournaments. Although she does not have a PDC Tour card, she is still a regular on the Women’s Tour, and Littler may be miffed about how she has ended up in the field.

Luke Littler vows he will not go easy on amateurs attempting to beat him for £501,000 READ MORE :

Other contestants, who are amateurs, include a former army captain, a jockey from Australia and a former player who has played against Phil Taylor.

Mark Pooke was on the circuit almost 20 years ago, taking part in the UK Open, and he will also be a real threat to Littler, having taken out a 501 leg in 12 darts during the audition. He is trying to get back onto the tour and says he is in the last-chance saloon.

‌



“My dream is to get myself back on to the PDC circuit, but I can’t afford to do it, so this really is my last chance,” he said. "I know I’ve still got the game; I just need to bring it out on the night. I have nothing to lose – the way I see it, he’s got to beat me, I don’t have to beat him.”

Australian jockey Zac Spain, known as Zachariah the Electrifiah, came from Melbourne for his audition last month and wants to stay in the winners’ circle. “I’ve had over 670 winners as a jockey,” he said. “For me, darts is a mental outlet – I get to go out and play darts and not take it so seriously. I got into darts three years ago because of Luke in the World Championship.”

‌



View 2 Images Luke Littler is taking on amateurs (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Former captain in the British Army Jasper Scarrott, 54, said: “I’m the current British Army darts champion, and I’ve still got a bit left in me. My dad was the inspiration behind me playing darts, and he sadly passed away a week before I hit a nine-darter, so I’m sure he was looking down on me.”

‌



Twenty-four hopefuls will have a shot at pocketing £501,000 by winning a one-off leg against the back-to-back world champion.

Littler will have to win 24 successive legs in order to survive, with the game ending if any of the amateurs check out before him.

Antonio Conte's two demands to take Man Utd job emerge after giving green light

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is under pressure to deliver results and the former Chelsea and Tottenham manager Antonio Conte has been linked with the role

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has been linked with the managerial position at Manchester United

Antonio Conte will make two demands to the Manchester United hierarchy if he is to take over from Michael Carrick. The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Napoli boss has been repeatedly linked with a move to Old Trafford given the club's recent struggles.

Carrick is under increased pressure to deliver results having won just two of their opening 11 games so far this season. The Red Devils boss is set face the music on Friday at his press conference before the clash with Bournemouth this weekend.

As things stand, Carrick is expected to take control of the clash with the Cherries, though reports claim the club have contacted prospective replacements if they decide to part company with the 45-year-old.
