The Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), on Thursday, launched its Living Archives Initiative, a project aimed at preserving Africa’s media history.

Dapo Olorunyomi, publisher of PREMIUM TIMES and chief executive officer of CJID, said the initiative would digitise and preserve the works and legacies of people who shaped journalism across the continent.

“Among its broader goals is to digitise and preserve the works, the times, and the personalities that give meaning to our parts of the region, that is, the African region,” Mr Olorunyomi said at the event in Lagos on Thursday.

He said CJID chose Mr Bonuola as the first subject because of his contributions to Nigerian journalism and his continued relevance to the profession.

“And fittingly, we thought to begin from our own constituency, the media, and with someone who remains a veteran on active duty, just as inescapable, Lade Bonuola,” he said.

The initiative seeks to address gaps in Africa’s journalistic memory, where newspaper records, personal papers, photographs, broadcast recordings and first-hand accounts are often scattered, deteriorating or inaccessible.

The launch coincided with the unveiling of ‘Lade Bonuola: A Life in Print,’ a collection of essays documenting the veteran journalist’s career and contributions to the profession.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Olorunyomi described Mr Bonuola as “perhaps the most remarkable of the most consequential editor of the late 20th century history of the Nigerian print press.”

The book, according to him, marks 50 years of Mr Bonuola’s professional career, which began at the Daily Times in 1976 and continued through The Guardian, The Comet and The Compass.

It examines six aspects of his life, including his commitment to excellence, editorial expertise, mentorship, courage and contributions beyond the newsroom.

Mr Olorunyomi also used the occasion to celebrate Mr Bonuola’s 80th birthday, wishing him continued good health and many more years of service to journalism and Nigeria.

50 years of journalism, 80 years of life

Friends, family and colleagues, including Olusegun Osoba, former governor of Ogun State and veteran journalist; Motunrayo Alaka, executive director and chief executive officer of the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism (WSCIJ); Ropo Sekoni, professor of semiotics and African literature, and Idowu Obasa, chairman of the PREMIUM TIMES board of directors.

Other notable personalities at the event includ Frank Keurhorst, consul-general of the Netherlands in Lagos; Dipo Ajayi and Kunle Ajibade, veteran journalist and former editor of The News magazine. They joined former colleagues from The Guardian to celebrate Mr Bonuola on his 80th birthday and for his contributions to Nigerian journalism.

Mr Osoba recalled Mr Bonuola’s uncompromising commitment to editorial excellence, recounting their frequent disagreements when he was deputy editor of the Sunday Times and Mr Bonuola served as sub-editor.

He said Mr Bonuola insisted on correcting grammatical and punctuation errors, sometimes delaying production as he worked to perfect stories before publication.

“I will keep telling him, I have a deadline, I have a deadline,” Mr Osoba recalled, adding that he often reminded Mr Bonuola that “If you produce the best paper and it’s not out in time, you’re a failure.”

He described Mr Bonuola as a serious-minded intellectual whose attention to detail helped raise editorial standards. Mr Osoba also recalled recommending him to become the first editor of The Guardian, where he said the veteran journalist helped establish standards that other newspapers later followed.

Another colleague, Mr Ajayi recalled how Mr Bonuola helped him after he was taken for interrogation following the assassination of then-Head of State Murtala Muhammed on 13 February 1976.

Mr Ajayi, who was acting editor of the Daily Times, said security operatives questioned him after the newspaper published vivid pictures of the assassination scene, suspecting that the paper had prior knowledge of the coup.

He said Mr Bonuola sent a dispatch rider to follow the vehicle taking him away and establish where he had been taken. He also contacted Mr Ajayi’s family as efforts were made to secure his release.

Mr Ajayi recalled that he was interrogated until late at night and was about to be taken to a detention cell when an order came for his release.

“Thank you, Lade, for that kindness on that day. God bless you on your 80th birthday. I wish you sound health and a graceful old age,” he said.

Ladbone: A Life in Print

Mr Ajibade, former editor of The News magazine, described Mr Bonuola as a journalist committed to excellence, truth and discipline.

Reviewing Lade Bonuola: A Life in Print, Mr Ajibade said the veteran journalist closely followed developments in the international media, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom. He also admired journalists such as Christiane Amanpour and regularly read books on journalism and autobiographies.

Kunle Ajibade reviews the book, Ladbone: A Life in Print in Lagos on Thursday.

Mr Ajibade said Mr Bonuola believed newspapers should be readable and inventive and “truthful, not neutral”. He also highlighted Mr Bonuola’s emphasis on preserving newspaper archives and maintaining libraries.

He said Mr Bonuola’s strict approach to discipline extended to his home, where he raised his children with firm rules and responsibilities.

Mr Ajibade also acknowledged that Mr Bonuola’s high standards could make him a demanding editor, recalling how he expected colleagues to deliver their work even during difficult personal circumstances.

“He obviously believed and said to us that if you must be known for excellence, you just have to be brutal sometimes,” he said.

Mr Ajibade added that Mr Bonuola believed tough love always pays in the end.

Bonuola thanks Olorunyomi, family, friends for honouring him

Mr Bonuola thanked Mr Olorunyomi for organising the event in his honour, praising the PREMIUM TIMES publisher’s dedication to work.

Lade Bonuola thanks Dapo Olorunyomi for organising the event in his honour.

He said he loved Mr Olorunyomi for his “matchless application and dedication to work” and noted that he reads PREMIUM TIMES stories daily.

Mr Bonuola rose to prominence at Daily Times, where he worked as a sub-editor and later features editor. He gained recognition for his “Caught Out” column, written under the pen name Ladbone, in which he highlighted common grammatical errors in newspapers.

He later joined the team that established The Guardian and served as its pioneer editor from 1982 to 1988 before becoming the newspaper group’s managing director from 1989 to 1999.

Mr Bonuola also co-founded The Comet newspaper and served as publisher of Nigerian Compass from 2009 to 2011.

At The Guardian, he introduced the “Cause List” column, which published court schedules, and “Flight Guardian”, featuring flight schedules of national carriers. He also created pages covering motoring and religious affairs, reflecting his interest in diverse subjects and balanced coverage.

He is currently chairman of VerityHeights Bureau Limited, an online publication focused on expanding knowledge.

World.title: CBD COP17: UNDP, UNICEF launch campaign to promote green careers among young people
World.content:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) have launched a global campaign to help young people discover skills and career opportunities that can contribute to a sustainable future.

The initiative, christened “See It, Be It,” was announced on Thursday on the sidelines of the ongoing 17th session of the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia.

The campaign seeks to showcase the people, skills and career opportunities shaping a nature-positive, low-carbon future, the United Nations said in a statement.

It will feature young professionals making a difference across science, technology, business, agriculture, communications, finance, the creative industries and community leadership.

From scientists restoring ecosystems and entrepreneurs building sustainable businesses to innovators developing new technologies and community leaders protecting local environments, their stories will demonstrate how young people can build careers that benefit both people and the planet.

“Young people need more than new opportunities to build a sustainable future: they need to know these opportunities exist, understand how to pursue them and see people with whom they can identify already making a living through them,” UNICEF said.

The agency noted that research, including the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s (OECD) Cultivating the Future report, highlights how young people’s career expectations remain concentrated in a relatively narrow range of traditional professions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It added that research by UNICEF and the European Training Foundation also found that career guidance failed to showcase opportunities emerging from the green transition adequately.

“These gaps underline the importance of making a wider range of career pathways visible, particularly to young people in developing countries who have fewer opportunities to access career guidance and professional networks,” the UN said.

Objectives and prospects

According to the UN, the “See It, Be It” campaign aims to broaden young people’s horizons by presenting diverse, relatable role models and showing how their interests, skills, and ambitions can help build a more sustainable world.

The campaign aims to reach 500 million young people worldwide by the end of 2027.

It brings together organisations, youth networks, educators, employers, communicators, and sustainability professionals to share stories and expand their reach.

Early supporters include the Global Youth Biodiversity Network, an international network connecting young people working to protect biodiversity; the Nature Working Group of YOUNGO, the official children and youth constituency of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change; and the Youth Negotiators Academy, a youth-led organisation that trains young people to participate in multilateral negotiations.

The UN said it was inviting partners to contribute stories, amplify profiles through their networks, and help ensure young people from different countries and communities can access a broad range of role models and career opportunities.

Silvia Mestroni, UNICEF’s acting representative in Armenia, said the initiative would help young people recognise their potential and explore ways to contribute to a more resilient world.

“Every child and young person deserves the chance to imagine a future full of possibility and see how their interests and talents can make a difference sustainably,” she said.

Ms Mestroni added that connecting young people with diverse role models and stories of change could broaden their horizons, build confidence, and inspire them to explore different ways to contribute to a sustainable future.

Similarly, Midori Paxton, UNDP’s global head of biodiversity and ecosystems, stressed the need to make sustainable career opportunities more visible to young people.

“Science tells us we’ll need three earths to sustain us by 2050 if we carry on the way we are,” she said, emphasising the need to transition towards nature-positive and low-carbon lifestyles and economies.

Ms Paxton said younger generations have significant potential to shape a future where people and nature thrive. Still, she stressed that this potential requires access to opportunities and the ability to envision what’s possible.

“Through See It, Be It, we want to make the people and pathways driving change far more visible and help many more young people recognise that there is a place for their talents in building a sustainable future,” she said.

CBD COP17

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that representatives of governments, Indigenous peoples, local communities and other stakeholders had convened in Yerevan, Armenia, for CBD COP17.

The conference, scheduled for 19–30 October under the theme “Taking Action for Nature,” brings countries together to accelerate efforts to halt and reverse global biodiversity loss.

The 2026 UN Biodiversity Conference also includes the 12th meeting of the parties to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and the sixth meeting of the parties to the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing.

Discussions are focused on reviewing collective progress, strengthening implementation support, advancing scientific and policy guidance, addressing the financial and economic factors influencing biodiversity outcomes, improving biosafety and promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.

At COP17, countries will undertake the first global review of collective progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

The review is expected to assess how far countries have progressed towards their commitments and identify gaps requiring urgent action.

Other priorities include mobilising finance, strengthening capacity-building and international cooperation, and expanding the participation of indigenous peoples and local communities in biodiversity conservation.

Financing remains critical because implementing biodiversity commitments requires sustainable resources, especially for countries facing competing development priorities and limited institutional capacity.

The conference will also examine the policy and economic conditions that influence biodiversity outcomes, including how governments and other stakeholders can align development activities with conservation objectives.

World.title: Mbah unveils multi-billion naira pharmaceutical company in Enugu
World.content:
Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State has commissioned Anchorage Pharmaceutical Industries Limited, a multi-billion naira pharmaceutical company in Trans-Ekulu, Enugu.

The coming on stream of the company is expected to boost local drug manufacturing, create jobs and strengthen healthcare delivery in the country.

This was even as the Chairman of the company’s Board of Directors, Rear Admiral Allison Madueke (Rtd), commended Mbah for creating an investment-friendly environment in the state, describing Anchorage as a legacy project conceived to generate employment, develop local talent and contribute to economic development.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony on Thursday, Mbah said the facility represented more than a pharmaceutical business, describing it as an investment in public health, economic growth and the future of young people in the state.

The governor congratulated the company’s founder, board and management, noting that establishing a manufacturing enterprise required substantial commitment and confidence in the state’s economic prospects.

He said the facility would provide employment opportunities, offer internship placements and facilitate skills transfer, while supporting healthcare delivery across Enugu State.

Mbah disclosed that the government would explore commercial partnerships with the company to supply medicines to its central medical stores and primary healthcare facilities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The governor further noted that the state was building 260 Type-2 primary healthcare centres, adding that the facilities would require reliable supplies of essential medicines to function effectively.

“We are interested in made-in-Enugu, and that’s what you’re doing here,” he said, reaffirming the administration’s commitment to partnering with private enterprises beyond providing an enabling environment.

Mbah added that private capital remained central to the state’s economic growth strategy, emphasising the need to retain skilled young people by creating opportunities for them to build their careers in Enugu.

Earlier, Madueke said Anchorage was the practical expression of his longstanding conviction that private enterprise could create jobs, broaden economic opportunities and improve prosperity.

The former Chief of the Naval Staff as well as ex military governor of old Anambra and Imo States said the company would prioritise product quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance and sound corporate governance, while acknowledging the role of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) in safeguarding public health.

Madueke expressed confidence that Anchorage would contribute to the development of Enugu State, the South-East and Nigeria, while thanking Mbah for commissioning the facility and building a resilient business-friendly infrastructure.

In his closing remarks, the Managing Director of the company, Engr. Chima Madueke, said the company was founded on quality and wellness, encapsulated in its slogan, “Anchored in Quality, Committed to Wellness.”

According to him, the company had obtained the necessary approvals and clearances from NAFDAC and the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN), reaffirming its commitment to quality assurance.

He added that Anchorage would help tackle fake and substandard medicines in Nigeria, adding that it was open to direct supplies to hospitals, healthcare institutions and pharmacies.

Meanwhile, the commissioning underscores the growing role of private-sector investment in the Mbah administration’s drive to expand Enugu’s economic base, with the governor assuring investors of continued government support to improve the business environment and enhance returns on investment.

World.title: Peter Obi promises support as family buries NDC supporter killed in Enugu
World.content:
The remains of Ifeanyi Nwolie, a supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) who was killed by suspected thugs in Enugu State, have been laid to rest.

Mr Nwolie, 43, was buried on Thursday amid tears at his home town in Affa, Udi Local Government Area of the South-eastern state.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that political thugs attacked NDC supporters at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Emene, Enugu, on 10 October and carried out sporadic shootings at the party’s secretariat in Enugu State during the party’s governorship campaign flag-off.

This newspaper gathered that Mr Nwolie died days after the attack following a gunshot injury sustained during the incident.

‘You will not be alone’

The 2027 presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chinyeaka Ohaa, and the senatorial candidates of the party in Enugu, Imo and Ebonyi states, as well as other NDC candidates and supporters attended the burial.

Speaking at the burial, Mr Obi appealed to the family to endure the loss, saying God knows the reason for every incident.

He described Mr Nwolie’s death as “a sad and irreplaceable loss.” Mr Obi assured the bereaved family that they would not be abandoned.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We have come here to you, Mama, and we’re all your children now,” he told the mother of the deceased in Igbo language.

“It is true that the Ifeanyi whom you used to see daily is no longer alive.”

Turning to the rest, he said: “And the family, you will not be alone. We’re now members of this family.”

Mr Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, promised that he and the NDC members would henceforth be part of the family and the larger community.

‘Don’t engage in violent politics’

Mr Obi also urged NDC members and candidates not to engage in violence while playing politics, insisting that the goal of politicking is to seek the development of society, not to kill or harm others.

“The only thing we’re seeking in government is the development of the nation.

“We don’t approve of killing somebody because we are doing politics. We don’t want it to happen again. This is for the NDC and other parties,” he said in Igbo.

“If you’re campaigning, tell the people your plans. I don’t do violent politics.”

NDC governorship candidate speaks

Also speaking, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, Mr Ohaa, said the party was still mourning Mr Nwolie’s death.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased and also consoled the family.

“We’re here to mourn. I am only thanking everyone who came here today to join hands to perform the normal burial ceremony of our brother,” he said in a combination of Igbo and English languages.

Background

Some suspected political thugs attacked NDC supporters in Enugu State on 10 October.

The attack began at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Emene, Enugu, where hundreds of supporters had gone to welcome the NDC governorship candidate, Mr Ohaa, who arrived at the airport ahead of the official flag-off of the party’s campaign.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that many supporters were either attacked with planks or shot at, while others were harassed by the attackers.

Apart from the attack, several vehicles belonging to the NDC supporters were damaged by hoodlums.

The attack continued at the NDC secretariat in GRA in Enugu.

The following day, the Secretary to the Enugu State Government, Chidiebere Onyia, claimed findings showed that the NDC attempted to gather at the airport without approval.

Mr Onyia, a professor, denied allegations that the state government was responsible for the attack.

But in a statement on 12 October, the Secretary of the NDC in Enugu State, Emmanuel Nebo, said the government’s claim that the NDC attempted to hold the campaign flag-off at the airport without approval was false.

“Our supporters only gathered at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport to welcome Sir Christian Chinyeaka Ohaeto upon his arrival.

“The main Campaign Flag-Off event was scheduled and held at his campaign office in GRA, Enugu, not inside the airport,” he said.

The NDC secretary said although the planned airport event was “simple,” the party had already formally notified all relevant security agencies.

The police in Enugu State would later order an investigation into the incident.

World.title: Otu budgets N987.8bn for 2027, capital projects get 72%
World.content:
Governor Bassey Otu of Cross River State on Wednesday presented a budget of N987.8 billion for 2027 to the state House of Assembly.

He earmarked N708.43 billion for capital projects.

Presenting the budget, christened “Budget of Consolidation and Renewed Hope,” Mr Otu said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education and economic diversification.

The governor said the 2027 budget represented a 2.57 per cent increase compared with the 2026 budget.

“Capital expenditure accounts for about 72 per cent of the total budget, while recurrent expenditure stands at N279.38 billion, representing 28.28 per cent,” he said.

The governor said his administration had not obtained fresh domestic or external loans since assuming office in 2023, noting that the state’s existing debt burden was mainly inherited from previous administrations.

He pledged to strengthen internally generated revenue and attract private investment to finance development projects.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reviewing the 2026 budget, Mr Otu said the government raised the spending framework to N963.07 billion through a supplementary budget to accommodate urgent interventions and counterpart-funding requirements.

He listed past achievements, including about 608 km of road projects, support for 8,000 farmers with over 20,000 bags of fertiliser, and the distribution of one million improved seedlings, among others.

READ ALSO: ICPC indicts Budget Office over inclusion of fake agency in 2026 budget

The governor also listed improvements to healthcare and education infrastructure, payment of WAEC fees for indigenes, and the promotion of 14,000 teaching and non-teaching staff as other achievements.

“Infrastructure received the largest sectoral allocation of N246.1 billion, followed by education with N99.6 billion, health with N85.4 billion, and agriculture with N28.2 billion,” he said.

Mr Otu also identified aviation, transportation, and maritime development as key areas for economic diversification.

He urged the assembly to consider and pass the appropriation bill, and pledged his administration’s commitment to prudent management of public resources.

The governor said the budget would consolidate ongoing projects and promote inclusive growth and improved welfare for Cross River residents.

(NAN)

World.title: NEC endorses 90-day plan to ease cost of living for Nigerians, but no specific details yet
World.content:
The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed what it described as a “90-day economic action plan” to ease the cost-of-living crisis caused by government policies and worsened by international wars.

The plan was announced by the spokesperson to Vice President Kashim Shettima, Stanley Nkwocha, in a statement on Thursday.

The statement did not, however, contain specific details of the plan but stated that

“The plan focuses on reducing the cost of living, improving food affordability, attracting investment, and accelerating the delivery of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians.”

Mr Nkwocha added that “The 90-day action plan identifies five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support.”

PREMIUM TIMES reports that Nigerians have, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, been experiencing the country’s worst cost-of-living crisis in a generation. This was first caused by government policies, including the removal of petrol subsidies and the deregulation of the foreign exchange market. The wars between the US/Israel and Iran, as well as the Russia-Ukraine war, exacerbated the crisis.

The government has repeatedly argued that the policies were essential to stave off a government collapse and that Nigerians will soon enjoy the benefits of the policies.

The policies have improved Nigeria’s macro-economy, with external reserves and foreign investment increasing significantly. However, most of Nigeria’s 200 million people have had to grapple with higher food costs than when Mr Tinubu assumed office.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The 90-day plan was presented by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, during the NEC’s 161st meeting held virtually and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima on Thursday.

According to Mr Nkwocha, the NEC also deliberated on Nigeria’s preparedness following the detection of a case of Ebola virus in Abuja, as well as the efforts to eradicate all types of polio from the country.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the NEC is statutorily headed by the vice president and includes all sitting state governors.

Read Mr Nkwocha’s full statement below.

The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate gains from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms.

The plan focuses on reducing the cost of living, improving food affordability, attracting investment, and accelerating the delivery of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians.

The council’s endorsement on Thursday followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, during its 161st meeting held virtually and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

This is just as the vice president said that while President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

The 90-day action plan identifies five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support.

NEC also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with particular emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting of how proceeds from fuel subsidy removal are being utilised.

Presenting the economic outlook, Mr Oyedele expressed optimism about the progress recorded under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery.

He identified the reduction of headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions.

The finance minister’s presentation placed particular emphasis on translating macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment.

Addressing members of council, Vice President Shettima charged state governors and relevant government institutions to ensure that the gains of the administration’s economic reforms translate into affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security for Nigerians.

He said the success of economic policies must ultimately be measured by their impact on citizens’ daily lives, stressing that the responsibility of government extends beyond announcing reforms to building institutions that enable Nigerians to plan their futures with confidence.

“The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said.

According to him, the council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform, and livestock development represent critical decisions about the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress.

“Our separate jurisdictions must serve a common public interest,” Mr Shettima said, emphasising that Nigeria’s federal structure must strengthen cooperation rather than become an obstacle to the delivery of essential services.

On the National Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Bus Initiative, the vice president underscored the need for state governments to support affordable transportation systems that would reduce the financial burden on commuters.

He maintained that the success of the programme should be determined by affordability and accessibility rather than the number of vehicles deployed.

“The cost of reaching a livelihood should never consume the livelihood itself. The passenger’s experience must guide our ambition, because the value of public transport resides in the journeys it makes possible. We should assess success through affordability and access, rather than fleet size alone,” he said.

Mr Shettima maintained that President Tinubu’s economic reform programme was designed to achieve broader national prosperity, noting that governments at all levels have a responsibility to translate its objectives into improved living conditions.

“His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, has made economic reform the instrument of a larger national ambition. Our contribution must give that ambition social depth and productive strength,” he stated.

He urged governors to bring their understanding of local realities into national policy decisions, insisting that effective implementation requires clear responsibilities and practical agreements among the tiers of government.

“Our separate mandates must not become competing excuses. Each Governor carries knowledge that no federal document can supply,” he said.

The vice president challenged members of the Council to judge every policy proposal by its capacity to reduce uncertainty, create opportunities and strengthen public confidence in government.

“Nigerians deserve institutions on which they can organise their lives. Providing that assurance is among the most consequential uses of public authority. That is the assurance we owe them,” the vice president said.

NEC Reviews Ebola Response, Tasks States On Preparedness

Meanwhile, the council received an update on the reported Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory from the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, who allayed fears of a major public health crisis, assuring members that Nigeria possesses the institutional capacity to contain the situation.

The minister briefed the council on efforts by the ministry, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, to operationalise a robust national response system.

He identified coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing capacity, logistics for essential kits and personal protective equipment, and effective strategic communication as critical components of the response.

The minister acknowledged the efforts of 21 state governments that had updated their response plans and urged the remaining 15 states to expedite the establishment of appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms.

NEC directs states to strengthen polio eradication efforts

The council also received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Polio Eradication, chaired by the Governor of Gombe State, Muhammadu Yahaya, and resolved to direct states to conduct post-campaign reviews, particularly in areas where children were missed during immunisation exercises and communities affected by insecurity.

The council emphasised the need for timely release of counterpart funds, strengthened routine immunisation, improved coordination with security agencies and closer cooperation among states to ensure better coverage in subsequent campaigns.

It further stressed that sustained political commitment from governors, traditional rulers and security agencies would remain critical to achieving the complete eradication of polio in Nigeria.

NEC moves to unlock livestock sector’s economic potential

On livestock development, the council received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Livestock Development, chaired by the Governor of Kebbi State, Nasir Idris, and acknowledged the sector’s potential to stimulate economic growth, create employment and improve livelihoods across the country.

The council noted that all states had indicated interest in supporting the federal government’s livestock development initiatives and resolved to strengthen collaboration between the federal and state governments to accelerate reforms and unlock the sector’s economic potential.

FG, States to establish joint financing framework for CNG, electric vehicles

In another major resolution, the council received a presentation on the National Affordable Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Transit Programme by the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Ismaeel Ahmed, and resolved to establish a joint financing framework between the federal and state governments to accelerate the deployment of CNG and electric vehicles across the country.

The council specifically directed that the programme must deliver tangible benefits to citizens through reduced transportation costs, rather than limiting its impact to the provision of alternative-energy vehicles.

It further resolved that relevant authorities should engage transport unions and operators to ensure that savings arising from the adoption of CNG and electric vehicles are passed on to commuters through lower fares.

To give effect to the decision, the council agreed to constitute a committee to coordinate the proposed financing arrangement, engage relevant stakeholders and develop practical measures to ensure that the economic benefits of the programme translate into affordable, accessible and sustainable transportation for Nigerians.

Stanley Nkwocha

Senior Special Assistant To The President on Media & Communications

(Office of The Vice President)

22nd October, 2026

World.title: Understanding the Gen Z approach to life
World.content:
By Morenike Taire, Woman Editor

RECENTLY, an unprecedented interview session with former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo broke the Internet. Obasanjo is one of the most interviewed Nigerians ever, yet this interview was different, specifically because it was conducted by Adebayo Ridwan Abidemi, more popularly known as Isbae U.

The interview, which succeeded in revealing a side of the statesman that had never been obvious to the public, garnered millions of views within the first 24 hours and continues to fascinate viewers because of its sheer creativity, audacity and innovation. The YouTube chat, during which Abidemi referred to the former president as his “tenant” and “employee” for eight years, is a classic illustration of the contrast between the old and new generations, highlighting the conservatism of the older generation and the audacity of the younger one.

On the other hand, 15 former nursing students who were recently suspended or expelled following the publication of a video in August were not so lucky. The young women, who participated in a viral video captioned “No sick oo, na Gen Z full hospital”, were apparently taking part in a “challenge”—a term used to describe the replication of particular digital content for the purpose of trending online.

Generational ‘Wars’ Are Normal, But…

Abidemi and the 15 nursing students were displaying behaviours characteristic of a generation known as Gen Z. Some love them, some hate them, some vilify them; while others admire them.

Generations are groups of people born within roughly the same period who may share similar historical experiences, cultural influences, technologies and social values. These labels are commonly used in sociology, marketing, media and workplace research.

Every generation has regarded the ones that follow as somewhat morally inferior. However, criticism of Gen Z does not seem to fall within the typical complaints about youthful exuberance that have persisted across generations. The major concern is that Gen Z appears to have a disdain for, and disregard for, well-established societal, social and professional norms.

“What sets Gen Z apart,” says Olatoun Lufadeju, a Lagos-based sociologist, “is that they seem to be the only living generation that does not defer to age. They don’t associate wisdom with age or even experience.

“For them, the generations before them have failed them and have been unable to give them a better life. They think, if you are so smart, why is the country like this? Why is the world like this? We should actually listen to them.”

As far as Lufadeju is concerned, the upsides of the generation’s characteristics far outweigh the downsides.

Asked to comment on the expulsion and suspension of the Madonna University students, she told Vanguard, “Is there an actual law against dancing? Seriously, I am asking not rhetorically. I might be wrong.”

Your Negativity, Their Creativity

Despite the admiration for their resilience, most members of older generations regard Gen Z with wariness, at best.

The 15 Madonna University students, despite the initial public outrage, have nevertheless garnered considerable sympathy over the disciplinary actions taken against them, particularly given that they were all in their fifth and final year at the School of Nursing.

Amnesty International has weighed in on the expulsion and suspension of the TikTok dancers, describing the actions as “disproportionate”.

The organisation’s published statement reads: “Imposing heavy-handed academic or disciplinary sanctions would terminate the academic progress of the affected students. The students have the rights to freedom of expression, academic freedom and education. The expulsion and suspension are harsh and would create a chilling effect on the enjoyment of these rights.”

The organization called on the university to ensure that its disciplinary policies and procedures comply with international human rights standards.

A Social Contagion?

While Gen Z is widely perceived as using negativity to make a point, its members do not necessarily have anything to prove. Nonconformity, by its very nature, does not always require justification.

A quick online poll conducted by Vanguard on the subject asked:

“Gen Z is completely rewriting the rules for school, work, and life. If you had to define their ultimate mindset, which trait takes the crown?”

Some 33.3 per cent of respondents described them as “unbound or free”, while 28.6 per cent described them as “nonconformist”; another 14.3 per cent said they were “fluid” or “always varying”, while 23.8 per cent described them as “pragmatic” and “system hacks”.

A UNICEF-led private-sector partnership study, however, found that despite their resilience, creativity and determination, a worrying combination of geopolitical conflicts, climate and ecological crisis, economic slowdowns and mental health challenges is leaving young people feeling overwhelmed, disconnected and adrift, without adequate mental health support or services.

The study, based on a survey of more than 1,000 Gen Z respondents aged 14-25 worldwide, found that, contrary to the beliefs of other generations, Gen Z is deeply engaged with global issues and consumes more news than any other form of content. Its members are also eager to help shape the future.

New Life Realitie

Born during the dot-com era, Gen Z did not have to acclimatize to a digital world. Rather, its members grew up helping to define it. As the generation prepared to enter the job market, the world was hit by the COVID-19 pandemic and the ensuing global shutdowns, accelerating the adoption of remote work—a development that has helped shape Gen Z’s attitude towards employment.

Iyin Aboyeji, a millennial and founder of two billion-dollar companies, found himself in the bad books of Gen Z after publishing a highly controversial LinkedIn article suggesting that young people should work in person during the early stages of their careers.

He stated, “What AI cannot automate is proximity, the senior colleague who corrects your first draft, the room where decisions are made and the peer mentorship and networking that build the skills for us which tomorrow’s business deals are built.”

While members of older generations largely agreed with him, the backlash from Gen Z was phenomenal, targeted a usually beloved tech guru whom many young people look up to. For them, even workplace networking can be disrupted.

One response read, “Working on-site for me isn’t a problem, but for a young person in Nigeria in 2026, what does that cost me in terms of finances, physically, and mentally? There are infrastructural problems that make it harder for a young person such as myself.”

Is the Rash of Information Shaping Gen Z’s Attitudes?

Social media has been widely blamed for Gen Z’s attitudes, with endless scrolling, the promotion of an unrealistic lifestyle, poor attention spans and inadequate sleep cited as some of the consequences of un-fettered access to various platforms.

Speaking recently at the Vanguard Mental Health Summit in Lagos, Professor of Psychiatry Moshood Abiola Bello-Mojeed highlighted concerns about cyberbullying, online exploitation, misinformation, unhealthy social comparison and pressures associated with body image.

Bello-Mojeed added that the digital environment creates additional challenges for young people and called for coordinated action by all stakeholders. She also urged greater accountability in the digital environment.

Lafadeju offers a more nuanced perspective, arguing that Gen Z, as digital natives, has adapted better to digital cultural changes than other generations.

“We always paint bugbears at Gen Z. Different generations, different beliefs. In our own days, we were happy to have any job… For Gen Z, who watched their parents struggle as the Nigerian economy took a nosedive, work just has to pay the bills. Remember they are usually multitalented and capable of multitasking, and they are not shy about having conversations around money.

“I saw one Gen Z individual on social media recently calling out a popular blogger for not paying for services rendered. Only a Gen Z individual can do that, and I assure you, he will get his money. Whether we like it or not, we all have to begin to empathize with their point of view,” she said.

Vanguard News

World.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 23, 2026
World.content:
The Nigerian Naira exchanged at around N1,330.95 to the US Dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM). The official window opened with early spot transactions hovering around N1,330.95 to N1,332.00 per dollar, maintaining relative stability following recent daily fluctuations.

In the unofficial parallel market, street traders and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across major commercial hubs, including Lagos and Abuja, quoted buying rates around N1,360 to N1,365 per dollar, while selling rates traded between N1,375 and N1,380 per dollar.

The gap between the official NFEM rate and the parallel market continues to reflect ongoing demand from retail buyers, small business importers, and individuals seeking foreign currency for international travel and tuition payments.

At current trading levels, exchanging $100 yields approximately N133,095 through official banking and NFEM channels, compared to up to N138,000 when purchased through parallel market operators. Market participants attribute current rate stability to sustained diaspora remittance inflows alongside foreign portfolio interest in domestic yield instruments.

World.title: 2027: Oborevwori banks on 13th-month pay for workers’ support
World.content:
Governor Oborevwori of Delta State

By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha

ASABA—Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State has linked his administration’s 13th-month salary package to workers’ support for the All Progressives Congress, APC, in the 2027 general elections, declaring that civil servants have no choice but to vote for the party.

Oborevwori spoke yesterday in Asaba during the inauguration of the Delta State APC Campaign Council for the 2027 elections, where he unveiled “MORE Plus” as the theme of his re-election campaign.

The governor, who chairs the campaign council, said the additional salary payment had strengthened the connection between workers’ welfare and the continuity of his administration.

“Today civil servants have no choice not to vote us. They have no choice. 13th month (salary) is huge, times two. Some people don’t understand what 13th month,” he said.

Explaining the package, Oborevwori said workers would receive double their regular salary in December, adding that political appointees and public servants were also covered.

“What you’re receiving now is times two in December. That is the meaning of 13th month. Whether you’re an appointee, whether a public servant, whether a civil servant, you’re receiving your 13th month,” he said.

He charged members of the campaign council to take President Bola Tinubu’s message to the grassroots and mobilise voters across polling units and wards.

Describing membership of the council as a call to service, the governor urged members to work with unity, discipline and dedication to secure victory for Tinubu, himself and other APC candidates.

“Our achievements must speak for us, but we must also be prepared to explain them convincingly,” he said, listing infrastructure, education, healthcare, workers’ welfare, youth empowerment and security among the priorities of his M.O.R.E Agenda.

Deputy Governor Monday Onyeme commended Oborevwori for aligning Delta State with the Federal Government and urged party members to consolidate the gains.

Onyeme called on the campaign team to publicise Tinubu’s achievements in local government autonomy, education funding, grassroots development, security, electricity and road infrastructure.

Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, defended the Federal Government’s economic reforms, arguing that difficult decisions were necessary to address the country’s economic challenges.

He said the reforms had caused temporary hardship but were intended to tackle underlying problems, including the cost of fuel subsidies.

Delta APC Chairman, Chief Solomon Arenyeka, said the inauguration demonstrated the party’s readiness to contest and win elections at all levels in 2027.

Former Governor Ifeanyi Okowa, who spoke for Delta North, said expectations were high following the state’s mass defection from the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, to the APC in April 2025.

He urged the council to demonstrate its strength through strong electoral performance, stressing the need to engage voters directly rather than rely solely on rallies.

Representing Delta Central, Olorogun O’tega Emerhor welcomed the APC’s emergence as the ruling party in the state and pledged support for the re-election of Tinubu and Oborevwori.

For Delta South, former Secretary to the State Government, Comrade Ovuozourie Macaulay, said the administration’s achievements would support the campaign, assuring that the district would work towards delivering substantial votes.

Director-General of the campaign council, Senator James Manager, pledged to work with party leaders and members to secure victory, describing the assignment as a demanding task requiring collective effort and sustained grassroots mobilisation.

Vanguard News

World.title: NYSC kidnap: DSS witness exposes how suspects were identified
World.content:
File photo of an NYSC-branded shirt.

By Chidi Nkwopara

OWERRI — A Department of State Services, DSS, operative yesterday told an Imo State High Court how 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members were abducted at gunpoint while travelling to orientation camps, as hearing began in the case against three alleged kidnappers.

The witness, Ikechukwu Emmanuel, who investigated the incident, said the victims and one of the bus drivers identified the three defendants during an identification parade.

The defendants, Usman Aliyu, alias Chonge; Babangida Aliyu; and Mohamed Ali, alias Smallie Pepper, are standing trial on a three-count charge of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms in suit number HOU/22C/2026.

Testifying before Justice Emeka Orafu, the DSS operative said the incident occurred at about 6.30am on October 1, 2026, when the 20 prospective corps members were travelling in two buses from Ibadan to NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states.

He told the court that armed men wielding AK-47 rifles attacked the buses and took all 20 passengers hostage, moving them into the bush.

According to the witness, security agencies in Imo State, including the DSS, launched operations using human and technical intelligence to track the kidnappers and secure the victims’ release.

He said the hostages were eventually released after the payment of ransom demanded by the kidnappers, while investigations continued.

Emmanuel further told the court that intelligence reports indicated that the suspects had moved to Rivers and Abia states, leading to their arrest between October 10 and 14, 2026.

Explaining the identification process, the witness said the three defendants were placed among 10 other persons during an identification parade. He said the abducted prospective corps members and one of the bus drivers identified them.

The witness also told the court that Usman Aliyu, in his confessional statement, said 11 persons participated in the kidnap operation.

The Imo State Director of Public Prosecutions, Mr Martins Udolwu, led the prosecution team, while Mr Nnaemeka S.C. Adipo and Mr Paschal Ofoma represented the defendants.

After the witness’s evidence-in-chief, Justice Orafu adjourned the case to October 27, 28 and 29, 2026, for continuation of hearing.

The judge urged the defence to be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately after the conclusion of his evidence-in-chief, stressing that he did not want the trial to extend into the new year.

“The Defence must be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately he is done with his evidence in chief,” the judge said.

World.title: Nollywood actor Francis Duru dies at 57
World.content:
Veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru has died at the age of 57 following a brief illness, his family has announced.

The family announced his death in a statement posted on the actor’s official Instagram page in the early hours of Friday, expressing appreciation to fans and well-wishers for their prayers and support.

“We, the family of Francis Duru, regret to announce his passing following a brief illness.

“We appreciate your prayers, love, and understanding. May his soul rest in perfect peace. Amen,” the statement read.

Duru is survived by his wife, Adokiye, and children

Duru, who began his acting career in 1989, became widely known for his role as Ahanna in Rattlesnake, the 1995 film produced by the late filmmaker Amaka Igwe.

His death comes months after he dismissed reports that he was battling a life-threatening illness, describing footage circulating online in June as false.

In a video posted on Instagram in response to the reports, the actor rejected claims about his health and criticised those circulating the footage.

Born on July 27, 1969, in Cameroon to Nigerian parents from Imo State, Duru completed his primary and secondary education in Cameroon before moving to Nigeria for university studies.

He studied Theatre Arts at the University of Port Harcourt, Rivers State, graduating with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1996.

Duru made his film debut in Missing Mark in 1989, in a production directed by the late Ndubuisi Oko. His performance in Rattlesnake later established him as a recognised face in Nollywood.

Over his decades-long career, he featured in several Nigerian films, including Blood Money (1997), Stigma (2013) and Mboputa (2020).

In 2020, he won the Best Actor in a Leading Role (Igbo) award at the Best of Nollywood Awards for his performance in Mboputa. He also received the United Nations Ambassador of Peace award in 2007 in recognition of his influence on young people.

Duru served as interim president of the Actors Guild of Nigeria in 2010 and was nominated for Best Actor in a Supporting Role at the Africa Movie Academy Awards that year.

World.title: State Police: 24 states approve bill; Lagos, 9 northern, 2 southern states dilly-dally
World.content:
IGP Disu

By Clifford Ndujihe, Dayo Johnson, Steve Oko, Ebunoluwa Sessou, Boluwaji Obahopo, Jeff Agbodo & Ben

Ngwakwe

THE push for state police to tighten the war against insecurity in the country got a boost, yesterday, as a flurry of approvals that started on Wednesday by no fewer than 13 states brought the number of states endorsing the legislation to 24.

Thus, the constitutionally required 24-state endorsement benchmark needed for the state police bill to become law has been met. Vanguard gathered that more states will conclude deliberations next week.

Currently, 14 of the 17 southern states have endorsed the bill and 10 of the 19 northern states have okayed the move.

Lagos, Ondo, and Ebonyi are the southern states still being awaited.

The nine northern states still dilly-dallying on the legislation are Kogi, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Bauchi, Jigawa, Katsina, Kano, and Sokoto. Five of the 10 states are in the North-West zone. The North-Central has two and North-East three states.

The National Assembly transmitted the 1999 Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, to the 36 state Houses of Assembly on September 16, seeking their concurrence.

The National Assembly had asked the state legislatures to communicate their resolutions within 30 days. However, the period is an administrative target and not a constitutional deadline. It is exactly 38 days since most houses of assembly got the bill. The state legislatures are expected to turn in their inputs on October 29, which is exactly six days away.

Under Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, alteration of the Constitution requires approval by at least two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly, 24 legislatures, before the amendment can proceed to the next stage.

Kaduna ‌‌Assembly endorses constitutional state police

Kaduna State House of Assembly, yesterday, joined approving states by unanimously endorsing proposed amendments to 15 sections of the 1999 Constitution to pave the way for the establishment of state police.

The Chairman House Committee on Information , Mr Henry Marah, disclosed this while briefing journalists on the House proceedings in Kaduna.

Marah, who represents Jaba State Constituency, said the Assembly supported the proposal transmitted by the National Assembly for concurrence.

He said the proposed state police system would strengthen community security, improve protection of lives and property, and create employment opportunities for youths.

According to him, the current security structure limits state governments’ ability to directly hold police authorities accountable for security failures.

He said the proposed system would provide a legal framework for community-based security initiatives and strengthen local responses to banditry and other crimes.

Marah said the Assembly would formulate appropriate laws to guide the operations and welfare of state police personnel when the proposal takes effect.

He assured that funding would be prioritised, even if the state had to reduce spending on other projects.

“Without security, you cannot even go to the farm or go to work,” he said, stressing that protecting human lives should take precedence over infrastructure development.

The lawmaker urged residents to support the proposed state police system, saying improved security would enable farmers to return to their farms and harvest their produce without fear of kidnapping.

Abia assembly concurs

Similarly, the Deputy Speaker, Abia State House of Assembly, Austin Nmeregini, told Vanguard, earlier yesterday, that the Abia lawmakers were at the verge of passing the Bill.

He disclosed that the Bill received the support of the lawmakers during their Executive session, hinting that they were proceeding into plenary where it would be passed into law.

However, Speaker Austin Nmeregini, told Vanguard later in the day that the bill was passed by unanimous vote

Bill yet to be received — Gombe lawmaker

In Gombe, the Chairman, House Committee on Appropriation, Aliyu Baba Manu, said the bill has not been officially presented on the floor of the House.

According to Manu, the bill has neither been formally tabled nor received by the House for consideration. He added that upon receipt, the bill would be referred to the appropriate committee responsible for police matters for further legislative action.

Speaking in a like manner, Deputy Speaker of Gombe House of Assembly said he is unaware of the bill.

Ebonyi to pass bill soon — Speaker

The Speaker of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Moses Ije Odunwa, has said the Assembly will soon pass the State Police Bill.

Odunwa disclosed that lawmakers had commenced deliberations on the bill and were close to completing the process, subject to necessary scrutiny.

He said the proposed legislation was aimed at strengthening the protection of lives and property in Ebonyi State and Nigeria at large.

The Speaker recalled that Ebonyi State had supported the establishment of state police during the National Assembly’s constitutional review engagement, where the state government and Assembly made submissions in favour of decentralised policing.

“We have started deliberating on the bill, and we are very close to its passage,” Odunwa said.

Action on bill delayed in Ondo

In Ondo State, the Chairman, House Committee on Information, Olatunji Oshati, said the draft has been forwarded to all 26 members of the Assembly to study and return with their resolutions for debate at plenary.

“Yes, we have received the draft from the National Assembly. We have read it on the floor of the House and subsequently distributed it to the 26 members of the Assembly to study. The lawmakers are expected to study the document and return with their inputs for full deliberation at the next plenary.

“The State House of Assembly, after thorough discussion under matters of urgent public importance, will add our inputs before returning it to the National Assembly.

“I want to assure that all these will be done within a short period. We won’t delay; we will soon send the State Assembly’s inputs to the National Assembly,” he said.

He however assured that the bill will be passed after the plenary sitting on Monday by the members.

According to him, “the plenary on Monday will decide when the bill will be passed into law.”

Kogi assembly yet to sit

In Kogi State, the House of Assembly is yet to sit on the State police amendment bill.

However, the Assembly admitted some weeks ago that it had received the transmitted copy, but a day was yet to be slated for its debate.

The Members had adjourned to attend an international conference in Rwanda, “maybe by the next adjourned date, answers to your questions will be provided”, Mr. Aka Bayo, Deputy clerk, Administration stated.

Why Lagos Assembly is yet to ratify the Bill — Lawmaker

The Chairman of the Lagos State House of Assembly Committee on Information and Strategy, Mr. Stephen Ogundipe, said the House will reconvene next week to ratify the bill.

Ogundipe disclosed that the Assembly is currently in recess but assured that lawmakers would resume plenary next week to consider the bill and take the necessary legislative action.

He explained that the planned ratification would form part of the Assembly’s legislative responsibilities upon resumption, although he did not provide further details on the specific provisions of the bill.

“The ratification process will be a key stage in determining the bill’s legislative status, subject to the applicable procedures of the House. The Assembly is expected to provide further information as deliberations resume and lawmakers proceed with their legislative business next week”, he said.

Presidential group moves ahead

Meanwhile, the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, on Tuesday, submitted the draft National Policing Bill, 2026, and 29 consequential amendment bills to the Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting review and validation.

The proposed Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, seeks to amend Section 214 of the Constitution to replace the single Nigeria Police Force with a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

In a statement by the Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Working Group, Femi Gbajabiamila, the group said it had completed the drafting stage of its assignment.

The PWG explained that the draft bill was submitted to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, last Monday.

“The submission was made on October 19, 2026, to the Honourable Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan.

“The ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws.

“The Ministry of Justice is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. The Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate,” it said.

Gbajabiamila said the work was proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the State Houses of Assembly, which “must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly”.

On October 15, Gbajabiamila told reporters that the policing bill was “90 per cent ready” and would be transmitted to the National Assembly on October 29.

The Senate passed the bill on June 24, after which it was also passed by the House of Representatives. Tinubu inaugurated the seven-member Presidential Working Group on July 7, and its steering committee started work on August 3 to produce a “technically robust, implementation-ready draft National Policing Bill.’’

World.title: Ebola: FG quarantines high-risk contacts, allays fears; patient zero shows signs of recovery
World.content:
*No evidence of community transmission yet — Minister *Tomori demands full disclosure *Ebola patient in Nigeria is Ugandan-born — Africa CDC *Why Vaccines aren’t available for latest Ebola outbreak *Abia, Enugu, Anambra intensify disease surveillance across LGs *States, hospitals step up preparedness

By Sola Ogundipe, Health Editor

LAGOS — The Federal Government, yesterday said it has intensified efforts to contain Nigeria’s confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease; place high-risk contacts in quarantine, isolate other contacts and strengthened preparedness across states as well as health facilities.

Read Also:

*FG confirms Ebola case in FCT, begins contact tracing

*Ebola patient arrived Abuja Oct. 3 via Ethiopian Airlines from Uganda – Source

*Africa faces ‘complex’ Ebola outbreak after virus spread to Nigeria – WHO

The government also allayed fears of a wider outbreak even as it also announced that the index patient is showing significant signs of recovery, while stressing that there was, so far, no evidence that the infection had spread into the community.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Ali Pate who spoke, expressing optimism that she could recover fully.

But the minister failed to respond on the number of contacts under high-risk or whether any of the 46 contacts have tested positive for the virus.

He however, insisted that government would not take anything for granted despite the absence of evidence of community transmission.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, had on Wedneday, directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, to place the 46 contacts on a no-fly list, comprising 44 persons who came into contact with the patient at a hospital after she developed symptoms and two members of her domestic staff.

Keyamo, in a statement on his verified X account following a virtual meeting with Pate, said he had also directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to notify domestic and international airlines of the restriction.

The measure is intended to prevent the contacts from travelling by air during the period within which symptoms may develop following exposure. The minister said efforts are ongoing to isolate the individuals pending confirmation that they had not been infected.

He also ordered heightened Ebola surveillance at international airports, including temperature checks, travel history monitoring, digital health declarations and stronger coordination with public health authorities.

Speaking at a briefing in Abuja, Pate said the patient’s travel history indicated that the case was imported. She was reportedly asymptomatic on arrival in Nigeria but developed symptoms days later.

He said contact tracing had covered people at the hospital where she received treatment, her domestic contacts and a private medical facility she had visited.

High-risk contacts have been placed in quarantine at a designated facility, while other contacts are being monitored in line with public health guidelines. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, has activated its incident management system in collaboration with the Federal Capital Territory Administration.

“I spoke with the clinicians today, and I understand that the laboratory results show significant improvement. There is a possibility that she will recover fully. However, we cannot take anything for granted.

“We currently have one confirmed case, and our priority is to contain it and prevent transmission into communities or a wider outbreak,” he said.

The government has informed state governments and directed those yet to complete their Ebola response plans to do so urgently. Additional resources have also been mobilised to strengthen the NCDC’s capacity, while the Presidential Task Force on Ebola Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats has stepped up coordination.

Chairman of the task force and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, said Nigeria’s surveillance system enabled early identification of the case.

Gbajabiamila said the patient had no symptoms when she arrived in Abuja, with the symptoms emerging four days later. He attributed the detection to protocols put in place by the Health Ministry, the task force and other agencies.

He assured Nigerians that the task force would strengthen existing protocols and ensure more rigorous enforcement, urging citizens to cooperate with public health authorities.

Africa CDC seeks travel history

Meanwhile, Director-General of the Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr. Jean Kaseya, said the patient was born in Uganda and called for full disclosure of her travel history to help establish where she contracted the virus.

Speaking on Channels Television’s Morning Brief, Kaseya said the woman travelled to Uganda, where she spent some days before her husband joined her. He said the couple returned to Abuja on October 3.

He said African health authorities are working together to determine whether the infection originated in Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo or another location.

“What we want is collaboration from this lady. She has to tell us, to disclose to the authorities; I need this information, Nigeria needs this information because we need also to support Uganda,” Kaseya said.

His comments came amid differing accounts from Nigerian and Ugandan authorities over the patient’s nationality and travel history. Uganda’s health authorities had said the woman is Nigerian and had travelled to eastern DRC for business before transiting through Uganda.

Uganda’s Director-General of Health Services, Charles Olaro, maintained that travelling through Uganda did not establish that the infection was contracted there, adding that the location of exposure remains under investigation.

Kaseya also explained that no vaccine is currently available for the Bundibugyo strain responsible for the outbreak, although clinical trials of candidate vaccines, including one manufactured in Egypt, had commenced.

He criticised what he described as inadequate global investment in developing vaccines for diseases predominantly affecting Africa, arguing that international partners needed to support vaccine research and development more urgently.

Why vaccines aren’t available for latest Ebola outbreak

It explained why the continent has yet to find a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola disease.

Dr. Kaseya, said some partners consider Ebola an African issue, adding that “if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccines would already be available”.

He, however, said that the agency had initiated clinical trials of new vaccines, including a new Bundibugyo vaccine manufactured in Egypt.

Tomori questions response timeline

Renowned virologist and chairman of the West African National Academy of Scientists, Prof. Oyewale Tomori, meanwhile, called on the Federal Government to provide comprehensive information about the case, warning that gaps in official communication could fuel rumours and undermine public confidence.

Tomori said: “The government must be completely transparent about matters like this. We don’t want to hear information in bits and pieces from different sources.”

He called for clearer information about the patient’s movements, the extent of contact tracing and the handling of diagnostic samples, while acknowledging that certain medical details might need to remain confidential.

Tomori recalled Nigeria’s experience during the 2014 Ebola outbreak, when the infection in Liberian-American Patrick Sawyer took several days to diagnose.

He urged health workers to consider patients’ travel histories and possible exposure to infectious diseases before dismissing symptoms as malaria or other common illnesses.

He also called for adequate isolation facilities, trained personnel and medical supplies to manage additional cases should any of the contacts test positive.

“Suppose two or three of those contacts test positive. What happens next? Do we have the hospitals, isolation facilities and other resources needed to manage additional cases?” he asked.

South-East states intensify surveillance

Across the South-East, state governments have activated precautionary measures, strengthened disease surveillance and placed health workers on alert, although no Ebola case has been confirmed in the zone.

In Abia, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health, Dr. Blossom Uma-Kalu, said the government is assessing its preparedness, including the provision of personal protective equipment, thermometers and hand sanitisers.

She said the Infectious Disease Hospital in Aba is nearing completion, while an isolation facility at a specialist hospital in Umuahia is undergoing remodelling.

Uma-Kalu said the state is also considering an additional facility that could be adapted for isolation if necessary.

She urged health workers, particularly those in private hospitals and laboratories, to remain vigilant and promptly report suspected cases.

In Enugu, Commissioner for Health, Prof. George Ugwu, said disease surveillance had been intensified across the state’s 17 local government areas, while the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre had been reactivated.

He said rapid response teams are on standby and urged public and private health facilities to isolate suspected cases promptly and report them to the appropriate authorities.

Ugwu noted that Enugu’s position as a travel and commercial hub, particularly through the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, made heightened surveillance necessary.

In Anambra, Commissioner for Health, Dr. Afam Ben Obidike, announced plans to deploy surveillance officers at strategic locations, including the Chinua Achebe International Airport, Umueri, motor parks, banks and other public places.

He said the state hasmonitored 40 persons of interest, with 33 completing their monitoring period and being cleared, while seven remain under active follow-up. All seven were reportedly stable.

Obidike said the state’s preparedness plan covered surveillance, rapid response, infection prevention, laboratory coordination and risk communication.

In Ebonyi, Commissioner for Health, Dr. Moses Ekuma, said the state had activated precautionary measures, established an equipped isolation centre and trained health workers on infection prevention and control.

He urged residents to practise good hygiene, cook bush meat thoroughly and exercise caution during burials where the cause of death was unknown.

FG urges calm, warns against misinformation

Continuing, Pate said the government had strengthened preparedness in federal hospitals and urged state governments to ensure adequate bed capacity, functional isolation facilities and strict infection prevention measures.

He called for closer cooperation between public health authorities and private medical practitioners, stressing that suspected cases must be promptly identified and reported.

The minister advised Nigerians to wash their hands frequently and avoid contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected or infected persons.

“Ebola is not an airborne disease. It is transmitted through direct contact with infected body fluids,” he said.

He added that the government was monitoring the situation and would rely on scientific evidence in deciding whether to alter plans for conferences, campaigns and other public gatherings.

The government also warned against spreading unverified claims on social media, urging people identified through contact tracing to comply with quarantine and isolation directives.

Pate said Nigeria had the experience and expertise to contain the outbreak, citing the country’s successful management of the 2014 Ebola outbreak.

He urged Nigerians to remain calm, rely on information from recognised public health authorities and cooperate with measures aimed at preventing further transmission.

Anayo Okoli, Steve Oko, Chioma Obinna, Vincent Ujumadu, Ugochukwu Alaribe, Jeff Agbodo, Emmanuel Iheaka, & Chidinma Chukwu also contributed to this report.

World.title: Why food prices remain high despite FG’s interventions, ongoing harvest
World.content:
AI-generated image for illustration.

By Cynthia Alo

Despite the Federal Government’s interventions meant to cushion the prices of farm inputs and ultimately reduce the prices of food items in the country, food prices have remained high even during the ongoing harvest season.

Read Also: Economy: Roadside restaurants drop food quantity, forcing customers to cut budgets

Meanwhile, farmers, agribusiness groups, traders and consumers have attributed several factors, including the high cost of transportation, delayed and uneven distribution of farm inputs, inadequate storage systems and insecurity in some farming communities, to the factors keeping food prices high in Nigeria.

They warned that increasing production alone would not guarantee affordable food if farmers could not preserve their harvests, move produce efficiently to markets or obtain inputs early enough for the planting season.

Renewed Hope Agenda

President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda promised to strengthen food security, increase local production, support farmers and reduce Nigeria’s dependence on food imports.

In 2023, the Federal Government declared a state of emergency on food security and announced plans to invest N200 billion in cultivating 500,000 hectares of farmland, alongside the distribution of fertiliser, seedlings and other farm inputs.

The measures were intended to boost production and ease pressure on food supply.

The administration has since announced further initiatives, including mechanisation support and fertiliser distribution.

In June 2026, the National Agricultural Development Fund launched a programme to distribute 515,720 bags of fertiliser to 128,930 smallholder farmers across 25 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The government also outlined measures to support local fertiliser production, improve access to farm inputs and expand agricultural productivity.

But farmers’ groups are questioning the impact of government interventions, saying the support does not always reach genuine farmers or translate into more affordable food.

What NBS says

Data obtained from the National Bureau of Statistics’ Consumer Price Index report for September 2026 show that, on a year-on-year basis, food inflation stood at 19.59 per cent in September 2026, slightly higher than the 19.57 per cent recorded in August but below the 20.16 per cent recorded in September 2025.

The bureau attributed the movement to price changes in guinea corn flour, sold loose; white maize flour, sold loose; local short-grain rice; eggs; fresh onions; palm oil; fresh green beans; Irish potatoes; okra; fresh tomatoes; dried green peas; plantain; among others.

On a month-on-month basis, the food index fell by 1.55 per cent in September, compared with an increase of 1.02 per cent in August.

The breakdown of food inflation by state shows that Lagos recorded the highest food inflation, at 34.40 per cent, on a year-on-year basis, followed by Imo at 33.79 per cent and Ondo at 31.49 per cent.

On the other hand, three northern states recorded the slowest rises in food inflation on a year-on-year basis, with Taraba recording a negative 7.47 per cent, Yobe a negative 0.37 per cent and Borno a negative 2.18 per cent.
