Email address Get the PDF Free. We send a confirmation link first, and the same address then receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing. Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

The Legal Basis for the Cuts

Rabat gave the law only in general terms and no source cites the exact provision. A reduction of sentence is an administrative benefit decided by the Ministry of Justice, and it is different from a presidential pardon.

Interferencia stresses that sentence reductions and pardons are separate mechanisms. Kast said in mid-May 2026 that he would use pardons case by case.

Kast also said that, as of mid-May, his government had pardoned no one, Meganoticias reported. Rabat said the 2022 reform on sex offenders against minors cannot apply retroactively, Radio Pauta reported.

El Mostrador says that reform does not by itself explain the two Punta Peuco decrees. It adds that the 56 child sex offender reductions are legally distinct cases.

What Punta Peuco Is

Punta Peuco, officially the Centro de Cumplimiento Penitenciario de Tiltil, opened in 1995 under President Eduardo Frei through decree 580. The decree cited the need for special security conditions to protect inmates’ physical and psychological integrity.

Its first inmates were Manuel Contreras, ex-head of the DINA secret police, and Pedro Espinoza. Later arrivals were military and police convicted of dictatorship-era crimes.

As of April 2025 it held 139 men, with an average age of 76 and most in poor health, The Clinic reported. The National Institute of Human Rights (INDH) put its capacity at 130 in 2017.

Why the Prison Has Long Been Controversial

After the Cordillera prison closed, human rights groups and legislators argued that Punta Peuco breaks equality among inmates, 24horas reported. Then Justice Minister Jaime Gajardo said in 2025 that inmates generally have one cell each, The Clinic reported.

The decree cites special security conditions, and a court filing described most inmates as elderly with serious illnesses, The Clinic reported. Concertación governments, the centre-left coalition that ruled after 1990, were criticised for not closing it, 24horas reported.

Boric, Kast and the Prison’s Status

On Sunday, 1 June 2025, Boric announced he would end the special status and open it to ordinary convicts, The Clinic reported. Common-crime inmates began arriving in November 2025, El Dinámo and The Clinic reported.

Kast said in May 2026 that Boric’s change broke a national consensus. Gendarmería then moved three common-crime inmates out by 28 May, El Dinámo reported.

On Monday, 20 July 2026, Gendarmería moved 21 inmates from Colina 1 to Tiltil. The Clinic reported that all appear convicted of crimes against humanity.

The Reaction to the Sentence Cuts

The Frente Amplio caucus, a left-wing party in the opposition, demanded Rabat’s resignation, CNN Chile reported. Deputy Emilia Schneider said the Kast government “has shown its total contempt for the victims”.

The Socialist Party asked the government to review and cancel the decrees, BioBioChile reported. Its statement recalled that Rabat once defended Augusto Pinochet as a lawyer.

Christian Democrat deputy Jorge Díaz said he would consult other opposition groups on a constitutional accusation against Rabat. Radio Universidad de Chile reported the plan, which has not been filed.

Most criticism concerns 56 reductions for people convicted of sexual crimes against minors, approved between March and September, Interferencia found. El Mostrador says those cases are legally distinct from the Punta Peuco ones.

Rabat said he respected the Constitution and the law and called his move diligent, T13 reported. Frente Amplio deputy Carolina Tello said the accusations against the previous government have no basis, in the caucus statement.

The Government’s Announced Legal Change

Rabat said the government will back urgent debate on bills to stop new benefits for people convicted of serious crimes, T13 reported. It will also send its own bill, Radio Pauta reported.

The bill would judge requirements under the law in force when a request is filed. Radio Pauta notes it must pass Congress and settle limits on retroactive criminal law.

The sources do not say whether a change would reach inmates convicted of crimes against humanity. The government has not said it will cancel the two decrees.

What It Means for US Readers

The sources show no travel or business effect, and no change to Chile’s trade ties with the United States. US investors in Chile’s copper and lithium should read it as a test of Kast’s political capital.

Background is in the Rio Times profile of President Kast and the guides to Chile’s political players and its power structure. The Santiago city page covers the capital nearest the prison.

What Is Not Known

The sources reviewed do not name the two inmates, their original sentences, the size of the cuts or the decree dates. They also do not name the legal provision used.

El Mostrador reports three further decrees for serious crimes, two of them for Punta Peuco inmates. It is not known whether the cuts take effect on release or whether victims’ families were told.

What Comes Next

Congress will take up the bills the government says it will fast-track, and the opposition says it is weighing a constitutional accusation. Neither step would reverse the two decrees by itself.

An accusation has not been filed, and the sources give no date for any vote. Whether the government cancels the decrees has not been announced.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Punta Peuco prison?

It is a prison in Tiltil, near Santiago, opened in 1995 for military and police convicted of dictatorship-era crimes. It is run by Gendarmería, Chile’s prison service.

Who benefited from the sentence reductions?

Two inmates at Punta Peuco, one convicted of aggravated kidnapping and one of torture. Their names and the size of the cuts have not been published.

Why did the Justice Minister cut the sentences?

Fernando Rabat says the law provides the benefit and that earlier governments granted it for 20 years. Critics say the Kast government should have refused.

Is a sentence reduction the same as a pardon?

No, a reduction is an administrative decision of the Justice Ministry, while a pardon is a presidential power. Kast has said he would decide pardons case by case.

What legal change has the government announced?

It says it will back bills in Congress and send its own. Benefits would be judged under the law in force when a request is filed.

Does this affect travel to Chile?

The sources show no effect on travel or business. Check the US State Department advisory for Chile before any trip.

Sources: The Clinic, 22 October; BioBioChile, 22 October; T13, 22 October; Radio Pauta, 22 October; El Mostrador, 22 October; Interferencia, 22 October; CNN Chile, Frente Amplio; BioBioChile, Socialist Party; Radio Universidad de Chile, 22 October; The Clinic, the 139 inmates; The Clinic, 22 July 2026; 24horas, history of Punta Peuco; El Dinámo, 28 May 2026; Meganoticias, Kast and pardons (all accessed 23 October 2026).

World.title: Chile Confirms Punta Peuco Sentence Cuts
World.content:
CHILE · JUSTICE

Key Facts — What is happening Chile’s Justice Minister Fernando Rabat confirmed on Thursday, 22 October, that his ministry signed decrees cutting the sentences of two inmates at Punta Peuco, convicted of kidnapping and torture.

— Why it matters Punta Peuco holds former military and police convicted of dictatorship era crimes, and the cuts come as the government already faces criticism over 56 reductions for child sex crimes.

— The numbers Two Punta Peuco inmates are affected, one for aggravated kidnapping and one for torture. The ministry granted 56 other reductions for sexual crimes against minors between 11 March and 13 September.

— Who is who Fernando Rabat is justice minister under conservative President José Antonio Kast. Amnesty International Chile, led by executive director Rodrigo Bustos, says reductions for crimes against humanity would breach Chile’s human rights duties.

— What to watch Whether Congress holds the special sessions planned for Monday, 26 and Tuesday, 27 October, and whether Rabat faces a formal summons or an investigative commission.

— Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US readers and investors face no direct effect, but the dispute adds political pressure on the Kast government and puts Chile’s human rights record back in the news.

Chile confirmed it cut the sentences of two Punta Peuco inmates convicted of kidnapping and torture. The justice minister says the law requires it, while critics ask why.

Chile’s Justice Minister Fernando Rabat confirmed on Thursday, 22 October, Punta Peuco sentence reductions for two inmates convicted of kidnapping and torture. He told T13 radio the decrees were signed, answering with the words “It is true.”

Punta Peuco is a prison in Til Til for former military and police convicted of crimes in the military dictatorship. The decision matters to US readers because it tests how far conservative President José Antonio Kast will go on dictatorship era justice.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Rabat Confirmed on Punta Peuco Sentence Reductions

The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights granted the cuts by two exempt decrees, the outlet Interferencia reported on Thursday. The Clinic and Pauta reported that Rabat confirmed them the same day.

The two inmates are held at the Til Til detention centre, known as Punta Peuco, El Mostrador and BioBioChile reported. One was convicted of aggravated kidnapping and the other of torture.

Rabat said such benefits have been granted for 20 years under governments of different political leanings. “The law establishes it,” he told T13, as The Clinic reported.

He said only the government of former President Gabriel Boric refused all such requests, if memory served. The Supreme Court overturned some refusals in at least four cases, he said, but El Mostrador noted he named no rulings.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Chile 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 3 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Free. We send a confirmation link first, and the same address then receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing. Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

The Legal Basis for the Sentence Cuts

The ministry says it must grant a reduction when the legal requirements are met, BioBioChile reported. As its general basis for such reductions it explains Law 19,856, which allows shorter terms for inmates with outstanding conduct.

Such decrees carry the formula “by order of the President”, which does not mean Kast signed each one. A commission reviews education, work and conduct, and Gendarmería, the prison service, prepares the list.

The sources do not say that Law 19,856 or any other ground was used for the two Punta Peuco decrees. BioBioChile noted that the documents it saw do not show how the requirements were checked.

For the 56 child sex crime cases, Rabat cites a 2022 reform and Supreme Court doctrine on earlier crimes. Interferencia noted that this argument does not explain the Til Til decrees on its own.

Reaction to the Punta Peuco Sentence Cuts

Amnesty International Chile said reductions for crimes against humanity would be grave and would breach Chile’s international human rights duties. Its executive director, Rodrigo Bustos, spoke conditionally, saying it would apply if sentences were indeed cut, El Mostrador reported.

The Children’s Ombudsman, led by Anuar Quesille, asked the ministry to explain the 56 reductions for sexual crimes against minors. La Moneda, the presidential palace, called the report on those cases “malicious”, Noticias Los Ríos reported.

Opposition lawmakers are weighing a formal summons of Rabat and an investigative commission, El Mostrador reported. Congress has special sessions planned for Monday, 26 and Tuesday, 27 October, but no party or deputy was named.

Interferencia first revealed 56 cuts for sexual crimes against minors, covered in Chile Cuts Terms of 56 Child Sex Offenders. Of those, 27 were for child sexual abuse and 29 for rape.

The Legal Change the Government Announced

Rabat said the government will back bills barring new benefits for people convicted of sex crimes against minors, The Clinic reported. He named motions by Deputy Ossandón and Senators Squella, Longton, Flores, Bianchi and Araya.

The ministry will also present its own bill, Pauta reported. It would judge eligibility under the law in force when a request is filed.

These changes target sex crimes against minors, and no source says they would reach dictatorship era convicts. A 2022 reform already excludes some child sex offenders, but Rabat says it cannot apply to earlier crimes.

Kast and the Dictatorship Era Prisoners

In July 2025, as a candidate, Kast said he was open to pardoning elderly or impaired Punta Peuco prisoners. In March 2026 he confirmed he would apply pardons; in May he said he had not promised them for everyone.

Interferencia reported these positions and stresses that sentence reductions and pardons are different legal tools. It says the two decrees raise questions about the criteria the ministry applies.

What It Means for US Readers

There is no direct effect on US citizens or on travel to Chile. The story matters for investors and policy watchers who follow the Kast government, which Chile’s own press now questions over justice policy.

Pressure on a minister in an index country draws attention beyond Santiago, and the Power Index row above shows Chile’s current standing. For background see the Chile explained guide, the Chile hub and the explainer Punta Peuco Prison Explained.

What Is Not Known

The names of the two inmates, their original sentences, the amount cut and the decree numbers and dates have not been published. The ministry’s written statement was not found, and the ministry website could not be opened.

It is not known which legal ground the ministry used or how it checked these two cases. El Mostrador and BioBioChile also reported a third decree, for someone not held at Punta Peuco; sources differ on the crime.

Sources differ on who first reported the cases: Interferencia and El Mostrador both published on 22 October. Whether more dictatorship era inmates received cuts is not known.

What Comes Next

Watch the special sessions planned for Monday, 26 and Tuesday, 27 October, and any move to summon Rabat. The government has not said whether it will publish the decrees or review the two cases.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Chile’s justice minister confirm about Punta Peuco?

Fernando Rabat confirmed on Thursday, 22 October, that his ministry signed decrees cutting the sentences of two Punta Peuco inmates. They were convicted of kidnapping and torture.

What is Punta Peuco?

Punta Peuco is a prison in Til Til known for holding people convicted of human rights violations in the dictatorship. BioBioChile describes it that way.

Why were the sentences cut?

The ministry says it must grant reductions when legal requirements are met, explaining Law 19,856 as its general basis. The sources do not say which ground applies to these two inmates.

Is this a pardon?

No, a reduction is not a pardon. Interferencia notes they are different legal tools, though both feed the debate over dictatorship era convicts.

What legal change is the government proposing?

It will back bills barring new benefits for people convicted of sexual crimes against minors, and present its own bill. No source says the changes cover dictatorship era convicts.

Sources: The Clinic, 22 October; Pauta, 22 October; El Mostrador, Rabat interview; El Mostrador, investigation; BioBioChile, 22 October; Interferencia, 22 October; Radio Universidad de Chile; Noticias Los Ríos (all accessed 23 October 2026).

World.title: Police raid home of Trinidad and Tobago’s acting chief magistrate, seize electronic devices in international investigation
World.content:
Police raid home of Trinidad and Tobago’s acting chief magistrate, seize electronic devices in international investigation

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police in Trinidad and Tobago have searched the residence of Acting Chief Magistrate Brian Dabideen and seized electronic devices as part of a wider investigation involving local and international law enforcement agencies.

The search was conducted on Monday, October 19, at Dabideen’s residence in Gulf View, San Fernando, prompting widespread attention because of his senior position within the country’s judicial system.

According to the Trinidad and Tobago Guardian, Police Commissioner Allister Guevarro confirmed that the operation formed part of a broader investigation involving international partners.

Guevarro declined to disclose specific details, explaining that the investigation was at a sensitive stage and that releasing additional information could compromise future investigative or judicial proceedings.

Investigators reportedly seized electronic devices considered relevant to the inquiry.

However, Dabideen has categorically denied wrongdoing.

Through his attorneys, Prakash Ramadhar, Michael Rooplal and Vishan Girwar, the acting chief magistrate confirmed that he cooperated with police and voluntarily handed over the devices identified in the search warrant.

His legal team emphasized that the execution of a search warrant does not establish that a criminal offence has been committed.

The Judiciary of Trinidad and Tobago has also issued a statement emphasizing the importance of due process, the presumption of innocence and equality before the law.

The Judiciary said it would refrain from further comment to protect the integrity of any ongoing investigation or legal proceedings.

Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar and Attorney General John Jeremie have declined to comment on the investigation, referring questions to the police.

The investigation has attracted considerable attention in Trinidad and Tobago, where Dabideen occupies one of the most senior positions in the magistracy.

Authorities have not publicly disclosed the specific allegations being investigated, and no criminal charge against Dabideen has been confirmed.

World.title: Bukele deploys 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti after gangs kidnap four Salvadorans
World.content:
Bukele deploys 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti after gangs kidnap four Salvadorans

By Breaking Belize News Staff: El Salvador has deployed 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti as President Nayib Bukele intensifies efforts to rescue four Salvadoran military personnel abducted during a gang attack.

According to The Associated Press, the troops arrived in Haiti on Thursday, October 22, a day after Bukele announced a military rescue operation and warned gang leaders of severe consequences if the four men were not returned alive and unharmed.

A Salvadoran government official also indicated that another 100 soldiers were expected to arrive Thursday night, potentially bringing the deployment to 200 personnel.

The four missing Salvadorans are aviation technicians serving with the international Gang Suppression Force in Haiti. They were abducted following an attack on Sunday, October 18, in Croix-des-Bouquets, northeast of Port-au-Prince.

According to authorities, gang members opened fire on an armoured vehicle carrying the men and used explosives during the ambush.

Bukele has emphasized that the missing personnel were assigned to humanitarian operations, including medical evacuations, rather than frontline combat duties.

In his warning to the kidnappers on Wednesday, Bukele invoked his government’s crackdown on criminal gangs in El Salvador, declaring that his country had already eliminated gangs at home and could do the same in Haiti.

The deployment represents a significant escalation in El Salvador’s response to the abductions and comes as Haiti continues struggling with heavily armed gangs that control large sections of the capital and surrounding communities.

The international Gang Suppression Force, which replaced the earlier Kenyan-led security mission, has faced persistent shortages of personnel and resources.

Salvadoran authorities reportedly believe the four missing men are still alive, although their whereabouts remain unknown.

No gang has publicly claimed responsibility for the abductions, and there has been no confirmed announcement that the hostages have been rescued.

World.title: Guyana boy, 6, found headless with body parts missing; spiritual adviser detained as father investigated for murder
World.content:
Guyana boy, 6, found headless with body parts missing; spiritual adviser detained as father investigated for murder

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The shocking murder investigation involving six-year-old Orlando Jaikarran in Guyana has taken another disturbing turn, with police confirming that the child’s body was discovered without its head and portions of his limbs, while his father and a spiritual adviser remain in custody.

Orlando’s partially decomposed body was recovered on Tuesday, October 20, from the Waterloo Main Canal in West Coast Berbice, five days after he was reported missing. Investigators confirmed that his head, part of his left hand and part of his right foot were missing.

According to News Room Guyana, preliminary police investigations suggest that the child was taken to the canal and struck in the neck with a cutlass.

The case gained international attention after the child’s father, 45-year-old Bharrat Jaikarran, reportedly confessed to throwing Orlando into the water despite knowing he could not swim.

According to the Guyana Chronicle, the father allegedly told investigators that a Hindu spiritual adviser, known as a pujari, had informed him that Orlando was not his biological son.

A pujari is a Hindu religious officiant who performs ceremonies and may provide spiritual guidance. The father’s allegation about what the adviser told him has not been independently established.

Police have since detained a second man believed to be the spiritual adviser, according to Guyanese media reports. Both men remained in police custody as investigators pursued the suspected murder.

In another development, police seized six cutlasses and other items during searches in Bath Settlement. Investigators have not established publicly whether any of the weapons were used in the killing.

Meanwhile, a post-mortem examination has failed to determine Orlando’s cause of death. Region Five Commander Senior Superintendent Lonsdale Whithrite confirmed that the examination was inconclusive, while police continued searching for the child’s missing head and portions of his limbs.

The disturbing discovery has raised further questions about the circumstances of Orlando’s death, including whether his injuries were inflicted before or after he entered the water.

The investigation remains ongoing, and authorities have not publicly established the precise circumstances of the child’s death.

World.title: Two men charged with murder of Wilson Perez, who was found decapitated in Carmelita Village
World.content:
Two men charged with murder of Wilson Perez, who was found decapitated in Carmelita Village

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have formally arrested and charged two men in connection with the brutal murder of Wilson Perez, whose body was discovered with severe chop wounds in Carmelita Village, Orange Walk District, earlier this month.

On Thursday, October 22, police confirmed that 23-year-old Belizean labourer Alex Anthony Banner and 22-year-old Belizean labourer Darnell Emil Rhaburn Sergio were jointly charged with murder in connection with the October 12 killing.

Perez was found dead on October 13 after relatives organized a search when he failed to return home the previous night. He had reportedly left his residence around 10:30 p.m., telling family members he was heading to the village football field.

His body was subsequently discovered bearing multiple chop wounds. Sources previously told Breaking Belize News that Perez had been decapitated, while other media reports indicated that portions of his body had also been burned.

Perez was known for his involvement in youth football and served as president of the New Horizon Sporting Club, which helped organize the Orange Walk Under-13 Mundialito tournament.

Police have not publicly established a motive for the killing. The two accused men will face prosecution for murder as the case proceeds through the courts.

World.title: Pastor Kevin Tzib charged with sexual assault, remanded to prison
World.content:
Pastor Kevin Tzib charged with sexual assault, remanded to prison

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 33 year old pastor has been remanded to the Belize Central Prison after being charged with sexual offences.

Kevin Tzib faces six counts of sexual assault and one count of unnatural crime.

Police say the charges were brought after four separate reports were made against him.

Tzib was arraigned on Thursday in San Ignacio, where he pleaded not guilty to the charges. Bail was denied, and he was remanded to prison.

Police have not released further details of the allegations.

The charges are allegations, and Tzib is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

World.title: Missing police constable Kenyon Barrow identified on surveillance footage before being found in Orange Walk; future in police department uncertain
World.content:
Missing police constable Kenyon Barrow identified on surveillance footage before being found in Orange Walk; future in police department uncertain

By Breaking Belize News Staff: New details have emerged about how missing Police Constable Kenyon Barrow was located in Orange Walk on Thursday, October 22, after disappearing for more than a month.

Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Stacy Smith, Staff Officer of the Belize Police Department, revealed during Thursday’s police press briefing that Barrow was identified on surveillance footage at a location he was known to frequent before his disappearance.

According to Smith, officers were immediately dispatched to the location and successfully located the missing constable.

Although Barrow appeared to be in relatively good physical condition, Smith said he was receiving medical attention as a precaution.

Barrow was reported missing on September 18 and had been the subject of an extensive search operation involving police officers, Belize Defence Force personnel and community volunteers.

During Thursday’s briefing, journalists also questioned Smith about Barrow’s employment status within the Belize Police Department, particularly since authorities had previously reported that he had abandoned his post.

Smith explained that established departmental procedures would determine how the employment matter is addressed but stressed that Barrow’s health and well-being remain the immediate priority.

She indicated that the department was prepared to provide whatever assistance the constable required during his recovery.

Smith also confirmed that investigators have not established where Barrow remained throughout his disappearance or whether he had left Belize during that period.

Further inquiries will be conducted once he has received the necessary medical attention.

The police department thanked everyone who assisted in the search, including members of the public who offered prayers and support.

Smith expressed particular relief for Barrow’s mother and family, noting that they could now rest easier knowing he had been located safely.

World.title: Pastor Kevin Tzib denied bail, remanded to prison on seven sexual offence charges; police warn church leaders against covering up abuse
World.content:
Pastor Kevin Tzib denied bail, remanded to prison on seven sexual offence charges; police warn church leaders against covering up abuse

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Pastor Kevin Tzib, founder of Dunamis Ministries in San Ignacio, has been remanded to the Belize Central Prison after being formally charged with six counts of sexual assault and one count of unnatural crime.

Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Stacy Smith, Staff Officer of the Belize Police Department, confirmed during Thursday’s press briefing that the 33-year-old pastor of Santa Elena pleaded not guilty when he appeared before the San Ignacio Magistrate’s Court.

The prosecution objected to bail, which was denied, and his case was adjourned until January 21, 2027.

According to Smith, the allegations involve four male complainants and span more than five years, from February 2021 to July 2026.

During the briefing, journalists questioned Smith about allegations that some complainants had previously raised concerns with church officials but reportedly received no satisfactory response.

Smith explained that while she could not confirm the circumstances surrounding those claims, anyone found to have deliberately obstructed an investigation or interfered with the course of justice could potentially face criminal consequences.

She specifically referenced the offence of perverting the course of justice, explaining that institutions or individuals who become aware of criminal allegations must ensure their actions do not obstruct the administration of justice.

Smith also issued a broader warning to religious institutions, schools and other organizations that allegations of sexual abuse should be reported to police rather than handled exclusively through internal procedures.

She emphasized that police officers investigating sexual offences receive training in trauma-informed approaches designed to protect complainants from further victimization.

“It is always concerning whenever there are allegations of sexual offences against persons who hold positions of trust,” Smith stated, referring to teachers, religious leaders and other authority figures entrusted with the care and protection of vulnerable persons.

“No position, no title, no standing in the community places anyone above the law,” she stressed.

Dunamis Ministries previously issued a statement indicating that it would take appropriate administrative measures while respecting the judicial process and the presumption of innocence.

The allegations against Tzib remain before the court.

World.title: Belizean Pride: Anthony Mangar earns Doctorate in Educational Leadership at Saint Peter’s University in New Jersey, USA
World.content:
Belizean Pride: Anthony Mangar earns Doctorate in Educational Leadership at Saint Peter’s University in New Jersey, USA

By Zoila Palma: Sacred Heart College is celebrating the academic achievement of alumnus Anthony Mangar, who has successfully completed a Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Educational Leadership, with a concentration in Higher Education, at Saint Peter’s University in New Jersey, United States.

The college congratulated Dr. Mangar on the milestone, describing his achievement as a reflection of his dedication to lifelong learning, professional development and educational leadership.

Sacred Heart College expressed pride in seeing one of its former students reach this accomplishment and encouraged him as he continues to contribute to the field of education.

World.title: Six charged in alleged $110-million loan fraud
World.content:
CHUNG... the activity alleged in this matter, although sophisticated, expansive and creative, was no match for the skills of our forensic investigators

THE Financial Investigations Division (FID) is reporting that six people have been arrested and charged following a joint investigation with the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) into an alleged fraudulent loan scheme totalling approximately $110 million.

According to the FID, the loans were obtained from a prominent financial institution between January 2023 and December 2024 through applications supported by forged and fictitious documents. The agency also said that loan proceeds were then moved through bank accounts held by third parties.

The FID identified the six individuals charged as Errol Williams, 39, a business owner and accountant from St Catherine; Christine Elliot, 52, a customer service representative from St Catherine; Staisha Campbell, 24, who is unemployed and from St Catherine; Paige Dixon, 34, a labourer and farmer and Adrien Kerry-Ann Gordon, 44, a self-employed shopkeeper, both from Kingston; and Admarie Ashman, 58, who is self-employed and from the Kingston 3 area.

The FID said Williams was arrested on September 24, 2026, during an intelligence-led search operation. “He is alleged to have benefited by approximately $20 million from the scheme. He was offered bail in the sum of $1.5 million with a surety,” the FID said in a news release late Thursday evening.

Elliot and Campbell were arrested and charged on September 16, 2026, following a search operation. They are alleged to have received $1.35 million and $1.2 million, respectively in loan proceeds. Each was offered bail in the sum of $500,000 with a surety.

Dixon and Gordon were arrested on September 9, 2026, following a search operation. Each is alleged to have received $1.5 million in loan proceeds, which was withdrawn. They were offered bail in the sum of $500,000 each with a surety, while Ashman was arrested and charged on October 20, 2026, following a search operation at her home.

“All six face charges of engaging in a transaction involving criminal property under the Proceeds of Crime Act; uttering forged documents under the Forgery Act; obtaining credit by fraud under the Larceny Act; and conspiracy to defraud under common law,” the FID said.

It added that Williams is also charged with possession of criminal property.

The FID said Ashman, who remains in custody, is scheduled to appear in the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court, Criminal Division on Friday, October 23, 2026. The other five accused appeared in the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court, Criminal Division, on October 13, 2026, each represented by an attorney.

The matter was adjourned for mention on February 16, 2027 with the following bail conditions:

• A stop order has been placed on their movement;

• They have surrendered their travel documents;

• They are to report to the police twice weekly; and

• They are not to interact or interfere with witnesses.

The FID said that on December 24, 2024, the financial institution reported to the police that documentation submitted in support of loan applications made by 79 individuals, between January 2023 and December 2024, was fraudulent.

“The institution had identified irregularities in the applicants’ files and, when it tried to verify the applicants’ stated places of employment, could not locate them at the addresses provided. By then, the loans had been disbursed and were not being repaid,” the FID said.

“It is alleged that forged job letters, utility bills, and pay advices were submitted to support the loan applications. Analysis of the bank accounts of two of the accused indicated that most of the loan funds received were subsequently transferred to third-party accounts,” the FID added.

The law enforcement agency also said it is further alleged that Williams “created fictitious documents, provided bank accounts to others and instructed that loan funds be transferred to them, and obtained a fraudulent driver’s licence and birth certificate and opened bank accounts in fictitious names to facilitate the deposit of loan funds”.

The FID said that Ashman was taken into custody following a search operation conducted on October 20, 2026, by members of the Constabulary Financial Unit, assisted by personnel of the Kingston Eastern Police Division, under a warrant issued pursuant to the Financial Investigations Division Act.

“She was held on reasonable suspicion of engaging in a transaction involving criminal property, obtaining credit by fraud, uttering forged documents and conspiracy to defraud, and was subsequently charged,” the FID said.

It added that during the search, “Ashman was found in possession of two separate forms of Government-issued photo identification, a driver’s licence and an electoral identification card, which carry different dates of birth: One in her name and the other in the name ‘Cassandra Burton’. Numerous items, including banking cards, letters and other printed documents, were seized by the police, taken into custody and entered into evidence.”

Commenting on the matter, FID Chief Technical Director Dennis Chung said: “The activity alleged in this matter, although sophisticated, expansive and creative, was no match for the skills of our forensic investigators. It spanned a long period, involved many individuals, and relied on documents, accounts and identities made to look legitimate. The investigation required close collaboration and the expertise of one of our longstanding strategic partners, the JCF.

“We also want the public to understand how easy it can be for persons to get caught up in a money mule scheme such as this. A request to receive money, or to lend an account or identification, can seem harmless, but it can make a person a pawn in someone else’s criminal activity. We urge everyone to remain vigilant, to ask questions and to refuse any such request, as you will be held criminally liable.”

Arguing that financial institutions also have a critical role to play, Chung said: “We encourage them to strengthen their due diligence capabilities, both in assessing loan applications and applicants, and in vetting their own employees, whether new hires or those with long tenures. Due diligence is not a one-time exercise. It must be sustained, as it protects institutions, their customers and the wider financial system.”

The FID also reminded the public that the charges are allegations and that each of the accused is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law.

World.title: ALL FOR ONE
World.content:
SHALLOW... it’s something that I’m sure is topical at the board level of the ICC, and maybe in the coming period, when there’s a discussion around that, who knows, it may be revised

ST JOHN’S, Antigua, CMC — President of Cricket West Indies (CWI) Dr Kishore Shallow has come out in defence of his chief executive officer Chris Dehring, who recently called for a revamp of the International Cricket Council’s (ICC’s) revenue model.

In describing the current model as unfair, Dehring said the world’s governing body needed to provide greater benefits for smaller cricketing nations such as the West Indies.

His comments came after it was revealed that the West Indies did not receive a share of India’s bilateral broadcast rights in the just concluded white-ball tour of India that featured three ODIs and five T20Is.

Under the current bilateral broadcasting arrangements, the board hosting an international series generally retains the revenue generated from the broadcast rights.

In an interview with Guardian Media Sports, Shallow said while Dehring’s comments were misconstrued, he was in full agreement with his colleague.

“I suspect it was sort of taken out of context what the CEO [Dehring] said.

“… I think the point that Chris was making, or he tried to make, was by and large an amendment to the commercial model would help smaller members, the likes of Cricket West Indies, New Zealand, and so on,” Shallow said.

“It’s something that I’m sure is topical at the board level of the ICC, and maybe in the coming period, when there’s a discussion around that, who knows, it may be revised.”

Shallow, however, admitted that the West Indies did benefit financially from the tour of India.

He said sponsorship opportunities were secured during the tour, noting that the size and commercial influence of the Indian market had helped CWI attract partners for the One-Day International and Twenty20 International series.

“When we host India, this is one of the series that we generate significant revenue from.

“Though we don’t get a share of their broadcast deal, we do benefit from them financially from the tour,” Shallow said.

World.title: 2026 Kia Sportage: Still a top contender
World.content:
The 2026 Kia Sportage X-Line continues its own impressive path in a crowded, cut-throat segment of the automotive market — the compact SUV. (Photos: Rory Daley)

Kia continues to blaze its own path in the vicious war that is the compact sport utility vehicle segment to much success. Leading this fight is the Sportage nameplate.

Venerable to the brand, but a relative newcomer in relation to class rivals, the Sportage, in X-Line trim, is a formidable option for buyers, and that continues strongly with the 2026 update.

EXTERIOR

The Sportage long made the transition from the visual conservatism that persists in the competition. For 2026 it has embraced its science-fiction looks even further. The arrow-shaped lighting has been converted to a mostly vertical configuration. This gives the Sportage a very distinct signature at night. The rear lights have been tweaked as well. Body lines are still sharp and angular. Nineteen-inch wheels are standard for the X-Line. A few new colours, including returning matte paint options, can make the Sportage stand out even further in the SUV malaise that affects modern parking lots.

INTERIOR

Access is via the traditional Kia detonator style key fob. Once past the keyless entry, the leather multi-function seats slide back and forth to aid ingress and egress for a taste of the premium life, as do the welcoming lit door handles. The roomy cabin isn’t as radical as the outside, having a clean, modern design that is very technology-forward.

Material choice and build quality are high, with soft-touch elements at the main contact points. Part of the ergonomic layout is that many functions have been moved into the infotainment screen. The few physical buttons are for frequently used features, like dual-zone climate and audio.

A wireless charging pad sits in the centre console alongside several storage solutions around the interior. The panoramic sunroof delivers a sense of space to all occupants. Not that rear passengers are wanting for much with amenities like heated seats. Front seats have both ventilation and heat. A refined cabin keeps exterior noises to a minimum while maximising the quality stereo system. At night, the ambient lighting provides a similar function.

Behind the ‘Squircle’ steering wheel is digital instrumentation that melds into the 12.3-inch touchscreen for the infotainment. Things run fast, smooth, and with clarity on both screens. Especially important, a live camera feed of either side of the vehicle pops up whenever the indicators are used. USB ports are plentiful, and smartphone connectivity is a breeze.

ON THE ROAD

Where the Sportage has always lifted itself above the rest is its drivetrain. However, even it cannot stop the march of demands from the modern SUV buyer.

For 2026, the X-Line can now be had in either petrol or diesel. This expands the market for the Sportage, while still appeasing those who still hold dear the ethos of an SUV. Those still stuck with the vision of clattering and black smoke should know Kia has long banished these things. The 2-litre turbodiesel delivers its wallop of low-end torque in a vigorously linear manner, pulling the Sportage along effortlessly to real-world speeds. It never intrudes negatively in any manner on the driving experience, including the pump, as frugality is another trait it possesses.

The transmission is just as invisible, unless the paddle shifters are engaged. Even then, the shifts are fast and flowing. Suspension-wise, the Sportage treads the fine line between comfort and control, never being harsh or too soft to upset occupants. Along with the all-wheel-drive system, the Kia inspires confidence over a wide variety of road conditions and speeds. Should one not want to drive, the Driver Assist suite can switch from safety to short bouts of supervised autonomous operation.

VERDICT

The Sportage, in X-Line trim, has always kept its connection to the original rules of SUV-dom, diesel power, and all-wheel drive, while layering modernity on top of all. However, even it cannot defy current demands and buying trends. But, rather than giving in, Kia has compromised by offering a petrol option, and — gasp — even front-wheel drive. All that hasn’t affected the Sportage X-Line. It’s still old-school cool, an SUV in touch with its past with an eye towards the future. It’s equipped and drives like something more upmarket, and yet priced like a bargain.

World.title: Mt Pleasant FA book consecutive Concacaf final spot after 3-1 aggregate win over Club Sando
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Defending champions Mt Pleasant FA qualified for consecutive finals of the Concacaf Club Championships after winning the semi-final return leg against Club Sando of Trinidad 2-0 at Sabina Park on Thursday for a 3-1 aggregate.

Second-half goals from Warner Brown and Nickalia Fuller made amends for a first-half penalty miss by Trayvon Reid, his second in the series, as Mt Pleasant FA set up a match-up with the winner of the other semi-final where Portmore leads Violette of Haiti 3-1.

The Jamaican team held the advantage coming into the game as they away goal in the 1-1 draw in Trinidad a week earlier gave them the edge.

Reid should have given them the lead in the 36th minute after Kyle Ming was fouled in the Sando penalty area, but the striker, who repeated his long, slow run up from last week, saw his shot saved by goalkeeper Teshaun Ragoo.

He however made some amends by providing the pass that led to Brown’s opening goal in the 57th minute to give them the lead in the game and on aggregate.

The failure by Mt Pleasant’s goalkeeper Shaquan Davis to hold on to a ball in the 60th minute, almost led to an equalising goal but Luke Philip fired over the crossbar.

Sando had another chance to score five minutes later but Davis was equal to Jaron Pascal’s shot from about three yards out.

Fuller, who replaced Brown in the line-up, killed off the game in time added when he fired past Ragoo from about 20 yards out.

— Paul A Reid

World.title: Unstable weather expected Friday through Sunday — ODPEM
World.content:
Motorists navigate heavy water on Short Hand Road in St Andrew in October 2025 as heavy rain pelted sections of the Corporate Area, flooding streets and triggering traffic snarls. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaicans are advised to prepare for showers and thunderstorms starting Friday and continuing through the weekend.

The Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management said Wednesday that a broad trough currently across the northwestern Caribbean is expected to move closer to Jamaica by Thursday night.

Consequently, unstable weather conditions are expected across the island beginning Friday morning.

The forecast is for periods of showers and thunderstorms, which may be heavy at times, to affect most parishes, especially eastern and central parishes, through Sunday.

Fishers and other marine interests, both inshore and offshore along the north and south coasts, should exercise caution, as sea conditions are expected to deteriorate in the vicinity of showers, thunderstorms, and squalls.

World.title: Water pressure
World.content:
Addressing a Jamaica Observer Press Club on Wednesday, Water Minister Matthew Samuda (left) acknowledges the public’s concerns about higher water bills, while NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the utility needs sufficient revenue to keep operating.Naphtali Junior

WATER Minister Matthew Samuda and National Water Commission (NWC) officials are defending the utility’s proposed 51 per cent tariff increase, arguing that rising operating costs, ageing infrastructure, and repeated droughts have made higher revenue necessary to maintain and improve water supply.

Speaking at a Jamaica Observer Press Club on Wednesday, Samuda acknowledged the public’s concerns about higher bills, but argued that the country can no longer postpone major repairs to its water system, while NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the utility needs sufficient revenue to keep operating.

“If we could have asked for one per cent and been okay we would have asked for one per cent. No politician on the planet Earth is interested in increasing the cost of living. This is a necessary step to resolve long-standing issues in our water sector,” Samuda said.

He said Jamaica is “in a race against time” to replace ageing infrastructure and improve the reliability of water supplies, warning that the country’s long history of inadequate investment has left the utility facing mounting challenges.

In the meantime, Shaw noted that the NWC needs to be able to meet the public’s expectations while maintaining its daily operations.

“We need to continue the operations from one day to the next. Our citizenry is expecting that when they go home and turn on that tap, there’s water in it. There can’t be any worse feeling. So if you were to measure when you go home and you turn on [the switch] and there’s no light versus turn on and there’s no water, I think it’s a no-brainer, and as such, this tariff is going to right-size our position to ensure that we continue to deliver, as is our commitment to the citizens of Jamaica,” he said.

Samuda said the proposed increase must be viewed against the economic and environmental challenges Jamaica has faced since the last interim tariff adjustment granted in 2019.

He said the COVID-19 pandemic caused significant revenue losses when hotels and other commercial customers shut down, while disruptions to supply chains and rising prices subsequently increased the cost of operating the utility.

He added that droughts in 2022, 2023 and 2025; along with Hurricane Beryl and Tropical Storm Rafael in 2024; alongside Hurricane Melissa last year, further affected the NWC’s operations and revenue.

The minister argued that the utility continued to incur expenses even when drought reduced the amount of water available to sell.

He also pointed to rising energy costs and changes to staff salaries, saying the NWC’s energy costs were now close to 50 per cent higher than in 2019, while salaries had doubled over the same period.

“Nobody plans for three out of your five worst droughts ever during this period. Nobody plans for the worst El Nino in 200 years, which is what this is becoming, and… when we talk about these things people say, ‘El Nino? Whatever.’ But the last time we had an El Nino like this it triggered global famine. This is not a normal weather phenomenon that we are going through,” he added.

Samuda argued that these pressures had been absorbed while the NWC’s tariffs remained unchanged, but said the utility could no longer defer essential repairs to its ageing infrastructure.

He noted that the NWC had never replaced even one per cent of its asset base in a single year during Jamaica’s independent history — a shortfall he said had contributed to the deterioration of pipes and other infrastructure.

He pointed to repeated breaks in a major pipeline at Coral Gardens in Montego Bay, which he said had broken six times in one month and required a $170-million intervention to safeguard the main supply line serving the city.

“The reality is the capital replacement ratio of a utility is not intended to fall below one per cent of total capital replacement being done on an annual basis. In our independent life that has never happened…we’ve never replaced one per cent of the asset base of the water commission in a single year. We’ve never gotten close, and that is the utility standard globally. So what you have happening in the middle of that seven-year period is also the collapse of ageing infrastructure. I should be changing the third generation of those lines now, not the first generation in that way,” he said.

Samuda said the combination of ageing infrastructure, climate-related pressures, and decades of inadequate investment have left Jamaica with urgent work to do.

“Ultimately, it is our responsibility to do now what should have been done a long time ago. We will do it. And we can have confidence that at the back end of our work and our investment in these varying programmes, they will have the confidence; and I assure them in the coming years we’ll have other things to complain about other than potable water in the pipes,” he said.

The proposed 51 per cent increase has not been approved by the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR), which is to review the NWC’s application.

Furthermore, Acting NWC President Kevin Kerr separately told the Jamaica Observer that the application includes a significantly lower proposed increase for the utility’s lowest consumers, but said the details could not yet be released because the OUR had not reviewed the application.

World.title: Gully bank relocation
World.content:
From left: K2 developer Richard Lake; Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness; developer Michael Lake; and Phillip Paulwell, Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal, cut the ribbon to the development. At back is Delano Seiveright, state minister in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce.(Photo: Andrew Holness on X)

AN initiative by the Government to relocate people whose houses are situated on gully banks, and who are often affected by adverse weather events, is to be piloted in four communities across the Corporate Area.

The disclosure was made by Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness on Wednesday, during his address at the official opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony of the K2 housing development in downtown Kingston.

Although the timeline of the pilot’s execution was not disclosed, Holness said the project will facilitate the construction of new abodes for people who will be relocated, or the provision of grants for them to source other spaces to call home.

One of the communities of concern mentioned by Holness was the flood-prone Burger Gully, situated in the Kingston Eastern constituency.

“We will be selecting maybe four communities across the Corporate Area to start the pilot project to have persons who are living on the gully banks, particularly those that are at risk of an epiphenomenal weather event, to help them to move from the gully banks. We cannot continue this unsafe practice… that must come to an end,” Holness said.

Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal Phillip Paulwell, who was also at the function, had disclosed in August that close to 150 residents of Burger Gully had signalled their willingness to relocate.

The flooding of the gully, an informal settlement also called 17 1/2 Mountain View Avenue, has been an ongoing problem, but worsened last year as sections of the gully which runs through the community were damaged by flood waters.

At that time, Paulwell said lands were identified in the communities of Mountain View and Rockfort to facilitate the relocation exercise, but a response was being awaited from minister with responsibility for works Robert Morgan.

Holness maintained Wednesday that the issue of communities which are currently irregularly settled “must come to an end”, but underscored that “the success of any government policy is dependent upon the government’s ability… to do what it says it’s going to do”.

“In my own constituency I have demonstrated to the people there how the Government can effectively do a relocation. In the best circumstances, relocation is always disruptive. In the best circumstances, persons are going to feel traumatised by relocation. No one wants to have their house uprooted, their furniture taken and destroyed. Nobody wants to have to move from where they have made their life,” said Holness, who is Member of Parliament for St Andrew West Central.

According to Holness, the National Works Agency will also test a programme that will reclaim the reservations [of buildings] 20 feet away from the gullies in Kingston.

“Whenever I speak like this, immediately everybody starts to get worried [that,] ‘Boy, the Government going to come throw me off [my land].’ That’s not what the Government wants to do. The Government has a right in law to, for the public good, have persons relocate. But the relocation must be done in such a way that the people who are relocated are made no worse off,” Holness said.

The K2 development, located in Bournemouth Gardens, Kingston 2, is a 10-storey residence featuring 119 units. It was developed by Sherbourne Limited, led by Michael and Richard Lake.

World.title: Mental Chung sees The Psychic Realm
World.content:
Mental Chung .

An animator/graphic designer by profession, Mental Chung wanted to express that creativity when he launched his music career eight years ago.

He called his sound Reggae Barque, which can be heard on The Psychic Realm, the St Ann artiste’s first album.

Released on October 10, it contains six songs which Mental Chung produced for his Art Creed Records.

“The songs come from new age spiritual concepts surrounding the hidden forces and ones guiding us in life,” he reasoned. “I went for a more mainstream, youthful sound that has elements of reggae, soul and dancehall.”

Quinting Pink Pinch is the only song from the project released to date. The Psychic Realm’s songs are driven by ethereal beats conjured by Stephen Dajure and Aye Psycho.

Their rhythms complement what Mental Chung describes as “playful, militant and thought-provoking” music.

Born Reinardo Chung, he got his creative start as an animator almost 20 years ago with Bad Influence, an eight-minute, dancehall-inspired film released in 2010. It won an award at the Reggae Film Festival which was held in May 2011 in Kingston.

Mental Chung’s stocks rose even more with the Dutty Bwoy series, which was driven by his love for dancehall culture. It has animated cameos by stars like Bounty Killer, Beenie Man, and Usain Bolt.

Lead, Blaze It, and Talk Back are some of the songs that announced Mental Chung’s music career.

— Howard Campbell

World.title: Die Suche nach dem Super-Sozi
World.content:
In der SPD brodelt es gewaltig an der Basis und in der Fraktion. Arbeitsminister Hubertus Heil bringt sich als neuer Parteivorsitzender in Stellung und sägt am Stuhl von Lars Klingbeil. Maximilian Heimatzheim analysiert, wer als weibliche Doppelspitze infrage kommt und warum Manuela Schwesig noch zögert.

Im 200-Sekunden-Interview fordert der SPD-Bundestagsabgeordnete Ralf Stegner eine personelle Neuaufstellung seiner Partei. Der Parteilinke erklärt, warum die Sozialdemokraten dringend wieder als breite Volkspartei auftreten müssen, um den Absturz bei künftigen Wahlen zu verhindern.

Auf dem CSU-Parteitag inszeniert sich der bayerische Ministerpräsident Markus Söder als unangefochtener Herrscher. Doch Landtagspräsidentin Ilse Aigner bleibt eine interne Gefahr. Nikolaus Doll beleuchtet, warum das taktische Rennen um das Amt des Bundespräsidenten über Söders politische Zukunft entscheidet.

Das Berlin Playbook als Podcast gibt es jeden Morgen ab 5 Uhr. Rixa Fürsen, Maximilian Stascheit und das POLITICO-Team liefern Politik zum Hören – kompakt, international, hintergründig.
