World.title: Hungary’s 23 October long weekend is here: When shops and pharmacies will be open
World.content:
Most shops in Hungary will close on Friday, 23 October, for the national public holiday, but normal Saturday opening hours will resume the following day. Here is what residents, expats and visitors need to know about shopping, pharmacies, post offices and rubbish collection over the three-day weekend.

Hungary is heading into a three-day long weekend as 23 October, the national holiday commemorating the 1956 Revolution, falls on a Friday this year. While most shops will shut for the public holiday, many services will return to their usual schedules on Saturday.

If you need to buy groceries or pick up medication, it is worth planning ahead to avoid finding closed doors.

Are shops open on 23 October?

According to 24.hu, under the general rules, shops will be closed on Friday, 23 October. Normal Saturday opening hours will apply on 24 October, while shops are expected to operate as usual on Sunday.

There are some exceptions for those who need to shop on the public holiday. Petrol stations and their shops may remain open, as may certain 24-hour convenience stores and smaller shops where the owner personally serves customers.

Other businesses that may open on the national holiday include:

Standalone florists

Newsagents

Sweet shops

Restaurants, cafés, bars and entertainment venues

Most shops inside shopping centres are expected to close on Friday. However, cinemas, restaurants and other leisure facilities within malls may still operate, depending on the venue.

Market opening hours will vary. Some markets have announced that they will close, while others plan to welcome customers, so check with your local market before setting off.

Photo: Daily News Hungary

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

Where can you find an open pharmacy?

Pharmacies will operate according to the holiday duty rota over the long weekend, the National Public Health and Pharmacy Centre (NNGYK) has announced.

On Friday, 23 October, medicine supplies in most towns and cities will be provided by 24-hour pharmacies, pharmacies that remain open on public holidays, and those operating an on-call or emergency service.

You can find the addresses and telephone numbers of pharmacies that are open or on duty through the official pharmacy search database. The information is also available in Hungary’s EgészségAblak health app.

On Saturday, pharmacies that normally open on rest days will generally be available until noon rather than following their usual Saturday schedule. After that, on-call or emergency pharmacy services will be available.

The NNGYK advises people to make sure they have enough of their regular medication before the holiday. Families with children should check that they have suitable fever and pain relief medicines, while adults may also want to stock up on remedies for cold symptoms, coughs and sore throats. Older people and those taking regular medication should pay particular attention to having sufficient supplies.

Will post offices and rubbish collection services operate?

Post offices will be closed on Friday, 23 October, according to the Hungarian Post’s published holiday opening arrangements. If you need to send or collect something, check the opening hours of your local branch for the rest of the weekend.

Rubbish collection, however, will continue according to the usual schedule. If your bin is normally collected on Fridays, it should still be emptied on 23 October.

Schools will also close for the autumn break

The autumn school holiday begins on Friday, 23 October, and runs until Sunday, 1 November. Thursday, 22 October, is the final school day before the break, and classes resume on Monday, 2 November.

The holiday period includes not only the 23 October national holiday but also All Saints’ Day on 1 November.

Tip: If you plan to visit a shop, market, pharmacy or other service on Friday, check its opening hours online beforehand. Holiday schedules can vary, particularly for smaller businesses and local markets.

World.title: Budapest’s newest metro line could be extended to two suburbs by 2035!
World.content:
A major proposal backed by Budapest’s District XV could extend Metro Line 4 in both directions, reaching Budaörs in the west and the Fót Auchan area in the north-east. The ambitious plan would also include large park-and-ride facilities, but it still needs detailed studies and support from the government and the capital.

Budapest’s Metro Line 4 could become the backbone of a much larger suburban transport connection under a proposal approved by the District XV council. The concept would extend the line westwards towards the Auchan shopping centre in Budaörs and eastwards through Zugló and Újpalota towards another Auchan site near Fót.

According to Portfolio, the proposed deadline is ambitious: the entire extended line would enter service by 31 December 2035 at the latest. However, the council’s decision is a request to begin preparing the project, not a commitment that construction will go ahead.

Park-and-ride facilities would help keep cars out of Budapest

A key element of the proposal is the construction of large park-and-ride (P+R) and bike-and-ride (B+R) facilities at both ends of the extended line, near the Auchan sites in Budaörs and Fót. The aim is to persuade commuters travelling towards Budapest from the M1/M7 and M3/M2 motorway corridors to switch to public transport before reaching the capital’s busiest roads.

According to the proposal, this could help reduce congestion, air pollution and through-traffic in inner Budapest, while easing pressure on roads in District XV and other residential areas. The extended line would also create stronger links between suburban railways, the metro, trams and buses, potentially making journeys across the wider metropolitan area easier.

If you missed it: Budapest’s busiest M3 metro to be extended after EU funding secured!

Zugló and Újpalota could gain new connections

The eastern extension would provide a high-capacity, step-free connection through areas including Zugló, Thököly Road, Bosnyák Square and Újpalota. The exact route has not yet been settled.

The proposal calls for detailed professional assessments before a final route is selected. These would include passenger-demand modelling, urban planning studies, cost-benefit analysis, environmental assessments and public consultation.

Two possible routes are being considered for the section from the Szentmihályi stop towards Fót. The District XV proposal favours option B, citing the need to protect green spaces.

The council also stresses that the section near Újpalota and the Pólus Centre must be planned and built with strict environmental safeguards. These would include protecting existing natural areas and local ecosystems, as well as restoring affected land and landscaping after construction.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

The proposed timetable runs until 2035

The proposal sets out a demanding schedule for preparing and delivering the extension.

By 30 June 2027: Complete a preliminary feasibility study covering route options, passenger forecasts, network connections, station and depot requirements, technical needs, environmental impacts, costs, risks and potential funding sources.

Complete a preliminary feasibility study covering route options, passenger forecasts, network connections, station and depot requirements, technical needs, environmental impacts, costs, risks and potential funding sources. By 31 December 2028: Complete the permitting documentation for the selected option and begin the necessary regulatory, environmental, construction and railway-authority procedures.

Complete the permitting documentation for the selected option and begin the necessary regulatory, environmental, construction and railway-authority procedures. In 2029: Conclude implementation and financing agreements between the government, Budapest Municipality and the relevant district and local councils.

Conclude implementation and financing agreements between the government, Budapest Municipality and the relevant district and local councils. By the end of 2035: Aim to bring the entire extended line, from the Budaörs Auchan area to the Fót Auchan area, into service.

The document acknowledges that these dates are political targets and cannot override statutory procedures or technical safety requirements.

The M4 metro line. Photo: BKK

The district cannot decide on the metro alone

Although District XV has approved the proposal, the district council does not have the authority to plan, permit and deliver a metro extension independently. It is asking the government and Budapest Municipality to launch the preparatory work, involving organisations including the Budapest Transport Centre (BKK), Budapest Transport Company (BKV), the Ministry of Construction and Transport, and the local authorities concerned.

The council’s decision does not create an immediate construction obligation or commit the district to a specific level of spending. The project’s cost and financing requirements would only become clearer after the feasibility study and cost estimates are completed.

The district mayor has been asked to send the decision to the prime minister, the construction and transport minister, Budapest’s mayor, the heads of BKK and BKV, and the mayors of Budaörs, Fót, Törökbálint and the relevant Budapest districts. The mayor must also coordinate with the other local authorities and report back to the council within 60 days on responses and progress.

Could European Union funding help pay for it?

The proposal fits with the broader emphasis on rail-based transport and reducing commuter car traffic associated with Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy’s portfolio. However, financing remains one of the biggest unanswered questions.

Vitézy said in September that EU funds made available to Hungary could support several major transport projects by 2029, including HÉV suburban railway upgrades, an extension of Metro Line 3, suburban rail developments and improvements to regional railway lines.

World.title: Democracy Digest: Czech Culture Ministry Cuts Funding for Velvet Revolution Anniversary
World.content:
Former Hungarian central bank chief detained; govt tries to solve budget dilemma

Hungary’s former central bank governor, Gyorgy Matolcsy, was detained on Wednesday on suspicion of economic fraud causing substantial financial losses and the use of forged documents. Under Matolcsy, the Hungarian National Bank spent lavishly on refurbishment projects and established several foundations that channelled money into dubious foreign investments and projects that seemed to benefit family and friends. Several hundred billion forints are alleged to have been diverted from the central bank during his tenure or lost through investments. Media estimates put the total losses at 400-500 billion forints (1.0-1.4 billion euros). The current governor, Mihaly Varga, a former finance minister, and his team had submitted more than 30,000 pages of documents to the special investigative committee on central bank affairs by the end of September. Matolcsy’s detention signals the new government and prosecutors are getting serious about making key figures in the previous administration accountable for financial losses incurred during their 16 years in power. Matolcsy, once former PM Viktor Orban’s cherished economy guru, became governor of the central bank in 2013 after serving as economy minister in 2010-2014. Matolcsy’s term ended in 2025. His son and people in his business circle were reportedly among the main beneficiaries of lavish renovations to the central bank building.

Hungary’s new government tabled its first draft budget for 2027, causing disappointment in various quarters. The finance minister warned that budget discipline is necessary to prepare the country for joining the euro, planned for 2030-2032. The government has pledged to cut the deficit from the current 7.0 per cent of GDP to 4.9 per cent by the end of next year and to 2.9 per cent for the end of its term in office in 2030. Inflation is forecast at 3 per cent and GDP growth at 2.4 per cent. Both Finance Minister Andras Karman and PM Peter Magyar acknowledged that there is a need for further wage increases in several sectors, but those could only happen “step by step”. As for immediate measures, the government fulfilled its electoral promise of doubling childcare to 24,000 forints (66 euros) a month per child and raising the minimum pension from January 2027. The draft budget would increase corporate taxes for multinationals, aligning with the global minimum tax regulations, from the current 9 per cent to 11.25 per cent. The government is introducing a special wealth tax for assets over 1 billion forints, and will further tax energy companies and banks. Major investments are pledged for health care, transport and energy, mostly funded by the unblocking of frozen EU funds. Magyar argued in his two-hour speech to parliament that cutting the deficit is essential, pointing to France and Romania as examples of governments unable to halt the spiral in spending. “Powerful, major economies – including European economies – are struggling in a debt trap, with the burden of interest payments choking their economies,” he said. Most controversial is the promised 1.5-trillion-forint (4 billion euros) cut in public sector funding. The police said they were disappointed by the 15 per cent wage increase and teachers voiced concerns about the 25 per cent increase pledged by the government from 2027. Workers in the cultural sector staged a small protest against their 10 per cent rise. “There are also sectors where there are no wages increases at all,” Magyar pointed out to those complaining, while asking for more societal solidarity.

World.title: War Crimes in Prison Camps Still Haunt Montenegro-Croatia Relations
World.content:
For more than three decades, Radmila Simovic from Montenegrin town of Niksic has been waiting for justice for her husband Ratko, who was killed at the age of 27 in the Croatian Lora military prison in Split in 1992.

Ratko Simovic was one of 14 Yugoslav People's Army (JNA) members from the Montenegrin towns of Niksic and Savnik who were tortured and killed in Croatia in 1992. The remains of 12 of the soldiers were later discovered in mass graves in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but full accountability for their deaths has yet to be established.

“My husband Ratko was not just a name in a case file or a number in a register. He was a man, a husband and part of a family that had its own life, its own plans and its own future. All of that was taken away from us,” Simovic told BIRN.

“Families should not have to spend decades searching for information and reminding institutions that the victims existed... It is the responsibility of the institutions to take action, keep us informed and demonstrate that establishing the truth is their duty, not our endless struggle,” she added.

World.title: Bulgaria’s Presidential Frontrunner Holds Lead Despite Drone Controversy
World.content:
Bulgaria is heading to presidential elections this Sunday and expectations are that the Ukraine-skeptic acting President Iliana Iotova will win. As former vice president under Prime Minister Rumen Radev when he was president, and supported by Radev’s party Progressive Bulgaria, Iotova’s victory would increase Radev’s grip on power.

The elections come amid tense moments geopolitically. Bulgaria’s zone in the Black Sea was hit by drone attacks on October 6 and 13, similar to attacks that occurred in Romania’s territorial waters this month. After these events, the government faced criticism for a poor response and the lack of a defence strategy as well for the widespread reluctance among ministers to name Russia as the likely attacker.

The elections on October 25, happening on the same day as snap elections in neighbouring Serbia, present a contest between two candidates who are running as independents but who are each supported by various political parties.

The Radev-backed acting President Iotova and her designated vice president, the director of the country’s state newswire Bulgarian Telegraph Agency Kiril Valchev, will face off against her main opponent: the reform-minded banker and 2026 interim Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov. Georgi Kandev, former chief secretary general to the Interior Ministry, is Gyurov’s running mate.

World.title: Merz Sees Montenegro in EU by 2028 as Berlin Process Summit Opens
World.content:
At the Berlin Process summit in Milocer, Montenegro, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday that Montenegro could realistically become the European Union’s 28th member by 2028. He urged Western Balkan countries to accelerate reforms and regional cooperation.

Speaking at the opening of the summit, Merz said that EU and regional leaders had made progress since last meeting in Tivat in June focused on the EU integration of the Western Balkans.

“Since we’ve met in Tivat in June, we have managed to get the enlargement process back on track, and you all know how difficult it used to be. But now we are on a positive path,” Merz said.

At a joint news conference with Montenegrin Prime Minister Milojko Spajic later the same day, Merz offered a concrete timeline for Montenegro’s EU accession, by 2028.

“We believe that is realistic,” he said.

Merz stressed that the current push for gradual integration into the bloc must remain merit-based.

The idea of gradual EU integration is being pushed most prominently by France and Germany. It would give candidate countries some benefits of integration before full membership such as potentially including greater access to the EU single market, research and education programmes, and observer participation in some EU meetings, without voting rights.

Access would depend on progress with reforms and could be withdrawn if a country backtracked.

“Let me be clear – gradual integration is also merit-based. We as the EU have delivered, but the reforms and the political will must come from you,” he said at the summit’s opening.

Merz also urged Western Balkan countries to strengthen regional cooperation, arguing that economic integration would make the region more attractive to investors and prepare it for the EU single market.

“You will succeed in the EU only if you work together, and you are doing that,” he said. “Eight million people in one market are simply more interesting for investors than in six small ones.”

Commenting on efforts to end Russia’s war in Ukraine, Merz stressed the importance of European involvement in negotiations.

“We all believe that lasting peace cannot be achieved without Europe. And every negotiating format that contributes to this goal is welcome,” he said.

Montenegrin Prime Minister Milojko Spajic said enlargement was central to Europe’s security and unity, reaffirming Montenegro’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

“Europe must bring the same clarity of purpose to enlargement,” Spajic said, describing it as “a reunification of our continent” that would extend freedom, security and opportunity to Europeans still outside the bloc.

World.title: Match-Fixing Probe Rocks Greek Basketball Federation
World.content:
Hellenic Basketball Federation President Vangelis Liolios is pictured at the EOK headquarters in Marousi, 03 October 2023. Photo: EPA/ALEXANDROS VLACHOS.

Greek police said on Thursday that six people have been arrested in an investigation into alleged attempts to manipulate basketball matches linked to domestic and international betting rings.

Greek media report that among the arrested is Vangelis Liolios, president of the Hellenic Basketball Federation, whose lawyer has denied the allegations.

The arrests followed a coordinated operation on Wednesday across the Attica region, Achaia and Katerini, led by the police directorate responsible for combating organised crime. Five suspects were arrested during the operation, while a sixth voluntarily reported to the police and was subsequently arrested.

According to a police statement, the arrest warrants concern alleged offences including “soliciting or accepting gifts and other benefits, offering advantages to referees or sports officials, and illicitly interfering with basketball matches to influence their progress, nature or outcome.”

Apart from Liolios, suspects also include current and former referees and other figures connected to the sport, according to Greek media reports.

Liolios has denied wrongdoing. His lawyer, Panagiotis Papaioannou, spoke outside the courthouse and described the case as a “poorly concocted scheme”, arguing that those making accusations against his client had themselves previously been reported by Liolios and asked to be investigated.

The searches yielded 14 mobile phones, six laptops, 22 USB storage devices, two tablets, memory cards, a hard drive, team shirts and memorabilia, police said. Additionally, 931,463 euros in cash and other electronic devices were seized from their homes.

In a statement issued on October 21, the Hellenic Basketball Federation said its board had met to brief members on the ongoing legal proceedings concerning Greek basketball. The federation said it would “continue to monitor” the case through official announcements and formal procedures.

The six suspects have been referred to the competent prosecutorial authorities as the investigation continues.

World.title: Dzimi’s Diggers: Big Contract Follows Show of Loyalty to Serbia’s Ruling Party
World.content:
One March morning last year, before the sun was up, a convoy of tractors and diggers snaked through downtown Belgrade and parked, in a line, around the Serbian presidency building and the park in front of it.

Days later, a protest was due, staged by a student-led movement calling for accountability for the deaths of 16 people when a concrete canopy at a newly renovated railway station in northern Serbia collapsed in November 2024.

Serbia’s then president, Aleksandar Vucic, warned of plans by the protesters to incite “major violence”.

The heavy machinery was there as a buffer between the protesters and Vucic’s supporters.

Among them were diggers of a company called Dzimi Commerce, diggers that Serbia’s NIS oil company – majority-owned by Russian Gazprom – and provincial authorities in the northern province of Vojvodina had hired for years. Until August this year, Dzimi Commerce was co-owned by 63-year-old Mile Samardzija, a close backer of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, SNS, before he transferred his 50 per cent share to his daughter. Samardzija remains a director.

In the end, there was no “major violence”. The tractors and diggers had their tyres slashed and windows broken, but this was a small price to pay for Samaradzija.

In January this year, his company received its most lucrative public contract yet, worth 1.1 million euros, with NIS subsidiary Naftagas, BIRN can reveal. Though Gazprom holds a majority stake in NIS, just under 30 per cent is still in Serbian state hands.

Experts say the case highlights the cosy, mutually beneficial relationship between the SNS and certain Serbian businesses, which put their resources at the ruling party’s disposal in return for financial rewards.

“Driven by the interest of profit, many are ready to enter into a pact with the authorities,” said Bozo Draskovic, a former board member of Serbia’s Anti-Corruption Agency.

“And in the service of that business, they put all their resources at their disposal – equipment, machines, means of transport, even workers.”

The collaboration appears to go even further in the case of Dzimi Commerce.

According to police case files seen by BIRN, the company’s co-owner of Dzimi Commerce, Ljiljana Teslic, reported Samardzija to the police last year for allegedly threatening her.

Teslic’s lawyer said Samardzija had been trying to push her out of the firm – with the help of “SNS representatives”.

BIRN contacted Samardzija, Dzimi Commerce, Naftagas, and the SNS for comment but none of them responded. Teslic declined to comment.

Close ties to Vucic regime

World.title: Berlin Process Needs to Level the Playing Field in Bilateral Disputes
World.content:
On October 22, Montenegro will host the Berlin Process Leaders’ Summit while itself dealing with a neighbouring EU member state’s power to halt its EU accession progress.

The country is widely considered a frontrunner for EU membership and has provisionally closed 21 of 33 negotiating chapters. Yet neighbouring Croatia is holding up progress over unresolved bilateral issues ranging from war crimes and missing persons to state property claims, maritime borders and the Jadran sailing ship.

Few would question the importance of investigating war crimes or settling state borders, which are legitimate matters that should not be pushed aside for the sake of enlargement. The real question is: is it acceptable for an EU member state to make the accession process conditional on its own demands without any scrutiny of the demands’ relevance, proportionality or prospects for resolution? When bilateral disagreements become EU accession vetoes, they cease to be a problem for just the two countries involved.

This issue has repeatedly arisen across the Western Balkans. In May 2024, Albania’s relations with Greece became strained after Albania imprisoned Fredis Beleris, the ethnic Greek mayor-elect of Himara, who was convicted of vote buying. Greece warned that the affair could affect Albania’s EU ambitions.

World.title: Four Croatian Aminess Campsites Win Prestigious ADAC Superplatz Award
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – Four Croatian Aminess campsites have taken home the prestigious ADAC Superplatz award, further spotlighting the progress camping in Croatia has experienced.

The latest prestigious ADAC Superplatz award has been given to Aminess Style Camping Atea Resort on the island of Krk. Poslovni reports that the latest prestigious ADAC Superplatz award has been awarded to Aminess Style Camping Atea Resort on the island of Krk, as part of the jubilee 20th Croatian Camping Congress, thereby joining the camping resorts Maravea and Sirena in Novigrad and Avalona on the island of Pag, which already carry this label.

The latest awards come at a time when Croatian camping is further strengthening its already enviable international position. Croatia is increasingly profiling itself as one of the highest-quality European camping destinations, and Aminess, with its investments, innovations and high management standards, is confirming its position among the leading Croatian companies in the premium camping segment.

“Four campsites with the ADAC Superplatz label are confirmation of the quality of Aminess’s camping offer and its position at the very top of Croatian camping, but also an incentive for further investment in its development. We are particularly proud of Atea Camping Resort, in whose development we invested 32 million euros last year. Such awards show that investments, knowledge and the dedication of employees bring concrete results. Our ambition is to actively raise European camping standards by developing products that, in terms of quality, facilities and guest experience, compete with the best in Europe. Croatian camping is at the very top in Europe, and Aminess wants to actively contribute to its further development and strengthening of competitiveness,” said Mladen Knežević, President of the Management Board of Aminess.

The renovation of Aminess Atea Resort, worth a hefty 32 million euros, was completed in 2025, transforming the campsite into a five-star premium resort. The renovation included raising the quality of accommodation, arranging pitches and modern accommodation units, developing additional facilities for guests and introducing modern digital solutions. Special emphasis was placed on preserving the natural environment and increasing the share of green areas, while reducing accommodation capacities in order to provide guests with greater privacy, comfort and a higher-quality holiday experience. Achieving the highest quality standards, including the criteria for ADAC Superplatz, was one of the key goals of this investment.

ADAC Superplatz is otherwise one of the most prestigious awards in the entire European camping industry and is awarded by the German automobile club ADAC on the basis of very strict quality criteria. The award is therefore an important indicator of excellence, but also additional confirmation of the competitiveness of Croatian campsites on the demanding European market.

World.title: Croatian Studio Mipmap Developing Digital Version of HEAT Board Game
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – The Croatian studio MipMap is currently developing the digital version of the award-winning and wildly popular HEAT board game.

The Croatian studio MipMap has joined forces with Asmodee, whose portfolio includes some of the world’s best-known board games. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that the Croatian independent video game development studio Mipmap Digital, in cooperation with the international company Asmodee (whose portfolio includes some of the world’s most famous board games such as CATAN, Ticket to Ride and Dobble) is developing the official digital adaptation of the award-winning board game HEAT: Pedal to the Metal, published by Days of Wonder. The digital version of the game will be available on Steam as well as on devices running iOS and Android.

putting a digital spin on a 60s wonder

Set in the golden age of motor racing back during the 1960s, HEAT: Pedal to the Metal is a board game by Asger Granerud and Daniel Pedersen in which victory depends not only on speed, but also on timely decisions and judging how much the engine can be pushed. Players use cards to manage speed, successfully negotiate corners and compete against friends, computer-controlled opponents and players from around the world.

One of the main challenges for the talented Croatian development team was to transfer the experience of playing HEAT at the table onto screens of different sizes. The digital adaptation features three-dimensional depictions of four tracks located in the USA, France, Great Britain and Italy. Players will be able to race against computer-controlled opponents known as Legends, organise local races with friends, take part in championships that include garage upgrades, sponsorships and different weather and track conditions. Cross-platform play will also be available, along with private rooms and automatic player matching. The Legends expansion will be included free of charge from day one, and additional official expansions are planned after launch.

The cooperation between Mipmap Digital and Asmodee began with a simple conversation at the SPIEL Essen 2024 fair. The Croatian studio approached Asmodee representatives with the idea of a digital adaptation of HEAT, and the first meeting gradually grew into a collaboration with Days of Wonder on the development of the game. One of the main challenges for the development team was to transfer the experience of playing HEAT at the table onto screens of different sizes. The digital adaptation remains faithful to the rules and visual identity of the original game, while using the possibilities of the digital format for clearer presentation of information, camera focus on key moments of the race and automation of certain parts of the game.

a major partnership

“Two years ago, we went to SPIEL 2024 hoping to start a conversation about the possibility of a digital adaptation of HEAT. Returning to this year’s fair, now that the game is in development, is therefore particularly significant for us. HEAT has a very distinctive identity, both visually and in the way it is played, and we have worked closely with Days of Wonder to transfer everything that makes this game special into the digital version,” said Joško Mikuličić, director and co-founder of Mipmap Digital.

“We’re extremely pleased to be working with Croatia’s Mipmap. An exciting and distinctive board game like HEAT deserves the best possible digital adaptation. We’re more than sure that Mipmap, owing to its experience and passion for HEAT, will create an outstanding digital experience for players and further enrich the experience of playing this board game,” said Christian Dunn, Head of Interactive Content Licensing at Asmodee.

who are mipmap?

Mipmap Digital is otherwise independent Croatian video game development studio specialising in digital adaptations of board games. The studio was born out of a shared love of games and the well-known problem of board game enthusiasts: finding the time, place and company for joint play. Drawing on experience in video game development, the team decided to make favourite board games more accessible in digital form while retaining their distinctive characteristics.

Mipmap Digital’s portfolio includes digital adaptations of the board games Roll Player, Point Salad and Canvas, while HEAT: Pedal to the Metal is currently in development. Asmodee is one of the world’s leading companies in the board game industry, dedicated to connecting people through games and stories. With over 2,200 employees worldwide, the company has one of the largest portfolios of board games.

World.title: Negotiations Continue Between Zagreb Airport and Wizz Air
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – Negotiations are continuing between Zagreb Airport and Wizz Air, with the popular airline citing cost issues being the primary remaining obstacle.

During September, 455,530 passengers passed through the airport, while the growth rate for the first nine months of the year fell to just 1.1 percent. As is somewhat seasonally appropriate, the capital’s airport recorded its third consecutive monthly drop in passenger numbers; in September traffic fell by 3.3 percent, continuing the slowdown that began back in July. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that during that month, 455,530 passengers passed through the airport, while the growth rate for the first nine months of the year shrank to only 1.1 percent. The latest figures come at a time when Croatia Airlines is reducing capacity during the process of renewing its fleet.

new routes and a new incentive scheme

Passenger numbers at the airport are expected to fall again in October, followed by a gradual recovery in November, while December, according to estimates, should remain at last year’s levels, reports Ex-Yu Aviation News. Zagreb Airport has attracted four new routes this year, including those to Warsaw (Modlin), Tel Aviv and Beijing (via Bucharest). By comparison, six new routes were introduced in 2025 and ten back in 2024. During 2026, the airport also lost four routes, three of which were operated by Croatia Airlines. Several factors have influenced the slowdown in growth: rising fuel prices, which make airlines more cautious about launching new routes; the stall in the expansion of Croatia Airlines’ network; and the increase in almost all basic airport charges and fees at Zagreb Airport.

Zagreb Airport is trying to return to stronger growth and has launched a new incentive scheme for which airlines can apply until the 31st of December. This new model significantly lowers the threshold for obtaining incentives compared with the previous system – in which the wildly popular Ryanair was the only beneficiary, and carriers were required to achieve at least 35,000 passengers per year. This change is expected to make the system more accessible, especially for smaller markets and airlines considering routes with lower passenger volumes. Another key difference concerns the duration and flexibility of the programme.

ongoing negotiations with wizz air

The previous model was designed for a five-year period, while the new one is limited to four years but introduces mechanisms that reward better results in the initial phase. Carriers that exceed the figure of 100,000 or 150,000 passengers in the first five years of operations can secure the continuation of incentives without the obligation to meet annual thresholds. As part of its new growth incentive model, Zagreb Airport is excluding certain destinations from the list of eligible ones, as they are considered either sufficiently developed or strategically less important within this programme.

Despite interest in Zagreb, Wizz Air announced this summer that costs associated with the airport remain the main obstacle to establishing a base in Croatia’s capital. Nevertheless, they have not ruled out the possibility of introducing flights to Zagreb and confirmed that negotiations are ongoing. Zagreb Airport ended last year with a record of almost 4.7 million passengers, an increase of 9.2 percent compared with 2024. Based on currently reported capacities on scheduled routes, Zagreb Airport is expected to record an overall capacity increase of 1.8 percent in November.

This is mainly contributed by Ryanair, which will offer just over 17,000 additional seats, as well as the new Air China route and capacity increases by Austrian Airlines, KLM and Air Serbia. For December, stagnation is currently forecast, with around 100 fewer seats than in the same month last year. Capacity reductions at Croatia Airlines, Lufthansa and Qatar Airways are the main factors negatively affecting growth during the last month of the year.

World.title: Hajduk Beats Thun 1-0 to End 32-Year Wait for European Away Win
World.content:
Hajduk made it two wins from two in the Conference League league phase on Thursday night, beating Thun 1-0 in Switzerland. Dalisson scored the only goal in the 17th minute. Gonzalo Garcia’s side dominated the first half but had to withstand heavy pressure after the break, in a match that featured remarkable misses at both ends.

The result ended a long wait. Hajduk’s last away win in the group or league phase of a European competition came on September 28, 1994, when Aljoša Asanović’s 88th-minute goal earned a 1-0 win over Steaua in Bucharest in the Champions League. Following their 2-1 win over Ajax in the opening round, Hajduk now have a maximum of six points from two matches.

Lineups

Thun (4-4-2): Steffen; Fehr, Bürki, Bamert, Mambwa; Reichmuth, Roth, Kait, Maier; Labeau, Dursun

Hajduk (4-2-3-1): Silić; Acapandié, Hadžikadunić, Marešić, Hrgović; Del Moral, Fayad; Bamba, Dalisson, Šotiček; Šego

Match report

Hajduk set the tone from the start. Bamba went down under a challenge from Mambwa in the Thun box in the 2nd minute without getting a decision, and needed treatment on his ankle. A minute later, Šego tested Steffen, who saved comfortably.

Hrgović broke superbly down the left in the 10th minute, but his pass for Šego was cut out. By the 13th minute, Hajduk had two-thirds of the possession and were pressing Thun high up the pitch, and four minutes later that pressure paid off. Nico Maier gave the ball away in midfield, and Dalisson carried it to the edge of the box. His first shot was blocked, but the ball came straight back to him, and the Brazilian flicked it into the net with the outside of his boot for 1-0.

Thun should have equalized in the 24th minute. Brighton Labeau got away from Acapandié and fired low inside the box, but Silić saved, and Furkan Dursun dragged the rebound wide from 16 meters. Mambwa blazed over from more than 20 meters in the 30th minute.

Thun saw more of the ball after falling behind, but Hajduk’s pressing kept them from settling, and the chances kept coming for them. Šotiček’s effort from around 20 meters in the 33rd minute was heading just inside the post until Steffen tipped it behind. From the resulting corner, Hrgović was free on the left of the box, but he fired well over. Fayad then shot straight at Steffen from 17 meters, and in the 37th minute Bamba struck the post directly from a corner.

Hrgović blocked a Fehr shot in the 44th minute. Two minutes were added, and Hajduk went in 1-0 up at the half, a lead that could easily have been bigger.

Neither side made changes at the break, but the balance shifted quickly. Del Moral was booked in the 47th minute for stopping a Mambwa run, and Thun began to push Hajduk back. Fehr curled wide of the right post from the edge of the box in the 54th minute. Labeau’s turn and shot was blocked two minutes later, and Roth was booked for pulling back Dalisson to stop a counter. Reichmuth then shot straight at Silić in the 58th minute.

Marešić was booked in the 64th minute. A minute later, Del Moral headed a Fehr free kick clear just ahead of Bürki, and Labeau sent a shot over from around ten meters after a corner.

Hajduk had a golden chance to double their lead in the 68th minute, when Olivier Mambwa shoved Bamba in the box, and Gillett pointed to the spot. Šego stepped up but struck a weak penalty down the middle, an easy save for Steffen.

Melnjak then replaced Šotiček for Hajduk. Reichmuth was booked in the 73rd minute for a foul on Del Moral.

Then came the miss of the night. In the 75th minute, Labeau broke down the right and squared the ball to Noah Christoffersson, who somehow put it wide of an empty net from close range.

García brought on Livaja and Dendoncker for Šego and Del Moral in the 78th minute, while Thun replaced Labeau and Roth with Braschi and Derbaci, and later Reichmuth with Lengen. Martin and Van Hoorenbeeck replaced Bamba and Fayad in the 84th minute. Livaja won a free kick two minutes later and then headed wide from the resulting cross.

Four minutes of stoppage time were added, and Hajduk nearly sealed it on the break in the 92nd minute, when Dalisson tried to lob from distance and hit the crossbar. Hajduk held on for a 1-0 win and a significant step towards the knockout phase of the Conference League.

World.title: Austrian Airlines is Scrapping Zagreb-Vienna Route After 40 Years
World.content:
October the 23rd, 2026 – Austrian Airlines is scrapping its direct Zagreb-Vienna route after 40 years, leaving the question of who will take on the Zagreb-Vienna route open.

Austrian Airlines will discontinue its long-standing route between Vienna and Zagreb next year. Index reports that the last flight between the two capitals is planned for the 10th of January 2027, and the Star Alliance member has confirmed that it will not reinstate the route even during the summer season of 2027.

“We can confirm that our flights between Vienna and Zagreb will, unfortunately, not continue during the summer season,” Austrian Airlines spokesperson Andrea Hansal told EX-YU Aviation News. With this, the carrier will leave Zagreb after more than four decades of operation. It introduced flights to the Croatian capital in the mid-1980s and interrupted services during the war and the COVID-19 pandemic.

the number of flights has already allegedly been reduced by austrian airlines

In recent years, Austrian Airlines has significantly reduced the number of flights operating on the Vienna–Zagreb route. The carrier previously operated up to 12 flights a week, but during the summer season of 2026 it reduced them to one daily flight. This represented a 37.5 percent reduction in the number of flights and a 27 percent reduction in available seat capacity compared with the previous year. The reduction in the number of flights during the winter began as early as the end of 2024, when the company thinned out departures and introduced smaller turboprop aircraft. At the same time, Croatia Airlines, also a Star Alliance member, expanded its offer on this route. During the summer of 2026 it doubled the number of flights to Vienna, to a total of ten per week.

Croatia Airlines will continue flying between Zagreb and Vienna during the upcoming winter season, which starts this Sunday, and will retain two daily flights, as it did last winter.

zagreb airport continues to expand its destination network and bring in new airlines

Austrian Airlines, on the other hand, will continue to operate daily flights until the route is discontinued in January. Many of them will be operated by aircraft of the company Air Dolomiti, which Austrian Airlines uses under a wet-lease agreement. All of this is happening at a time when Zagreb International Airport is trying to attract new carriers and expand its destination network. The airport is participating in the Routes World conference currently being held in Frankfurt. Zagreb Airport is represented there by President of the Management Board and CEO Huseyin Bahadır Bedir and Head of Route Development Yavuz Aytis.

World.title: NEC Stun Dinamo 4-2 at Maksimir in the Europa League
World.content:
Dinamo suffered their first European defeat of the season on Thursday night, losing 4-2 at Maksimir to NEC Nijmegen in the third round of the Europa League league phase. Dion Drena Beljo scored twice for the home side, but NEC captain Tjaronn Chery struck two of his own, with Clement Bischoff and Bryan Linssen also on target.

Dinamo went in as clear favorites. NEC arrived in Zagreb having gone two months without a win, and the stakes for the home side were high: according to Football Meets Data, a win would have given Dinamo roughly an 80 percent chance of a top-24 finish, while defeat would drop those odds below 50 per cent.

Lineups

Dinamo: Kotarski; Galešić, Domínguez, McKenna, Perez Vinlof; Stojković, Mišić, Ivanušec; Almena, Beljo, Hoxha

NEC: Crettaz; Storm, Schuurs, Fonville; Geiger, Nejašmić, Lebreton, Kaplan; Chery, Linssen, Bischoff

Match report

Dinamo had the better of the opening exchanges. Beljo forced the first save from Gonzalo Crettaz in the 3rd minute with a shot on his weaker right foot. Five minutes later, Schuurs cleared a Galešić cross just ahead of Stojković. Ivanušec went down in the box in the 17th minute, but the referee waved play on.

The home side went closest in the 20th minute. Almena slipped Stojković into space, and he lifted the ball over Crettaz, only for Kaplan to hook it off the line. Two minutes later, NEC produced their best effort to that point, as Lebreton’s long-range strike came back off the crossbar. Beljo was booked in the 24th minute.

Against the run of play, NEC went ahead in the 25th minute. Tobias Storm raced down the right and crossed for Bischoff at the far post, who took a touch, beat Galešić and scored.

Dinamo equalized in the 33rd minute. Stojković sent Perez Vinlof away on the left, and his cross to the far post was met by Beljo, who rose highest between two defenders to head in for 1-1. Ivanušec thought he had put Dinamo ahead two minutes later, but his goal was ruled offside. In the 37th minute, Stojković laid the ball off in a quick move for Beljo to finish from around ten meters and make it 2-1.

Lebreton was booked in the 44th minute for bringing down Beljo, and NEC equalized right on half-time. Bischoff broke down the left and delivered a difficult cross that Linssen met with a diving header for 2-2.

Neither side made changes at the break, and it was NEC who took control. By the 52nd minute, Dinamo were pinned inside their own final third, and two minutes later, the visitors went back in front. Darko Nejašmić played the ball forward to Linssen, who found Chery in the middle. The NEC captain applied just enough of a touch to beat Kotarski for 3-2.

Rodríguez replaced Almena in the 58th minute and quickly became Dinamo’s main outlet down the right. Stojković lobbed Crettaz on the counter in the 62nd minute but missed the target. Ivanušec went down in the box again two minutes later without reward, and Crettaz parried another Stojković effort in the 65th. Mario Kovačević turned to Oršić and Valinčić in the 67th minute, replacing Galešić and Hoxha.

NEC rode their luck in the 72nd minute. Rodríguez beat three players and set up Mišić, whose fierce shot from distance was saved by Crettaz, who then stopped Oršić’s follow-up. Three minutes later, Rodríguez cut inside and teed up Beljo, who could not convert from close range. Goda came on for Perez Vinlof in the 76th minute, with Monteiro replacing Geiger for NEC.

Chery settled it in the 80th minute, collecting a loose ball on the edge of the box and firing into the top corner for his second of the night. Crettaz denied Rodríguez after a counter in the 83rd minute and then saved an excellent Oršić free kick two minutes later, and NEC saw out four minutes of stoppage time to complete the win.

It was a first defeat in Europe this season for Dinamo and a first Europa League win for NEC. Dinamo travel to Sunderland on November 5 for their next league-phase match.

World.title: Croatian Government Gives 15,000 Unlicensed Apartments 4 More Years
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – The Croatian Government has given in on certain aspects of the Hospitality Activity Act, providing 15,000 unlicensed apartments 4 more years to operate.

The Croatian Government has now accepted the final proposal of the Hospitality Activity Act, which extends the validity of temporary decisions for around 15,000 landlords by an additional four years, the Ministry of Tourism and Sport announced. Index reports that these temporary decisions – on the basis of which apartments and rooms operate in buildings that do not have all the necessary papers, an occupancy permit, or are still waiting for the completion of the legalisation process – were due to expire at the end of this year. If the law had remained unchanged, thousands of landlords would have had to lock up, but with the new legislative proposal the Government has moved the deadline all the way to the 31st of December 2030.

protecting the livelihoods of family landlords

Tourism and Sport Minister Tonči Glavina said that this protects the livelihood of family landlords and ensures the continuity of their business so that they have enough time to legalise their properties and obtain permanent permits. “This is an important measure, especially when we take into account that at the end of 2024 around 15,000 landlords were operating on the basis of temporary decisions,” Glavina stated.

unique registration numbers as of 2027

In addition to extending the permits for legalisation, the law also brings novelties aimed at combating unregistered rentals. A unique registration number is being introduced for accommodation units advertised via online platforms such as Booking and Airbnb, but this provision will not enter into force immediately – only from the 1st of May 2027 so that the market has time to adapt. The state plans to establish direct data exchange with the platforms, which means that properties without a valid registration number would no longer be allowed to be advertised online. At the same time, county bodies are obliged to submit accurate data on the number of resolved cases and temporary decisions to the Ministry once a year, by the 30th of June.

higher penalties and closer inspections

The new legal framework also provides for higher misdemeanour fines for violations of the regulations, expanded powers for tourism and tax inspectors, and the digitisation of administrative procedures through the eTurizam system. Another novelty is that the rental of rooms and apartments in family houses will in future also be able to be registered through a craft or a limited liability company (d.o.o.), and not only in the status of a private landlord as has been the case until now. The bill has been sent to the parliamentary procedure for a second reading.

World.title: €3,000 Parking Fine Arrives a Year After Dubrovnik Trip – Poles Outraged
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – A €3,000 parking fine arrived at the addresses of tourists following their Dubrovnik trip an entire year later, and it’s safe to say they’re not happy…

Fines that some former visitors to Dubrovnik “earned” by parking their cars around the historic city centre are arriving months after they return from their holidays, and the case has attracted plenty of attention in the Polish media. Morski reports that one of the fined tourists contacted Croatia’s well known media outlet Index, claiming that because of two entries into the restricted zone he received two fines of €1,500 each, meaning the total sum amounted to €3,000.

“I’m writing to you on my own behalf and on behalf of many Polish tourists who, instead of returning with nice memories from a holiday in Croatia, specifically Dubrovnik, came back deeply disappointed by the greed and inhumane rules that apply in that city,” he wrote.

The Polish tourist claims that the fines reached him more than one year after his trip to Croatia. “Personally I received two separate fines of €1,500 each. In addition, the law firms hired by the city authorities don’t even reply to e-mails and it’s extremely difficult to communicate with them,” he stated. According to him, the problem has caused a lot of dissatisfaction among Polish tourists, and television stations and internet portals are reporting on it.

In addition, this particular Polish tourist complained that traffic signs warning about the entry restriction are in place, but he considers that it is nowhere near clear enough to tourists what they must do in order to be allowed to enter the zone by car, and that the fines are disproportionate to the offence. On the 2nd of June 2025, the City of Dubrovnik introduced a special traffic regime zone around the historic centre in order to reduce traffic congestion and protect the area that has been exposed to a large number of vehicles for years.

The City of Dubrovnik otherwise prescribed fines of €260 for natural persons, €660 for craftspersons and persons performing independent activities, and a significantly higher €1,320 for legal entities. The responsible person in a legal entity can be fined an additional €260.

World.title: Clocks need to be set back as Estonia switches to winter time this Sunday
World.content:
Estonia will switch to winter time in the early hours of Sunday, October 25, meaning clocks will be turned back one hour from 4 a.m. to 3 a.m.

By turning back the clocks and switching to winter time, Estonia will return to standard time.

All European Union member states will switch to winter time.

The Labor Inspectorate points out that while the fall clock change means an extra hour of sleep for many people, it could mean an additional hour of work for those working night shifts.

The clock change does not automatically extend agreed working hours. If an employee's regular shift lasts eight hours, they are not required to work nine hours simply because the clocks are turned back. Employers and employees must agree on any extension of a work shift. Without such an agreement, employees have the right to finish work after eight hours of actual work.

Every hour worked must be paid. If an employee works nine hours instead of the usual eight because of the clock change, they must be paid for all nine hours.

World.title: Lithuanian energy company's subsidiary mulls gas-fired power plant near Tartu
World.content:
The Estonian subsidiary of Lithuanian energy group Ignitis is making preparations to potentially build a gas-fired power plant with a capacity of up to 200 MW in Kastre Municipality, Tartu County.

Ignitis Estonia CEO Timo Tatar said the company's interest in building a gas-fired power plant with a capacity of up to 200 megawatts in Kastre Municipality stems from TSO Elering's plans to procure power generation capacity across Estonia to restart the electricity system in the event of a blackout.

"Under the terms of Elering's procurement for distributed system restoration capacity, such a plant must, first and foremost, be ready to start up and operate independently whenever Elering needs it to restart the system. At other times, the plant can also participate in other electricity markets and generate additional revenue," Tatar said.

Kastre Mayor Priit Lomp said Uniküla is technically well-suited for a power plant of this kind.

"There is a main gas transmission pipeline nearby, as well as a 330-kilovolt electricity transmission network. There are three potential locations in southern Estonia, stretching from Jõgeva County to southeastern Estonia. One is in Jõgeva Municipality, another in Tartu Municipality and the third in Kastre Municipality. There are no other locations in southern Estonia where such a project would be technically feasible," Lomp said.

Tatar also said Uniküla's proximity to Elering's natural gas network and its strong electricity grid connections made it an attractive location.

"Of course, it is difficult to say whether the natural gas supplied to the power plant would arrive via LNG tankers or from somewhere like Norway," Tatar said.

The company has submitted an application to Kastre Municipality to initiate a detailed spatial plan. However, Tatar stressed that its interest in developing the project does not constitute a final investment decision.

"At this stage, we are simply making preparations so that, if Elering's procurement terms prove attractive to us, we will be ready to submit a bid. It should also be noted that our interest is not limited to Kastre Municipality. We are also looking at suitable plots of land elsewhere, although it is too early to discuss those locations," Tatar said.

Elering said that, under its current plans, the procurement is expected to be announced toward the end of this year.

Lomp added that the municipality has not yet begun processing the detailed spatial plan application as Ignitis is not the only company interested in building a gas-fired power plant in the area. He said the municipality had first forwarded Ignitis' application to the state for review.

"We have sent Ignitis' proposed location to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications so that it can review all national mineral resource plans and other planning documents to see whether there is anything that, from the ministry's perspective, would rule out the project. The municipality does not want to waste time on unnecessary work. Under our municipality's comprehensive plan, the site is designated as valuable agricultural land. However, the plan also states that projects of significant public interest can be considered for development there and we believe electricity generation capacity is a matter of significant public interest," Lomp said.

The cost of building a gas-fired power plant with a capacity of up to 200 megawatts is estimated at around €200 million.

World.title: Center and Social Democrats overtake Isamaa in Emor poll
World.content:
In October, the Center Party topped Emor's party ratings with 20.6 percent support, followed by the Social Democratic Party with 20.4 percent.

Emor ratings Oct. 12–21, 2026. Source: Emor

Monthly changes in party ratings were substantial. Support for the Center Party rose by 3.7 percentage points compared with September, ending a three-month decline. Support for the Social Democratic Party (SDE) increased by 3.0 percentage points, reaching its highest level this year.

By contrast, support for Isamaa fell by 4.7 percentage points to 19.4 percent, the party's worst result in three years.

Emor research expert Aivar Voog said that, given the survey's margin of error, the ranking of the three parties could not be determined with certainty.

"The large changes over the past month may be temporary, so it is worth looking at the results of the coming months to assess whether the rise in support for the Center Party and SDE and the decline in support for Isamaa will persist," Voog said.

Isamaa lost support among younger age groups, while its position remained more stable among those aged 65 and older. SDE was already the most popular party among voters under 35 but also took the lead among those aged 35 to 49 in October.

The Reform Party and the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) ranked fourth and fifth, respectively, with virtually equal levels of support. In October, the Reform Party had 14.2 percent support, compared with 13.8 percent for EKRE.

Parempoolsed ranked sixth, with its support falling from 9.6 percent in September to 6.5 percent in October.

Support for all other parties remained below the electoral threshold. Eesti 200 had 1.5 percent support, trailing the Koos party, which had 1.7 percent. The Greens, which had considered merging with Eesti 200, had 0.8 percent support. The Estonian Nationalists and Conservatives party had 0.7 percent support.

The share of respondents with no party preference, or those who answered "don't know," fell from 30 percent in September to 27 percent in October. Combined support for the governing coalition remained at 16 percent, while total support for opposition parties rose from 71 percent to 74 percent.

When respondents with no party preference were also included, the Center Party had 15.5 percent support in October, followed by SDE with 15.4 percent, Isamaa with 13.3 percent, the Reform Party with 10.6 percent, EKRE with 8.7 percent and Parempoolsed with 5.0 percent.

SDE top choice for ethnic Estonian voters

Among ethnic Estonian respondents, SDE took the lead with 23.9 percent support, while Isamaa fell to second place with 23.2 percent. They were followed by the Reform Party with 16.6 percent, EKRE with 15.4 percent, the Center Party with 9.5 percent and Parempoolsed with 7.9 percent. Support for Eesti 200 among ethnic Estonian respondents stood at 1.9 percent.

Among respondents of other ethnic backgrounds, the Center Party led in October with 62.9 percent support. Support for all other parties in this group remained below 10 percent. The Koos party had 8 percent support, followed by EKRE with 7.9 percent and SDE with 7.2 percent.

Among voters in Tallinn, the Center Party led with 31.7 percent support, although SDE was not far behind with 26.3 percent. The Reform Party ranked third in the capital with 14.5 percent. Isamaa, which holds the mayor's office, had 10.5 percent support in Tallinn, compared with 7 percent for EKRE and 4.5 percent for Parempoolsed. The Center Party also led in Ida-Viru County with 46.3 percent support.

SDE remained the most popular choice among voters aged 18 to 24 and 25 to 34 and also took the lead among those aged 35 to 49 in October. Isamaa, which previously led in that age group, was now the most popular choice among voters aged 65 to 75 and those over 75. The Center Party led among voters aged 50 to 64.

Emor surveyed 1,487 voting-age citizens across Estonia online and by telephone from October 12 to 21. The maximum margin of error for a sample of this size is ±2.1 percentage points. More information about the party ratings is available on ERR's dedicated ratings page.

World.title: British influencer living in Estonia: My first sauna was a shock
World.content:
Shauna Soitu moved to Estonia two years ago, loves the country's nature, culture and outlook on life. Although learning Estonian's special characters proved quite a headache, she is determined to master the language.

Shauna Soitu, originally from the United Kingdom, moved to Estonia two years ago. Love brought her here.

"We met on vacation in Mexico. We were staying at the same hotel and we met in the swimming pool. The odds of us meeting were so small. I'm so grateful because now I live in Estonia and I have an amazing life here," Soitu told ETV's "Ringvaade."

Estonia was not entirely unfamiliar to her. For example, she knew that companies such as Skype and Bolt originated here. She had also visited Estonia a few times before moving.

"I fell in love with, not just Tallinn, but the countryside as well. We were going on hikes in the bogs. The peacefulness and the safety; everything I felt here, I just loved it. When we decided England or Estonia, I was like, 'Let's give Estonia a try.'"

Today, Soitu's observations about Estonia and Estonians have attracted tens of thousands of followers on social media. Her decision to start making videos about life in Estonia came about by chance when she wanted to share what she had learned in an Estonian language class on TikTok.

"I'd just learned fully how to introduce myself, say where I was from. I was so proud of myself! 'Oh my God, I need to tell everyone!' I was telling all my friends at work, too, like so excited. And I said I need to record this and send it to my mom and dad, like 'I can speak Estonian.' So I recorded it and said I'm just going to post this on TikTok as well. I didn't look at my phone for a while and it had just blown up on TikTok, which surprised me. So I decided to start documenting my journey," she said.

While the English enjoy making small talk even with strangers, Soitu has found that Estonians are rather different.

"The first time I went to work in Estonia and I was trying to talk to someone in the kitchen, they were so confused. They were like, 'Why is this girl talking to me? Why is she asking me what I've got for lunch? Why does she care?' I was a little taken back by that, but I'm used to it now. Now, I'm a little more reserved and protective of my time and energy, which I think is good," she said. "Also, I love being outdoors and I love the sauna. So I'd say I've been Estonianized."

Soitu still vividly remembers her first sauna experience. She was visiting the parents of her husband, Kert, in Rapla at the time. What stood out most was the traditional practice of vihtlemine or striking the skin with a bundle of leafy branches.

"I was like, 'what the hell is going on?!' I was blown away and I'd never had a sauna like it. But it was a cool experience," she said with a laugh.

A couple of months ago, Shauna and Kert held a big wedding celebration. That, too, came with plenty of surprises for Shauna and the other English guests. One particularly memorable experience was the traditional Estonian custom of "bride kidnapping," in which the groom must complete challenges to win back his bride.

"My husband was challenged to do some things. He had to change a doll's diaper and sing a song to get me back. The English [guests ] were just like, what is going on. It was crazy! But they loved it. I'm just getting such good feedback from everyone that came to Tallinn. They want to come back, they want to see more of Estonia. And they said it was the best wedding ever!"

There are still some things Soitu has not quite gotten used to, however, such as how much pork Estonians eat. She has yet to develop a taste for blood sausage, either.

"Maybe this year I will like it. I don't know? Apparently, it grows on you over time," Soitu said with a smile.

At home, Shauna and Kert speak a mixture of Estonian and English. Shauna believes it is important to learn at least some basic Estonian as a sign of respect.

"I want to have children and raise them here. They're going to speak Estonian. How silly that the mom doesn't understand her children. I'm definitely going to be putting full effort into being fluent in Estonian."

World.title: Education ministry to temporarily restrict access to Moodle platform
World.content:
The Ministry of Education and Research is implementing additional security measures starting Thursday in response to critical software vulnerabilities to ensure the security of the Moodle learning platform and the data processed within it.

The Moodle learning platform will be temporarily shut down starting Thursday until the necessary security updates have been installed and their effectiveness verified.

The ministry emphasized that ensuring the security of the learning platform and the data it contains is its top priority.

"The temporary shutdown of Moodle is a preventive measure aimed at avoiding potential data leaks, damage to the learning platform and resulting prolonged disruptions," the Ministry of Education and Research added.

The ministry said it understands that the temporary shutdown may cause inconvenience to users and is working with technical partners to implement the necessary security updates as quickly as possible.

Normal operations will resume once the necessary security updates have been installed and their effectiveness verified. A separate announcement will be made when Moodle reopens.

On Wednesday, the National Archives also announced that several of its online services had been temporarily shut down or restricted to users with Estonian IP addresses as a precautionary measure.

"Critical security vulnerabilities have been discovered in the widely used PHP web software. We are installing security patches and will restore services as soon as possible."

Moodle is an open-source Learning Management System (LMS) designed to create customizable online classrooms where educators can organize course content, host interactive assignments, run tests, and facilitate discussions. In Estonia's digital education ecosystem, Moodle serves as a core e-learning platform used extensively across vocational schools, general education institutions, and major universities such as the University of Tartu and TalTech.

World.title: Shorter-range HIMARS missiles arrive in Estonia
World.content:
Defense Minister Martin Herem confirmed to ERR that missiles with a range of 70 kilometers for the HIMARS rocket artillery system have arrived in Estonia.

Estonia has been waiting for some time for U.S.-supplied ammunition for its HIMARS multiple launch rocket systems.

Estonia ordered both ATACMS missiles with a range of up to 300 kilometers and GMLRS rockets with a range of approximately 70 kilometers.

However, the United States suspended ammunition deliveries in the spring due to the war in Iraq.

While deliveries of long-range ammunition remain on hold, the 70-kilometer-range rockets have arrived, Herem told Vikerraadio.

"Everything that was originally included in our contract is now in Estonia. The launchers for the Korean system (K239 Chunmoo) will arrive next year, while the ammunition will hopefully arrive next year as well, but more likely in early 2028," Herem said.

"In addition, we are expecting various types of ammunition both this year and next year with ranges well beyond 50 kilometers, approaching 100 kilometers. These include artillery ammunition as well as loitering munitions, which are large, winged drones," the defense minister added.

The Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) has six HIMARS (M142 High Mobility Artillery Rocket System) multiple launch rocket systems. In April, the Estonian Center for Defense Investments and U.S. defense contractor Lockheed Martin signed a contract to purchase three additional HIMARS launchers, which are expected to arrive in Estonia in 2027.

A HIMARS interchangeable rocket pod can carry either six GMLRS rockets with a range of 15 to 92 kilometers, two guided PrSM (Precision Strike Missile) missiles with a range of 60 to 499 kilometers or one guided ATACMS (Army Tactical Missile System) missile with a range of up to 300 kilometers.

World.title: Prime minister: We'll definitely work better with the Social Democrats under Vseviov
World.content:
Prime Minister and Reform Party Chairman Kristen Michal said his party would certainly have better cooperation with the Social Democratic Party if it were led by Jonatan Vseviov.

Jonatan Vseviov, the longtime secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and a security expert who has announced he is joining the Social Democrats, criticized the current government and Prime Minister Kristen Michal's leadership at a press conference Thursday, saying they lacked sharpness of mind, intellectual breadth and the courage to assert themselves.

Michal responded to Vseviov's criticism in broader terms.

"I think it's very good that Jonatan has entered politics. When I think about people who want to have a say and contribute, it's very good that they enter politics. It would be rather peculiar if people just wrote poetry and kept it in a drawer — not that there's anything wrong with that. Writing poetry and keeping it in a drawer is fine, too. But if you actually want to engage in politics, you have to do it in politics. So I certainly welcome Jonatan's arrival," Michal said at the government's press conference.

"And I'll add something on a personal note. I understand that he may have been given a few Social Democratic talking points. I think we'll certainly have better cooperation with the Social Democrats led by Jonatan Vseviov. I really do. So I'm genuinely pleased. I understand it might not seem logical for me to be happy about a political rival, but I actually am," Michal said.

SDE head Lauri Läänemets said at the Social Democratic Party's press conference that he would remain the party's leader. Michal's reference to the Social Democrats being led by Vseviov can therefore be interpreted as a jab at the party's current chairman.

"Second, I want to thank him for his work on foreign policy. We've done a great many things together. Some really impressive things. We've shared all the highs and lows of Estonian foreign policy and I want to thank him for that. We've carried that responsibility together," he added.

"And third, I understand that there's one recurring point in the Social Democrats' talking points, which I also noticed during Monday's confidence vote. They say Estonia's economy is on the wrong track. I heard something similar from that press conference, that Estonia's economy is supposedly heading for catastrophe or something along those lines. Well, it isn't. This year, Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the European Union average. I think that should be written in the corner at every press conference and we should say: Friends, let's start with that. I'm not just talking about the economy in general — Estonians' incomes have increased, precisely because of what we did with income tax reform: We eliminated the tax hump created by the progressive income tax system introduced by the Social Democrats, the Center Party and Isamaa," Michal said.

Michal added that the Reform Party and the Social Democrats would not find common ground on economic issues, but said cooperation was possible on foreign and security policy.

Both Lauri Läänemets and Vseviov said Estonia needs to do more to assert itself on the international stage and in various discussions concerning security. In their view, the country's current leadership has failed to achieve this.

"After all, we've all worked on foreign policy together. Jonatan, myself, Margus [Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna — ed.] and everyone else, including the presidents. If I look at the issues that matter to us, first of all, Russian assets have been permanently frozen since the end of last year. From our perspective, that's a very good result. Previously, we had to vote on extending the freeze every three or six months. Should our voice be heard? I think it has been. When it comes to the shadow fleet, we took the lead. I even remember criticism at home and I remember going to parliament where I think it was either EKRE or the Center Party trying to argue that we shouldn't be bothering these honest ships sailing to and from Russia. Why were we harassing them? They said the whole thing was suspicious and some even claimed we were about to trigger World War III. But then [French President] Emmanuel Macron came up to me and said they were doing the same thing and they also detained a ship that we had already detained. Then the Americans came along and said, 'Good, let's get to work.' I don't know, is that good or not? I think it is. I'm personally satisfied and I think it was the right thing to do," Michal said.

"Then there are Russian fighters. This is something we're all working on, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is working on, Jonatan has worked hard on it, Margus has worked on it, I've worked on it and I think many others have as well. The result is that European countries are seriously discussing, at the European Council summit I'm attending, how to put an end to Russians vacationing in Europe — the very same people who are killing women and children. We want to stop issuing them visas. Finland has joined us, Petteri Orpo [the Finnish prime minister — ed.] has made such a proposal and many other countries have come on board. I think the countries where Russians go on vacation are clearly moving in that direction as well," Michal said.

"I'm not sure how you would measure that. I also read an article by Lauri Läänemets, again featuring Social Democratic talking points, in which he said Kaja Kallas used to exchange messages with Macron. But here's a candid admission: I exchange messages with Macron more often than I do with Lauri Läänemets. It's actually quite funny," Michal added.

World.title: Gallery: Tallinn hosts 11 Ukrainian artists' work from international residency
World.content:
Three Tallinn locations are showing work by 11 Ukrainian photographers and visual artists, capping a recent international art residency held in Estonia, Finland and Germany.

The four-and-a-half-month "Waves of Creativity" project supported Ukrainian artists whose lives and work have been affected by Russia's war against Ukraine, including two who have spent time on the front.

Residencies took place in Saaremaa, Estonia, Joutsa, Finland and Stuttgart, Germany earlier this year.

The project's final exhibition opened in Tallinn on October 15, with displays at the Vabamu Museum of Occupations and Freedom, Okapi Gallery and the open-air Baltic Station Art Street.

The Tallinn show brings together documentary photography, experimental photo art, video and installations. While not all the works depict war directly, many explore personal experience, memory, home, everyday life, changing surroundings and people's relationships with the world around them.

Three ways to encounter the work

The three participating locations offer three different ways to encounter the work.

Okapi Gallery presents work developed during the residency in a traditional gallery setting, while a pop-up exhibition at Vabamu connects the artists' personal experiences with broader historical and social themes.

An outdoor display along the Art Street at Tallinn's Balti jaam, meanwhile, brings contemporary Ukrainian photography into public space, reaching audiences who may not typically visit galleries.

Curated by Temuri Hvingija and co-curator Andrii Mur, participating artists include Mykyta Bezus, Oxana Chorna, Iryna Klachek, Olia Koval, Herman Krieger, Ievgeniia Kupchan, Valentyn Kuzan, Oleh Pereverziev, Alina Prisich, Olesia Saienko and Elena Subach.

The exhibition runs at Okapi Gallery through November 20 and will remain on display at Baltic Station Art Street through March 30. 2027.
