World.title: Rooney calls United squad ‘selfish babies’ after Fernandes criticism
World.content:
Manchester – Manchester United great Wayne Rooney has labelled the current squad “babies” and “selfish” after a humiliating Champions League capitulation and post-match criticism by Bruno Fernandes of manager Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s men are 13th in the Premier League ahead of Sunday’s visit by Bournemouth and could drop into the bottom three if results go against them this weekend.

With the club beset by infighting and off to their worst domestic league start for decades, Carrick was left clinging to his job after the 4-1 defeat at Como on Wednesday.

Deepening the sense of crisis, the captain Fernandes afterwards took aim at his manager’s tactics, saying United had to be more “brave”.

Defender Lisandro Martinez last week criticised the club’s board for not investing enough in the transfer market.

Rooney, United’s all-time leading goalscorer, said he was in “shock” and “disbelief” at the Como display.

A friend and ex-teammate of Carrick, former striker Rooney pointed the finger at the players.

“When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart,” Rooney told The United Stand podcast on Thursday.

“That was the start. We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players because these players, they don’t want to take responsibility.

“You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players.”

He added: “These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

“If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.”

World.title: Japanese coffee brand % Arabica opens first Iraq branch in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Japanese specialty coffee brand % Arabica officially opens its first coffee branch in Iraq today, at Iraq Mall in Baghdad, marking the brand’s 249th location worldwide.

The new retail, situated on the mall’s ground level, has a unique architectural style inspired by Iraq’s ancient Mesopotamian civilization.

ARCHIEE, a Paris-based architectural company, designed the store with inspiration from the Ziggurat of Ur, including terraced brick terraces, tiered seating, and minimalist white interiors to create a contemporary coffee shop experience.

The design incorporates traditional brickwork, which reflects materials used in Mesopotamian construction for thousands of years, as well as modern lighting and open areas.

The inauguration follows a master franchise deal inked in early 2025 between % Arabica and Al-Handal International Group to bring the Japanese coffee brand to Iraq.

Further locations are planned, including a branch in Baghdad’s Downtown Al-Mutanabbi area and another in Erbil, as the company expands its presence in the Iraqi market.

World.title: China’s first AI film hits cinemas but ticket sales lag
World.content:
Beijing – China’s first fully AI-generated feature film opens in cinemas on Friday, in what promises to be a tough box-office test for the country’s booming tech industry as advance ticket sales lag.

More than 10,000 screenings of “Sanxingdui: Future Past”, a sci-fi thriller, are scheduled for Friday, according to ticketing platform Maoyan.

However, public reception has been less than enthusiastic.

Presale revenue as of Thursday evening stood at 65,000 yuan ($9,700), while total box-office takings were forecast to remain below 100,000 yuan, only a fraction of the reported production cost, according to Maoyan.

Jiang Defu, CEO of the production company Bona Film Group, acknowledged the lukewarm reception in a recent interview, but said the film was pushing boundaries.

“We are the first to try it, the first to get a theatrical release permit, and the first to be tested by the audience,” he told Chinese film industry outlet Yuli.

“I think that is not easy at all.”

Nearly 100 people took more than two years to make the film, which cost more than 10 million yuan ($1.5 million), Bona said.

But that was not enough to convince Iris Yang, who attended a free preview screening of the film on Thursday and said she would not have paid for a ticket, given the movie’s quality.

“If AI generation can match the theatrical experience of ‘Avatar’, I think I would be willing to pay for it,” Yang said, referring to the US franchise known for the quality of its animation.

AI-generated video has gained popularity in the world’s second-largest economy. On Douyin, the Chinese equivalent of TikTok, AI-generated short dramas garnered more than 200 billion views in September alone.

But “the audience won’t automatically pay for the tickets just because it’s an AI-generated film”, independent AI director Zhang Jun told AFP.

Online, Chinese social media users also seemed unconvinced by the launch of AI movies in cinemas.

“If it’s free to watch on streaming platforms, it could become legendary. But paying to watch? People are not going to accept it at this stage,” one user on Weibo commented.

In Hollywood, the rise of AI has sparked concern among film workers about the prospect of job losses.

An AI-generated sci-fi feature called “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” is scheduled for US release on December 4.

And a virtual Hollywood actor called Tilly Norwood, whose interviews have gone viral while fuelling job fears, is also set to star in an upcoming movie called “Misaligned”.

World.title: 76ers rally to stun Cavs in James’s first home game for Philadelphia
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Philadelphia 76ers erased a 29-point deficit to stun the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 on Thursday in NBA superstar LeBron James’s first home game since landing in Philly as a free agent.

Tyrese Maxey scored 32 points and Joel Embiid added 24 — including a jump shot with 6:54 left to play that gave the Sixers their first lead of the night — one they wouldn’t relinquish on the way to an epic comeback.

Former Celtics star Jaylen Brown, the Sixers’ other big off-season acquisition, scored 21 points and pulled down eight rebounds and four-time NBA champion James added 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists to help the 76ers author their biggest comeback of the play-by-play era that started in 1996.

It was also the biggest comeback of James’s storied career. The league’s all-time leading scorer called it a good win — but not a position he wants to be in often.

“You don’t want to rely on that,” he said. “I think it’s great to know (that) deep down we’re not going to have that quit mentality. You never want to look around and say guys gave up.

“But you don’t want to put yourself in too many of those situations.”

Cleveland, disappointed not to land hometown hero James after he announced he was leaving the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons, appeared to be on a mission to show him what he missed.

Donovan Mitchell scored 22 of his 32 points in the first half as the Cavs seized control against a 76ers team struggling to find a rhythm and protect the ball.

Philadelphia center Joel Embiid looked creaky, and James had five of the Sixers’ 15 first-half turnovers — which led to 22 Cavs points and provoked boos from Philly fans whose hopes of a title run have been raised by the arrivals of James and Brown.

The boos turned to raucous cheers as the re-energized 76ers opened the third quarter on an 11-0 run. They cut the lead to single digits on back-to-back baskets from Maxey that pulled them within 80-73.

The Cavs were struggling to regroup. Maxey reduced the deficit to two points with a running finger roll layup with 2:33 left in the third before Cleveland reeled off six straight points to take a 90-82 lead into the fourth quarter.

But the 76ers, who beat the reigning champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday, kept coming. They out-scored the Cavaliers 60-37 in the second half, clamping down defensively and giving up just two turnovers.

Evan Mobley scored 18 points for Cleveland but had just three in the second half Jarrett Allen scored 14 but was held scoreless after the break.

“We stayed together, that’s the main thing,” Sixers guard VJ Edgecomebe said. “When it got worse we could have given up, we didn’t. It’s an early season test, early season adversity, and we overcame it.”

World.title: Asian stocks head into weekend on a low as tech extends losses
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks sank again Friday as tech firms took another beating from investors increasingly losing faith in the sector, with the traditional safe haven yen and government bonds benefiting from the risk-off mood.

Since AI-linked companies hit record highs in June, their equity prices have been pummelled by concerns they were overvalued, their huge outlays on infrastructure and hardware might not return a profit and, more recently, their servicing costs were spiralling.

That has combined with an Iran war-fuelled surge in oil prices to more than $100 that has ramped up inflation, forced central banks to hike interest rates and sent government borrowing costs to multi-decade highs.

Strong earnings in past quarters have been able to temper many of the concerns, but analysts pointed out that investors are demanding better and better results to justify their backing.

Earnings from Facebook-parent Meta and chip equipment maker Lam Research this week have beaten forecasts but seen their shares dive.

“Even positive news is being ignored,” said FOREX.com’s Fawad Razaqzada.

“Strong results are no longer enough if the outlook fails to match an already demanding valuation. Investors are becoming much less forgiving.”

The rush out of tech has, however, boosted industrial companies overlooked for much of the AI boom, with the Dow rising this week while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 retreated.

The general losses in New York have filtered through to Asia.

Seoul — which was at the forefront of the AI boom and is now leading losses — shed more than two percent Friday, at the end of a tough week for the Kospi index.

Chipmaker and market heavyweight SK hynix’s US shares fell more than eight percent after it said it was scrapping plans for an initial public offering for its US subsidiary Solidigm, citing “market conditions and share price trends”.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225, which is also heavily weighted to tech, was sharply lower along with Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington, Jakarta and Manila.

Taipei was closed as Typhoon Champi neared the island.

However, safe-havens benefitted, with the yen rallying against the dollar, helped by strong Japanese inflation data that boosted bets on another interest rate hike.

The currency has struggled against the greenback in recent years owing to the wide interest rate gap between the United States and Japan, as well as worries about the Asian giant’s fiscal situation.

US Treasuries were also in demand, with yields falling from two-decade highs.

“Markets are looking for safe havens as the now familiar fears over AI and the tech sector, alongside ever higher oil and energy prices are powering a move back into bonds,” said National Australia Bank’s Gavin Friend.

“Regardless of the continued climb in oil prices, investors are increasingly looking for safe havens with the recent pullback in US Treasury yields getting a sizeable push,” he said, adding that two- and 10-year Treasury yields were at one-month lows.

And Carol Kong at Commonwealth Bank of Australia said the yen could benefit further if the tech trade continued to deteriorate.

Oil prices added to the dour mood, with Brent heading back towards $115 a barrel for the first time since May on fresh Middle East worries.

It came after Iran threatened to hit US bases in the region if its military continued to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Trump slams NBA’s LeBron James for national anthem actions
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump lashed out at NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behavior during the playing of the national anthem.

Trump posted a video of the basketball legend doing apparent warm-up movements while lined-up with his Philadelphia 76ers teammates.

“While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social network.

“LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” he wrote.

The video used by Trump had an internal caption that read: “LeBron working on his golf swing pregame.” It showed him doing lateral swing motions and basketball shooting movements.

It was not immediately clear when the video was filmed.

There was no immediate reaction from James, 41, who is entering a record-extending 24th NBA season with his fourth team, or the 76ers.

Trump has been critical of athletes before — particularly Black athletes — for their behavior during the playing of the US national anthem before games.

During his first term, Trump singled out NFL star Colin Kaepernick for his decision to kneel during the “Star-Spangled Banner” to protest at racial injustice and police brutality.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate against Iraqi dinar remains stable in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar remained stable on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and declined in the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate remained stable in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,695 Iraqi dinars throughout the day.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,700 Iraqi dinars and 1,690 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate slightly declined, fluctuating between 1,694 and 1,693 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following a cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Gulf Keystone says Iraq’s Hamrin oilfield has 7 billion barrels of oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – CEO of Gulf Keystone Petroleum Jon Harris said on Wednesday that the firm believes that Iraq’s Hamrin oilfield has seven billion barrels of oil, of which 0.5 billion to one billion barrels are recoverable.

Harris told Reuters that the oilfield currently produces 20,000 barrels per day, and by the end of 2028, output is expected to reach 60,000 barrels per day.

This week, Gulf Keystone Petroleum and ShaMaran Petroleum have reached a merger agreement, becoming one of the top private oil producers in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to a statement from the corporation, the all-share acquisition is worth $601 million.

As of October 19, shareholders of ShaMaran, who are listed on Euronext, will receive 0.075 shares of Gulf Keystone for each share of ShaMaran they own, reflecting a premium of 23 percent.

The agreement integrates operations in the four Iraqi fields of Hamrin, Sarsang, Atrush, and Shaikan.

If drilling begins next year, the Shaikan oilfield in Iraqi Kurdistan is likely to increase its gross output from around 45,000 bpd to over 90,000 bpd by 2030, according to Harris.

Harris anticipates that the corporation will take advantage of other possibilities in Iraq, such as stake sales on US assets in the country.

World.title: 'Can't drive into future looking at rearview mirror': India calls for urgent UNSC reforms
World.content:
India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish

India has called for urgent reforms to the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), warning that its 80-year-old structure is struggling to address some of the worldâs gravest conflicts. New Delhi said the Councilâs composition must reflect present-day global realities, arguing that its post-Second World War framework no longer adequately represents the international community.According to news agency PTI, Indiaâs Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, said on Thursday that the authority inherited from the Second World War could no longer compensate for the Councilâs lack of representative membership.âThe cost is already visible. Eighty years on, the Organisation is struggling to deliver peace and reconciliation in some of the gravest conflicts before the Council,â Parvathaneni said while addressing the UN General Assembly on equitable representation and an expansion of the Security Council.He added that âthe authority derived from a victory eight decades ago cannot compensate for the deficit in legitimacy of an unrepresentative Security Council today.âThe Indian envoy argued that 1945, when the UN was established after the Second World War, could not remain the sole reference point for global governance.âNo war, especially one that took place over 80 years ago, should determine todayâs state of the world,â he said.âHistory can be a guide for what not to do. It cannot determine todayâs choices for what needs to be done to face contemporary challenges. We cannot reasonably drive into the future by constantly looking at the rearview mirror,â he added.Parvathaneni also highlighted Indiaâs contribution to the World Wars, arguing that the sacrifices of several nations had not received adequate recognition in the post-war international order.âAn organisation crafted of the victors, for the victors and by the victors did not, obviously, care to include the concerns of the victims,â he said, calling for the Security Council to evolve âfor the sake of its own relevanceâ.According to PTI, he noted that around 2.5 million Indians participated in the Second World War, with approximately 90,000 dying in military service. He also referred to the Bengal famine, which he attributed to colonial wartime policies.India further pointed to the under-representation of Asia-Pacific, Africa and Latin America. The Asia-Pacific region accounts for more than 60 per cent of the worldâs population but has only one permanent seat on the Council, alongside a fluctuating elected representation.âReform is not the settlement of old scores. It is an investment in a Council that all Member States can trust, and which would be stronger as a result,â Parvathaneni said.The 15-member UNSC comprises five permanent members â China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States â with veto powers, alongside 10 elected members serving two-year terms.India supports expanding both permanent and non-permanent membership, arguing that changes limited to elected seats would leave the central imbalance intact.Criticising the pace of negotiations, Parvathaneni said, âThat is not negotiation; it is merely perpetuation of status quo.âHe added, âConvergences are not consensus, and the search for a lowest common denominator must not become an excuse for cosmetically tinkering with the existing structure while calling it reform.âIndia also maintained that any permanent membership expansion must address the veto question fairly. âA two-tier permanent membership would only institutionalise inequality,â he said.

World.title: 'Shaurya commandos' prepared: ITBP chief flags ‘ongoing’ China faceoff along Arunachal border
World.content:
The

(ITBP) has raised a new combat unit, the Shaurya commandos, who have demonstrated their capabilities during the âongoingâ faceoff with Chinese Peopleâs Liberation Army (PLA) troops at multiple locations in Arunachal Pradesh, ITBP chief Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor said on Thursday.

Kapoor said the commandos would be deployed in every border battalion as the force strengthens its combat readiness along the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China. The ITBP chiefâs remarks came as the force steps up its modernisation drive, with a greater focus on emerging warfare technologies and specialised training.

Addressing personnel at an ITBP base in Alwar, Rajasthan, ahead of the forceâs 65th Raising Day on October 24, Kapoor said traditional methods of warfare were no longer sufficient to counter China, which he described as Indiaâs âbiggest adversaryâ.

The force has raised drone platoons in all its border-guarding battalions and is training personnel to operate drones and develop the technology. Kapoor said the ITBP had received Rs 400 crore in government funding, with 70% earmarked for strengthening its drone warfare capabilities. The Ministry of Home Affairs has also given in-principle approval to a Rs 4,000-crore modernisation plan, including Rs 1,000 crore for drone and anti-drone systems.





The ITBP has also developed a new âStrikeâ course to prepare personnel for combat situations similar to the June 2020 Galwan Valley clash. Kapoor said the entire force would undergo the training by the end of 2027.

During the Galwan clash in eastern Ladakh, 20 Indian soldiers were killed in a violent confrontation with Chinese troops. China later acknowledged the deaths of four of its soldiers.

Beyond combat training and technology, the force is also strengthening infrastructure at forward locations.

Kapoor said the ITBP was building underground shelters in border areas to reduce vulnerabilities in the event of a conflict, as above-ground structures could become targets during a war.

The force is also upgrading troop facilities in high-altitude areas, including insulating barracks, installing solar water heaters and providing generator sets to ensure electricity at remote posts. It has introduced cold-start kits to help vehicles start in freezing conditions.

Kapoor said these measures were part of a broader plan to develop the ITBP into a specialised high-altitude mountain-fighting force capable of responding to evolving security challenges along the China border.

World.title: Sudan’s RSF fighters deliberately targeted atleast 43 hospitals during el-Fasher siege: Report

A recent BBC investigation has uncovered alarming evidence of the RSF's assault on numerous healthcare facilities in el-Fasher, Sudan.

A BBC investigation has uncovered evidence suggesting that Sudanâs paramilitary rapid support forces (RSF) systematically targeted and dismantled healthcare facilities in el-Fasher during a prolonged siege and the subsequent capture of the Darfur city a year ago.UN high commissioner for human rights Volker TÃ¼rk described the findings as âdeeply disturbingâ. He said repeated RSF attacks on civilian infrastructure, including medical facilities, constituted serious violations of international humanitarian law and could amount to war crimes.The RSF has rejected the allegations. The groupâs health minister dismissed the findings as propaganda, alleging that Sudanâs national army and its allies were attempting to damage the paramilitary forceâs reputation.Drawing on accounts from people who were present in el-fasher, the BBC identified details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and other healthcare facilities between May 2024 and October 2025. Some sites were reportedly struck multiple times.International law prohibits attacks on medical facilities and healthcare workers during armed conflicts.Medical workers killed, injured or abductedThe investigation also documents the impact of the conflict on medical personnel in the western Sudanese city.According to the BBCâs data, 120 healthcare workers were injured, 55 were killed and 10 were forcibly disappeared or abducted between April 2023 and October 2025.Dr Muhamed Suliman, a surgeon who worked in el-fasher during the siege, told the BBC that the RSF sought to force hospitals out of operation.âThe RSF [were] trying to evacuate the hospitals, to put them out of service because the health system is the cornerstone of any city or any state,â he said.Suliman alleged that attacks were intended to make it impossible for civilians to remain in the affected areas, describing the campaign as intense, deliberate and planned.El-Fasher siege marked a brutal phase of Sudanâs warThe investigation was published a year after the fall of el-fasher, one of the most devastating episodes in Sudanâs civil war, which erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and the countryâs military.Both sides have faced accusations of attacking healthcare facilities.In March 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) condemned a bombing at al-Daein hospital in eastern Darfur, an area controlled by the RSF. The attack killed dozens of people and forced the facility to close. Sudanâs military was believed to have carried out the drone strikes, but it denied responsibility.Responding to a BBC inquiry, the WHO described the events in el-fasher as âone of the clearest and most severe examples of the wider impact of the conflict on health care in Sudanâ.UN investigators have also said the violence in el-fasher bore the âhallmarks of genocideâ. The cityâs population includes non-Arab communities that have faced attacks amid longstanding ethnic tensions, with Arab militias now forming the backbone of the RSF.The BBC investigation provides a detailed chronology of attacks on healthcare facilities during the prolonged siege, shedding further light on the conflictâs impact on medical services and civilians.

World.title: 2 Election Commissioners complained against poll panel officer, but Cabinet Secretariat took no action: RTI
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cabinet Secretariat did not take any action on complaints filed by two election commissioners against an officer in the Election Commission, saying the letters were written in their âindividual capacityâ and did not represent the poll panel as a whole, according to documents released in response to an RTI application.

Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and

had separately written to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29, raising concerns about the conduct of senior deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg, an IAS officer appointed to the Commission by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) on September 2, 2024.

The letters were provided in an RTI response to activist Commodore Lokesh K Batra (retd).

The Indian Express had reported in September that the two Election Commissioners approached the Cabinet Secretary after Garg issued a work allocation order that they believed could concentrate powers over changes to voter records at the central level, instead of allowing officials at the state level to handle them.

In a statement on September 26, the Election Commission said the work allocation orders issued by Garg were never implemented following directions from the two Commissioners.

The poll panel also said the complaints concerned an officer on deputation and not matters related to policy or the IT division.

What did the Election Commissioners allege

According to a Cabinet note included in the RTI response, both Commissioners alleged that Garg had issued an order changing the work allocation of officers senior or equivalent to him after taking charge as the link officer of the deputy election commissioner (Administration).





The Commissioners said the changes were made without consulting the Commission or the officers concerned. They also alleged that Garg acted despite repeated oral and written instructions against making such changes without prior discussion or approval from the Commission.

"Both the ECs have stated that Shri Garg, after assuming the charge as link officer of DEC (Admn), has issued an order regarding work allocation of equivalent and senior officers to him without discussing the revised work allocation with the Commission or the officers concerned.

Further, the aforementioned ECs have stated that this has happened despite repeated oral and written instructions to all concerned officers against taking such actions without prior discussion/approval of the Commission," the Cabinet note said.

The two Commissioners alleged that Garg's actions violated the chief election commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

Joshi also said that when he sought the relevant file from the Administration Division, it was not provided to him.

Why did the Cabinet Secretariat refrain from taking action

A Cabinet note prepared on August 3 proposed seeking the chief election commissioner's opinion on the complaints.

"In this connection, we may request the chief election commissioner for his opinion on the issue. Accordingly, a draft DO is put up for approval, please."

However, a subsequent note dated August 4 said taking action on complaints from individual Election Commissioners without an official communication from the Commission as a whole could be seen as interference in the functioning of the constitutional body.

"The Commission is a Constitutional Body and is insulated from executive interference by design to ensure that it functions independently and in a transparent manner. The working and functioning of the Commission are governed by the rules and guidelines of the Election Commission. The above communications are from the Election Commissioners in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the Commission as a whole," the note said.

It added that although Garg had been appointed by the ACC, he was now an officer of the Election Commission, and his work and conduct were governed by the poll panel's rules and guidelines.

The note also referred to Section 18 of the 2023 Act, which states that the Commission should conduct its business unanimously as far as possible, with any differences of opinion settled by a majority decision.

"Election Commissioners have sent these communications for appropriate action; however, in the absence of any official communication from the Commission as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate.

It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the Constitutional Body. Hence, it would be appropriate to send acknowledgement to both Election Commissioners with a copy to PPS to CEC for information of CEC," the note said.

The draft note signed by Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan was also marked to the secretary of the department of personnel and training and the establishment officer to keep the matter on record.

Somanathan also signed an acknowledgement letter confirming receipt of the complaints and sent copies to both election commissioners.

The letters were acknowledged on August 5, 2026, with copies marked to the department of personnel and training, the Establishment Officer and the office of the chief election commissioner.

World.title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
World.content:
PM Modi with Polish counterpart Donald Tusk at Hyderabad House Thursday.

NEW DELHI: Looking to further expand their strategic partnership, India and Poland agreed to double bilateral trade by 2030 and announced dialogue mechanisms for defence industrial collaboration and counterterrorism cooperation as PM Narendra Modi hosted his counterpart Donald Tusk for talks Thursday.Modi and Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.Poland views the war in Ukraine as a direct threat to its national security and sovereignty due to its shared border, influx of refugees and the threat of future Russian aggression in eastern Europe.âThey reiterated the need for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in line with international law, consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity,â said the joint statement. The leaders also noted the negative impacts of the war on global food and energy security, especially for the Global South.Modi and Tusk, the first Polish PM to visit India in 16 years, also backed an MoU under negotiation for cooperation in critical minerals.Modi said the friendship between India and Poland was based not only on diplomatic ties but also on a shared heritage of humanity and empathy. He recalled how, during the Second World War, the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter in India to thousands of Polish children and families. He also thanked Poland for helping India evacuate Indian students from Ukraine shortly after the Russia-Ukraine war began in 2022.Modi said the world was passing through a period of uncertainty and change, and even in such times, both India and Poland were emerging as important hubs of growth, technology and innovation.âToday we have agreed to deepen ties in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India,â he said.He also announced a startup bridge to facilitate cooperation in IT, Artificial Intelligence and critical technologies.âBoth India and Poland believe in democratic values and the rule of law,â Modi said, underlining that both sides considered reforms essential to make global governance institutions more empowered.The two countries agreed that the UN needed structural reforms, including expansion of UNSC in both permanent and non-permanent categories, to remain relevant, credible and effective. In the joint statement, Poland expressed support for Indiaâs membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC, as well as its candidature for a non-permanent seat on the council for 2028-29.Modi and Tusk unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, and stressed that there could be no justification for terrorism on any grounds.âThey condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in J&Kâs Pahalgam on 22 April, 2025. They called for strong and concerted action against terrorists and terrorist entities, including those designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee,â said the joint statement.Defence and security cooperation was a major focus, with the leaders underlining importance of an Agreement on Mutual Protection and Exchange of Classified Information and expressing expectation it would be signed soon.They proposed a defence industry dialogue to develop a âforward-looking framework for defence industrial cooperationâ, including business-to-business engagement and, where mutually agreed, partnerships in technology, co-development, co-production and other forms of collaboration.

World.title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
World.content:
The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds using Indian numbers

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has made SIM binding mandatory from Jan 1, 2027, and the move will mean that messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram will not work without a SIM card in the smartphone. The department of telecom has issued guidelines requiring messaging platforms to integrate the accounts with live SIMs used for registration by Dec 31, 2026. If the SIM is removed, replaced or deactivated, the appâs functionality will stop until a valid SIM is reinserted.The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.From Jan 1, messaging services to be used will have to ensure a registered SIM card is installed in a device. This is likely to impact users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without registered SIMs. And also those who use more than one device or frequently change their SIM cards.Last Nov, DoT had issued the rules after finding âthat some app-based communication services utilising Indian mobile numbers for identification of its customers allows users to consume their services without availability of the underlying subscriber identity module (SIM) within the device in which app-based communication services is running. This feature is being misused to commit cyber-frauds especially from outside the country,â a statement read.To curb this menace, many govt agencies had been asking for SIM binding to be made mandatory. Subsequently, DoT issued directions to major app-based communication services, under the Telecom Cyber Security (TCS) Rules, 2024. These include WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Arattai, Sharechat, Jiochat and Signal.Now, app-based communication providers will have to ensure that their service is âcontinuously linked to the SIM card (associated with mobile number used for identification of customers/users or for provisioning or delivery of services) installed in the device, making it impossible to use the app without that specific, active SIM.â And also ensure that âweb service instance of the mobile app, if provided, shall be logged out periodically (not later than six hours) and allowing the facility to the user to re-link the device using QR code. â

World.title: Voting in first phase of panchayat polls concludes in Rajasthan
World.content:
Polling for the first phase of Panchayati Raj elections in Rajasthan concluded on Thursday (October 23, 2026), even though some villages boycotted the polls over local issues.

Long queues were seen at polling stations across villages in the state as voter turnout was recorded at 63%, according to election officials.

The panchayat elections being held a month after the urban local body polls are being seen as another important test of strength for the ruling BJP and the Opposition Congress ahead of the Assembly elections due towards the end of 2028.

Thousands exercised their franchise for the panchayat polls, with both parties seeking to consolidate their support at the grassroots level and demonstrate their organisational strength in rural Rajasthan.

Polling began at 7 a.m. across 16 districts to elect members of 16 zila parishads and 104 panchayat samitis.

The overall voter turnout stood at 63% till 6 p.m., the officials said. The final polling percentage is yet to be declared.

Among the districts, Jhalawar recorded 69.16% polling, followed by Jaipur at 68.29%, Phalodi at 67.26%, Nagaur at 66.79% and Kota at 64.90%.

While voters turned out in large numbers at several places, polling was boycotted in some villages over grievances related to administrative boundaries and local issues.

In Kota district’s Itawa area, residents of Chaktodi-Todikhedli village under Sinota gram panchayat stayed away from voting, protesting the inclusion of their village under a gram panchayat located about 11 km away.

Krishna Meena, a resident, said the village was earlier part of the Dhipri Chambal gram panchayat but had been shifted to Sinota, causing inconvenience, particularly to elderly residents.

In Pali district, villagers boycotted polling in Duthariya village under Rani panchayat samiti and Nepawas village under Sojat panchayat samiti.

Voting was also boycotted at a booth in ward number 3 of Sojat panchayat samiti and Khirja Mangal Singh Nagar in Jodhpur district.

In Rajsamand district, polling was briefly disrupted in Keshuli under Nathdwara following a technical snag in an electronic voting machine (EVM). Officials replaced the faulty machine and voting resumed around 8 a.m.

More than 85 lakh voters were eligible to elect representatives to 293 zila parishad wards and 1,788 panchayat samiti wards in the first phase.

A total of 6,976 candidates are contesting 2,081 seats, including 1,693 candidates for zila parishad seats and 5,283 for panchayat samiti seats.

The first phase covers Ajmer, Alwar, Barmer, Bhilwara, Bikaner, Dungarpur, Jaipur, Jhalawar, Jodhpur, Kota, Nagaur, Pali, Phalodi, Rajsamand, Sirohi and Udaipur districts.

Among the zila parishads, Bhilwara has the highest number of wards at 28, followed by Udaipur with 25, Barmer with 24 and Jaipur with 22.

Jaipur has the highest number of candidates for zila parishad seats at 154, followed by Bikaner with 138 and Alwar and Jodhpur with 133 each.

In the panchayat samiti elections, Nagaur has the highest number of candidates at 470, followed by Barmer with 467 and Bhilwara with 466.

The Panchayati Raj elections are being conducted in three phases for 41 zila parishads and 457 panchayat samitis, besides elections for panches and sarpanches in 14,403 gram panchayats.

Polling for zila parishad and panchayat samiti members in the second phase will be held on October 28, followed by the third phase on November 3.

Elections for panches and sarpanches are scheduled for November 5, while indirect elections for up-sarpanches (deputy sarpanches) will take place on November 6.

World.title: Traffic restrictions around Hyderabad’s Hussain Sagar to remain in place till Saturday as Durga idol immersions continue
World.content:
With Durga idol immersion processions entering their final stretch, over 3,000 idols have been immersed across Hyderabad and its neighbouring police commissionerates, while hundreds more are scheduled to be taken to water bodies on Friday (October 23, 2026).

The immersion processions have also necessitated traffic arrangements around Hussain Sagar, where the Hyderabad Traffic Police announced restrictions from 3 p.m. on October 21 until 6 a.m. on October 24.

In Hyderabad, 1,625 idols were immersed as of Thursday (October 22, 2026). The immersion activities also gathered momentum in the Cyberabad, Malkajgiri and Future City Commissionerates, with October 21 witnessing particularly heavy movement of idols towards designated water bodies.

The Malkajgiri Police Commissionerate recorded 1,295 immersions at water bodies within its jurisdiction between October 20 and 8 p.m. on October 22. However, this included 510 idols brought from other commissionerates, while 785 belonged to Malkajgiri, where 1,074 idols were installed this year, excluding another 20 under the Abdullapurmet Police Station limits.

Of the locally installed idols, 96 were immersed on October 20, followed by a sharp increase to 646 on October 21. Another 43 were immersed by 8 p.m. on Thursday, leaving 289 idols awaiting immersion.

A similar increase was recorded in Cyberabad, where 791 idols were installed for the festivities. Immersions began with just one idol on October 18, followed by six on October 19 and 76 on October 20. The number surged to 482 on October 21, making it the busiest day recorded so far in the commissionerate. Another 141 idols were scheduled for immersion on Thursday, while 85 remained pending for Friday. If Thursday’s scheduled immersions were completed, Cyberabad would have accounted for 706 immersions.

In the Future City Police Commissionerate, 474 of the 517 installed idols WERE immersed by Thursday, leaving 43 pending.

Traffic diversions are being implemented on a need basis around People’s Plaza, Garden Point, Jalavihar and Sanjeevaiah Park, which are among the locations affected by the movement of immersion processions.

Motorists travelling through the Tank Bund and Necklace Road corridors may also encounter diversions at V.V. Statue, Nirankari Junction, Old Police Station Saifabad, Ravindra Bharathi and Masab Tank, depending on the movement of processions and traffic conditions.

The restrictions are intended to facilitate the movement of vehicles carrying idols towards immersion points while regulating regular traffic on roads surrounding Hussain Sagar.

The numbers also highlight the movement of idols across police commissionerate boundaries. In Malkajgiri alone, nearly 40% of the 1,295 immersions recorded at water bodies within its limits involved idols brought from other jurisdictions.

Across Cyberabad, Malkajgiri and Future City, 417 locally installed idols were either pending immersion or scheduled for Friday as per the latest available figures, while the final count for Hyderabad was yet to be updated.

With immersion activities continuing through Friday, the traffic restrictions around Hussain Sagar are scheduled to remain in place until 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 24, 2026).

World.title: Fire at Parawada pharma unit’s metformin block; all workers evacuated safely
World.content:
A minor fire incident was reported at the production block of Aurobindo Unit-15 in the early hours of Friday (October 23, 2026) in Parawada mandal of Anakapalli district. All personnel working inside the block were evacuated safely, and no casualties were reported, the police said.

According to Parawada Inspector L. Bhaskar, the incident occurred in the production block of the pharma unit, where metformin is manufactured. A tablet compression machine was being cleaned using isopropyl alcohol. A static electricity discharge is suspected to have triggered the initial ignition, which was followed by the spread of smoke inside the production block. But the exact cause of the incident has not yet been officially confirmed. The circumstances surrounding the incident are under investigation.

The personnel engaged in the cleaning operation, along with other employees working in the block, evacuated the premises safely. Fire tenders reached the scene and doused the fire.

Personnel from the Factories Department from Anakapalli visited the site to assess the situation and examine the circumstances that led to the incident.

The authorities are investigating the causes of the fire and gathering information. Further details are awaited.

World.title: BRS demands announcement of drought mandals, immediate relief measures
World.content:
The drought conditions in the State were not due to nature’s impact but due to the failures of the Congress Government and the Chief Minister was in a deep slumber even when standing crops in 12 lakh acres were withering, former minister and Deputy Floor Leader of the BRS Legislature Party T. Harish Rao alleged.

Speaking after examining the withered crops, mostly paddy, at Burugupalli of Gajwel mandal in Siddipet district on Thursday, he said the previous BRS Government had provided a helping hand to the farming community during the Covid-19 pandemic and achieve one-crore tonnes of paddy production, the Revanth Reddy Government had announced crop holiday in the name of El Nino impact.

Despite the forecast and warnings given by Met scientists on the El Nino impact 10 months in advance, the State Government had failed to maintain sufficient coal stocks at the thermal power stations and also failed to procure energy in advance. Now, the Chief Minister was washing his hands by stating that there was no energy in the market for procurement, though the government was ready to purchase it at any cost.

Mr. Harish Rao faulted the government for its failure to switch on/run the motors 24x7 at Kannepally, Devadula and Kalwakurthy lifts to ensure sufficient water for irrigation and drinking needs.

He mentioned that neighbouring Maharashtra Government had released ₹5,000 per acre immediate relief to farmers and Andhra Pradesh had declared drought mandals. But, the Telangana Government had not even declared drought mandals.

Criticising the government for burdening people with ₹5,420 crore of energy charges in the form of true-up charges, the BRS leader demanded that the government announce drought mandals immediately and extend ₹12,000 per farm worker, as promised in the Congress election manifesto.

World.title: Pakistan refused to accept bodies of its own soldiers killed in Kargil war: India at UN
World.content:
India slammed Pakistan at the UN, reminding the country that it did not even accept the bodies of its own soldiers killed in combat in the 1999 Kargil war but speaks about faith, religious freedom and burials.

The interim report of the Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion and belief, Nazila Ghanea, said that "Reports of systemic denial of funeral rights in the context of individuals killed in security operations in Jammu and Kashmir, India, including denial of return of bodies to families and remote and secret burials, disproportionately affecting Muslims and notably inconsistent with their practices, raise serious concerns.”

"It is deeply ironic that a State that did not even accept the bodies of its own soldiers who were killed in combat in 1999 in Kargil unabashedly speaks with fervour on faith, religious freedom, and burials,” First Secretary at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Bhavika Mangalanandan said at the United Nations on Thursday (October 22, 2026), a strong reference to Pakistan.

Indian Army recovered bodies of Pakistani soldiers who died in the Kargil War and provided them with burials after Pakistan refused to acknowledge the involvement of Pakistan Army personnel in the war.

Addressing the interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion and belief on the topic of funeral rights in exceptional circumstances, Ms. Mangalanandan reminded Pakistan that it was the Indian Army that buried several Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic rights.

“Pakistan's deep obsession with what is happening in the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir should be actually directed at the developments that are underway in the parts of Jammu and Kashmir under its illegal occupation, such as Rawalakot,” she said, adding that in Pakistan, a number of minorities are shrinking; their rights regularly abused.

“A State that cannot ensure the safety of its own minorities has no standing to lecture India,” she said.

Ms. Mangalanandan added that burial rights for terrorists are being justified by indicating that States may restrict funeral rights of terrorists, but only within legal limits.

“Legal limits should be determined in accordance with the principles of sovereign rights. A terrorist not only kills innocent people but damages the psyche of a nation,” she said, adding that the report’s fervent advocacy for the rights of terrorists, who violate the most sacred right of humans — the right to life — does not similarly extend to the victims of terrorism.

“The report goes back half a decade to find references to my country. It fails when it comes to grave violations committed recently in our region and in the developed world,” she said.

Ms. Mangalanandan said that as per the report, all discrimination and wrong practices during COVID-19 supposedly took place only in the Global South.

“What benefit does the report derive by not mentioning similar tragic situations in the developed world? Deriving political mileage out of people's pain and loss should not be a topic that SRs (Special Rapporteurs) should base their relevance on,” she said.

World.title: Mortal remains of two Keralam residents killed in Germany apartment fire brought home
World.content:
The mortal remains of two youths from Keralam who were killed in a fire at an apartment building in Bochum, Germany, were brought to Kochi early on Friday (October 23, 2026). The bodies of Sivin Johny, 26, and Anjali Sheela Joy, 27, of Chemmakkad, Periyanad, in Kollam district, were brought to Cochin International Airport around 1.30 a.m., while the body of the third victim, Nova Sabu, 25, of Kattappana in Idukki district, is expected to arrive at 8.15 p.m. on Friday, officials said.

Relatives of the deceased, public representatives, including Kalady grama panchayat president Pouly Baby, and NoRKA officials received the bodies.

Sivin’s body was taken to his residence at Manickamangalam near Kalady after medical formalities were completed at a hospital in Aluva. The funeral is scheduled to be held at St. Rocky’s Syro-Malabar Church, Manickamangalam, in the afternoon. Anjali’s mortal remains were taken to her home in Kollam.

Sivin had reached Germany only about two weeks earlier for higher studies, while Anjali had been in Germany since July. She was working at a warehouse there. Nova, who had worked as a fitness trainer in Keralam before moving to Germany in July, was reportedly about to start a new job when the tragedy claimed her life. Nova had earlier worked with Anjali and had gone to visit her for the weekend when the accident happened.

The three were killed in a fire that broke out early on October 13, 2026, in a multi-family residential building in Bochum’s Hofstede district. Firefighters found the three victims dead in an apartment on the second floor. Five other people who were injured were taken to hospitals in Bochum.

Investigations are under way into the arson attack on the apartment building. Preliminary findings indicate that the tragedy stemmed from personal enmity between the flat owner and a Romanian national who is currently in police custody.

World.title: Economist Parakala Prabhakar to participate in protest against SIR in Hyderabad on October 24
World.content:
Economist Parakala Prabhakar will be participating in a human chain protest at Tank Bund in Hyderabad on October 24 against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that the exercise undermines democracy and could lead to the exclusion of eligible voters.

In a video message posted on social media platforms, Mr. Prabhakar said people across the country were questioning the Election Commission of India (ECI) and expressing their disapproval of what he described as the ‘shenanigans’ of the poll panel and the ‘sham called SIR’. He also alleged that electoral mandates were being stolen.

“People from every region, every age group and every walk of life are raising their voices,” he said, arguing that Jantar Mantar, the site of several protests in New Delhi, represented not just a physical location but every street and lane where people expressed dissent. “Every protesting, questioning and dissenting mind is Jantar Mantar,” he said, adding that the authorities could not suppress dissent everywhere.

Calling on people to participate in the Hyderabad protest, Mr. Prabhakar said the human chain would begin at 4 p.m. on October 24 near the Makhdoom Mohiuddin statue at Tank Bund.

He urged participants to demand the scrapping of SIR, the restoration of all eligible voters to electoral rolls, the revocation of the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, and greater accountability and impartiality on the part of the ECI. “Let us unite to restore democracy,” he said, asking participants to bring the national flag and placards to the protest.

World.title: Chennai Northeast monsoon rains: T.N. CM Vijay directs officials to maintain continuous vigil
World.content:
With the onset of the Northeast monsoon, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has instructed officials to maintain a “continuous vigil” across all constituencies throughout the season, according to sources.

He made this remark while reviewing monsoon preparedness, waterlogging at 35 locations including Velachery, Manadi, and the Madras High Court area, and the Greater Chennai Corporation’s (GCC) response to the heavy rain that has been lashing the city, at the Integrated Command and Control Centre at Ripon Buildings earlier this week.

He asked officials to respond promptly to complaints, and applauded civic and other departmental personnel for their work following the downpour.

Fund allocation

According to data presented by officials to Ministers last week,, of the ₹100 crore special fund for the monsoon, ₹44.46 crore was allocated for drainage and roads, including ₹22.46 crore for desilting 1,671 km of stormwater drains and ₹22 crore for patchwork and road restoration.

Another ₹26.68 crore was earmarked for pumps and maintenance, including hiring 150 high-capacity pumps and 500 tractor-mounted pumps. Another ₹15 lakh was allocated for repairing electric motors at ₹1 lakh per zone. Additionally, ₹4.65 crore was allocated for pump and sump maintenance, along with five temporary personnel per division for emergency monsoon works. Another ₹10 crore was allocated as an emergency response fund, at ₹5 lakh per division.

Stormwater drain construction under the Asian Development Bank (ADB) fund is complete in the Tiruvottiyur (93.68 km), Manali (126.296 km), Madhavaram (165 km) and Anna Nagar (13.87 km) zones, and under the Capital Fund in the Royapuram, Thiru. Vi. Ka. Nagar, Ambattur, Teynampet, Alandur, and Perungudi zones.

Balance work is due on October 25 in Tondiarpet (Capital Fund). It is due on October 31 in Ambattur (ADB fund), Anna Nagar, Kodambakkam, Valasaravakkam, and Adyar (Capital Fund), Kodambakkam and Valasaravakkam (CMRL fund), and Alandur (KfW fund). Under the KfW fund, 145.27 km of 154.19 km is done in Perungudi and 101 km of 125 km in Sholinganallur, with the balance due by March 31, 2027, according to the presentation.

Of 2.440 km under the ADB fund, 2.060 km is done and the balance is to be completed by October 31. Anna Nagar Zone All 13.87 km under the ADB fund have been completed. Adyar Zone Of 34.98 km under the Capital Fund, 33 km is done and the balance is to be completed by October 31. Perungudi Zone All 2.35 km under the Capital Fund have been completed. The Highways Department has completed desilting 275 km of stormwater drains, 18,000 catchpits, 321 culverts, and six vehicular subway wells. Pumps and relief centres
